CONFIDENTIAL

June 23, 1941.

Nanking Government Leaders' Visit to Japan

The recent calling of Wang Ching Wei, Chow Fu
Hai (周佛海), Lin Pai Sheng (林柏生) and
other leaders of the Nanking Government to Japan
has given rise to rumours to the effect that the
visit is of great significance; that the Japanese
authorities intend to give these visitors instructions
concerning the international situation and that
discussions will be held in connection with the
situation in China. These are, however, merely
conjectures.

According to information secured from reliable
sources in Nanking, the present visit of Wang Ching
Wei etc. to Japan should not be regarded as of a
very important nature. It is simply a plan of the
Japanese authorities to arouse in the Chinese leaders
an aspiration to further improve their pro-Japanese
spirit. As Wang Kuh Min (王克敏) of the former
Provisional Government in Peiping and Liang Hung Tee
(梁鴻志) of the now defunct Reformed Government
in Nanking have visited Japan before, it seems
necessary for the leaders of the Nanking Government
to pay a similar visit. It is expected by the
Japanese that the favourable treatment which will be
accorded the Nanking officials during their visit
to Japan will arouse in the latter a grateful feeling
and a desire to repay them. It is further expected
that as a result of their visit to the various parts
of Japan, the Nanking Government leaders will be

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / SPECIAL BRANCH / Jun 3 . 1941）
FILE
pages.zh:
机密

1941年6月23日。

南京政府领导人访日

近期汪精卫、周佛海、林柏生及其他南京政府领导人的被召赴日，引发了种种谣言，称此次访问意义重大；日本当局意图就国际局势向这些访客下达指示，并将就中国局势进行讨论。然而，这些仅仅是猜测。

根据从南京可靠来源获得的情报，汪精卫等人此次访日不应被视为具有极其重要的性质。这仅仅是日本当局的一项计划，旨在激发中国领导人进一步改善其亲日精神。鉴于前北平临时政府的王克敏和现已解散的南京维新政府的梁鸿志此前曾访问过日本，南京政府的领导人似乎也有必要进行类似的访问。日本方面期望，南京官员在访日期间所受到的优待将在他们心中激起感激之情和报答之意。此外还期望，通过访问日本各地，南京政府领导人将

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 特务科 / 1941年6月3日）

given an impression that China is not in a position
to compete with Japan, thereby becoming afraid of
and respectful towards her.

With regard to the policies of the Nanking
Government, the Asia Development Board is the sole
organ regulating its conformity with the will of
the Japanese authorities in Tokyo. In this connection,
the Nanking Government is not in direct contact with
the Japanese Government. Hence, the Wang party has
no qualification whatsoever to hold discussions
with the Tokyo authorities regarding the plans of
the Nanking Government.

关于南京政府的政策，兴亚院是调节其是否符合东京日本当局意志的唯一机构。在这方面，南京政府并不与日本政府直接接触。因此，汪派完全没有资格就南京政府的计划与东京当局进行讨论。

02825

Wang And His Party
Reach Nanking

Tendered a rousing reception
as he and his party stepped
from their plane at the Nan-
king aerodrome yesterday, Mr.
Wang Ching-wei immediately
proceeded to the official re-
sidence which he will make his
headquarters during the forth-
coming Central Political Con-
ference.

Mr. Wang, future head of the
new Central Government of
China, was accompanied by a
number of other delegates from
Shanghai who will confer with
representatives from Peking,
the Mongolian Government,
Nanking and Canton in the
near future. The official date
for the opening of the confer-
ence has not been announced.
pages.zh:
02825

汪及其随行人员
抵达南京

昨日，汪精卫先生及其随行人员在南京机场走下飞机时受到热烈欢迎，他随即前往官方寓所，该处将成为他在即将召开的中央政治会议期间的总部。

汪先生，这位未来中国新中央政府的元首，由多位来自上海的其他代表陪同，他们将在不久的将来与来自北平、蒙古政府、南京和广州的代表举行会谈。会议开幕的正式日期尚未公布。

pages.en:
10+6

Wang Leaves
For Nanking

Trip Made By Yangtze
With Five Gunboats
In Escort

Taken as an indication
that formation of a new
Central Government is
drawing nearer, Mr. Wang
Ching-wei, deposed Kuo-
mintang leader of the Chung-
king regime and currently
head of a new Kuomintang
party, is reported to have left
Shanghai some time yesterday for
Nanking to attend a final meeting
of the recently-formed Central
Political Council.

Mr. Wang's departure to Nan-
king was carried out by ship and
he was accompanied by five gun-
boats of the Reformed Govern-
ment. Danger of making the
journey by rail, owing to frequent
attacks by Chinese guerillas, are
believed to have prompted the
river voyage.

New Regime

A reliable Chinese source reveal-
ed this morning that during
previous conferences held between
Mr. Wang Ching-wei and various
leaders of his regime, a new Cen-
tral Political Council was formed
to nominate delegate to the latest
conference in Nanking which is
slated to take place within the
next few days.

The new Central Political Coun-
cil will continue to function after
the conference, the Chinese source
indicated, and will be charged with
the task of appointing various
ministers for the cabinet of the
new regime.

Buildings Repaired

"Three more weeks," Japanese
reports state, remain in which to
restore buildings to house the gov-
ernment. 400 workmen are engaged
in repairing structures which were
formerly used by the Examination
Yuan and the Manufacturers'
Bank of China and more than 20
other buildings are in readiness
for the new administration."

Dr. Tsu Ming-yi, former Sec-
retary-General of the Chinese
National Government and at pre-
sent secretary to Mr. Wang Ching-
wei, is reported to have been
assaulted by Japanese soldiers
when he arrived in Nanking re-
cently with the Chinese National
flag and the Kuomintang party
banner.

Flags Destroyed

The soldiers tore both flags to
ribbons, declaring that they had
no orders to permit entry of the
flags into the former capital. Dr.
Tsu's belongings were also search-
ed by the soldiers.

Following his return to Shang-
hai, Dr. Tsu reported the incident
to Mr. Wang Ching-wei, this re-
sulting in a decision to add a yel-
low pennant to both flags in order
to indicate the difference from the
old regime.
pages.zh:
10+6

汪启程
前往南京

乘船沿长江而行
五艘炮艇护航

被视为新中央政府组建日益临近的迹象，被重庆政权罢黜的国民党领袖、现任新国民党党魁汪精卫先生，据报已于昨日某时离开上海前往南京，参加最近成立的中央政治委员会的最后一次会议。

汪先生前往南京是乘船进行的，陪同他的是维新政府的五艘炮艇。由于中国游击队频繁袭击，铁路旅行存在危险，据信这是促使他选择水路旅行的原因。

新政权

一位可靠的中方消息人士今晨透露，在汪精卫先生与其政权各位领导人之前的会议期间，成立了一个新的中央政治委员会，以提名代表参加定于未来几天内在南京举行的最新会议。

该中方消息人士表示，新的中央政治委员会将在会议结束后继续运作，并将负责为新政权的内阁任命各部部长。

修缮建筑

日本方面的报道指出，还有“三周时间”用于修复容纳政府的建筑物。400名工人正在修缮以前由考试院和中国制造银行使用的建筑，另有20多座建筑已准备就绪，供新行政机构使用。”

据报，前中国国民政府秘书长、现任汪精卫先生秘书的褚民谊博士，最近携带中华民国国旗和国民党党旗抵达南京时，遭到日本士兵的袭击。

旗帜被毁

士兵们将两面旗帜撕成碎片，声称他们没有接到允许旗帜进入前首都的命令。褚博士的物品也受到了士兵的搜查。

回到上海后，褚博士将此事件报告给汪精卫先生，这导致决定在两面旗帜上增加一面黄色三角旗，以示与旧政权的区别。

Date October 31, 1939.
Subject Alleged Removal of Wang Ching Wei to French Concession.
Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

The newspaper report of the Ta Ying Yeh Pao
in its issue of October 29th, 1939, is absolutely
groundless, the house at 570 Rue Frelupt is at present
occupied by Madame Wang and her children.
Since his arrival here, Wang Ching Wei
has never visited this address.
Dr. Chu Ling Nyi and Chow Fu Hai invited
on October 27th a number of prominent merchants including
Yu Ya Ching to a dinner at 570 Rue Frelupt and while
entertaining them asked their assistance in the peace
movement. The French Police were aware of the function
and were in attendance and it was this event which created
the impression that Wang Ching Wei had removed to 570
Rue Frelupt.
No confirmation is available regarding
the attempted suicide by taking poison.

SEP 2 ~ 1939

Hwa Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao :-

RUMOURED MURDER OF WANG CHING-WEI

Just before noon yesterday it was rumoured
among various local circles that Wang Ching-wei had been
murdered in Nanking, while some said that Wang had been
assassinated at his residence on Yu Yuen Road. Actually
it was not definite as to where Wang Ching-wei had been
killed.
However, at the time of going to press, our
representative had ascertained that the above rumour was
untrue. It appears that the rumour was fabricated by
some irresponsible persons with the object of effecting
the gold exchange, for following the false report, the
price of gold soared to $4,105 per bar.
pages.zh:
1939年9月2日

《华报》、《新闻报》、《申报》：-

汪精卫被谋杀之传闻

昨日中午前不久，本地各界流传汪精卫在南京被谋杀的消息，也有人说汪在其愚园路寓所被暗杀。实际上，汪精卫究竟在何处遇害并不明确。
然而，在付印之时，本报记者已查明上述谣言不实。看来，该谣言是由一些不负责任的人捏造的，目的是影响黄金交易，因为在虚假消息传出后，金价飙升至每根金条4,105美元。

pages.en:
September 24, 1939.

MAINICHI

MEMBERS OF "DARE TO DIE" CORPS TO ATTEMPT ASSASSINATION
OF WANG CHING WEI

It is reported that five members
of a "Dare to Die Corps", under the command of Tseu Ta 秋大周
Chow, an important member of the Communist People's Food
Committee, are now actively engaged in the assassination
of important Chinese in an attempt to overthrow the New
China movement.

A few days ago they are said to
have smuggled themselves and a large sum of money into
the Foreign Settlements by a foreign ship arriving from
an outport, their intention being to assassinate Wang
Ching Wei. Further it is reported that they are trying
to poison Wang Ching Wei with food by securing co-operation
from hotels and restaurants which supply foodstuffs to
him. They are also proposing to set fire to the
buildings near Wang Ching Wei's residence.

1939年9月24日。

《每日新闻》（MAINICHI）

“敢死队”成员企图暗杀汪精卫

据报道，在共产党人民粮食委员会重要成员周大秋（Tseu Ta Chow，音译）指挥下的五名“敢死队”成员，正积极从事暗杀重要中国人的活动，试图推翻“新中国运动”。

据说几天前，他们乘坐一艘从外埠抵达的外国轮船，将自己和一大笔钱偷运进外国租界，其意图是暗杀汪精卫。此外，据报道，他们正试图通过争取向汪精卫供应食品的旅馆和餐馆的合作，用食物对汪精卫下毒。他们还提议在汪精卫寓所附近的建筑物纵火。

27. 8. 9(1944) WARRANT FOR THE ARREST OF CHOW VAI-HAI AND CHEN PEI-CHUIN
ISSUED BY THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT

Chungking, August 26.

The National Government issued the following
order on August 26: "As Chow Vai-hai (周佛海) and Chen Pih-
chuin (陳璧君), wife of Wang Ching-wei, are allying with the
puppets and have surrendered to the enemy, a violation of
the Regulations Governing the Punishment of Traitors,
military and political organs throughout the country are
hereby ordered to effect their arrest in order to severely
deal with them according to law and thus uphold the
disciplinary measure taken by the government."

S.2, Special Branch.
August 29, 1939.

RETURN OF WANG CHING WEI TO SHANGHAI.

It is reported that Wang Ching Wei returned
to Shanghai on August 28 and presided over a preparatory
meeting of the "People's Conference" held at 76, Jess-
field Road yesterday afternoon. At this meeting, it
was decided to elect a number of pro-Japanese elements
to serve on the Executive and Supervisory Committees
of the Central Kuomintang in order that measures be
taken to organize the Central Political Council. These
having been completed a Central Government will be formed.
There was a large attendance mostly ex-Kuomintang members,
each being invited ostensibly to celebrate a birthday
party. They were carefully scrutinized at the entrance,
each to produce the invitation card for identity.

(左侧边栏批注)
Vice Special Branch report dated 7/7/39.
Vice Special Branch report dated 2/8/39 (Copy)
Vice Special Branch report dated 1/8/39.

B.m.
Cis
FILE

(正文)
With reference to attached report from Bubbling Well Station regarding House 61, Lane 1136, Yu Yuen Road, this house is the proposed fortified local residence of Wang Ching Wei, the ex-Deputy Executive of the Kuomintang, while Houses Nos. 60 and 64 in the same alleyway are occupied by the Japanese Gendarmerie who established therein a "Brennan Road Sub-station" on July 29, 1939.

Wang Ching Wei has never been in occupation of House 61, Lane 1136, Yu Yuen Road, and there is no likelihood that he will do so in the near future. The house is at present, however, being guarded by a number of armed men.

The Hollywood Garden, 1204 Yu Yuen Road, and the Li Kai Lo Amusement Society, a gambling den behind the garden, which are situated to the immediate west of House 61, 1136, Yu Yuen Road, and which were instructed to remove before the end of July, 1939 have now been permitted to carry on their business at the present addresses after they had each agreed to allow eight armed guards appointed by the Wang Ching Wei Clique to be stationed on their premises and to provide these guards with food, lodgings and a monthly salary of about $50.00 each per mensem.

Lao Chung Chi
D. S. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

(正文)
关于附带的静安寺捕房有关愚园路1136弄61号房屋的报告，该房屋是前国民党副总裁汪精卫拟建的 fortified（设防）本地寓所，而同一条弄堂内的60号和64号房屋则由日本宪兵队占据，他们于1939年7月29日在此设立了“布伦南路分遣队”。

汪精卫从未入住过愚园路1136弄61号，且在近期也不太可能入住。然而，目前该房屋正由多名武装人员守卫。

位于愚园路1136弄61号紧邻西侧的好莱坞花园（愚园路1204号）以及花园后面的赌场李开乐游艺社，原被指令在1939年7月底前搬离，现已被允许在原址继续经营，条件是双方均同意允许八名由汪精卫派系指派的武装警卫驻守其场所，并为这些警卫提供食宿及每人每月约50美元的薪水。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No..........

S.2, Special Branch....Station
REPORT    xxxx
Date....August 14, 19 39.

Subject....City Government Officials nervous over peace talks.
Waung Ching Wei to return to Shanghai shortly.

Made by.................... Forwarded by....................
（印：SECRET）

There is much talk amongst pro-Japanese
elements that through the efforts of Waung Ching Wei,
Japan will before long cease hostilities and conclude
a peace agreement with Chiang Kai Shek's regime.
What will be the terms for the peace no Reformed Govern-
ment official seems to know, but in view of the growing
atmosphere and the possibility of losing their posts
and facing other troubles, a number of the City Govern-
ment officials have become nervous. Li Ting Sz (李鼎士),
the Commissioner of Public Utilities Bureau, has tendered
his resignation, but his application has been refused by
the Japanese. Li is a native of Ningpo. He entered
the City Government in March 1939. Prior to that time,
he was proprietor of the Wei Ming Powder Milk Coy, 451
Kiangse Road, and served on the Committee of the Japanese
sponsored Citizens' Association.

It is also reported that Waung Ching Wei
will depart from Canton for Shanghai on August 15 to
renew his efforts for peace. Whilst at Canton, he is
alleged to have attained much success in the establish-
ment of a local government and arrived at some under-
standing with the Commanders of the Forces in Kwangtung
who are on the side of Chungking.

Certified true copy.
Harlow

Date August 22 1939.

Subject (in full) Return of Mr. Waung Ching Wei to Shanghai.

Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

（批：A / For / Secy C. C.）

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE / 22 AUG. 1939）

（批：E / C / 22/8）

Further to reports dated July 31 and August 2,
information which has been confirmed, has been received
that Mr. Waung Ching Wei arrived in Shanghai on
August 19 and is staying somewhere in Kiangwan.
Although preparations have been made for him to
reside at the former residence of Wong Peh Chun
(ex-Minister of Communications), House 31, Lane 1136,
Yu Yuen Road, Mr. Waung is hesitating to go there
in view of the recent clash between S.M.P. and
Ta Tao Police.

Tan Shaoliang
Superintendent.

A. C. (Special Branch)

August 10, 30.

Activities of Wang Ching Wei

With reference to the article appearing in
the Ta Mei Wan Pao of July 25, 1939 relating to the
establishment of a "China Peace and National
Salvation Association" in Shanghai and the conditions
arrived at between Wang Ching Wei and the Japanese
authorities, enquiries tend to show that these
conditions are the basis of the original proposals
reached between the ex-Deputy Executive of the
Kuomintang and the Tokyo politicians.

Considering him as the new leader of China,
the Tokyo politicians coerced Wang Ching Wei into
organising a Federal Government, and concluded with
him a series of conditions which were to mark the
prelude towards the creation of a new regime in China.

The plans drafted by the Tokyo politicians
and Wang Ching Wei, however, met with the disapproval
of the Japanese militarists in North and Central
China, who strongly opposed the arrangements arrived
at especially the organisation of a new government
with the name of Kuomintang and the "Blue Sky White
Sun" flag as the Chinese national emblem. It was
due to this fact that the Tsingtao Conference did
not arrive at any concrete decisions and as a
result, Wang Ching Wei suffered a serious setback
to his activities, and consequently abandoned the
plans he had for Shanghai.

The Tokyo politicians are reported to be
also greatly disappointed at the outcome, but are

1930年8月10日。

汪精卫的活动

关于1939年7月25日《大美晚报》上刊登的关于在上海成立“中国和平救国联合会”以及汪精卫与日本当局之间达成条件的文章，调查显示，这些条件是基于前国民党副总裁与东京政客之间达成的原始提案基础。

东京政客将汪精卫视为中国的新领导人，胁迫他组织联邦政府，并与他签订了一系列条件，作为在中国建立新政权的序幕。

然而，东京政客与汪精卫起草的计划遭到了华北和华中的日本军国主义者的反对，他们强烈反对所达成的安排，特别是反对以国民党名义组织新政府并使用“青天白日”旗作为中国国徽。正是由于这一事实，青岛会议未能做出任何具体决定，结果，汪精卫的活动遭受了严重挫折，因此放弃了他为上海制定的计划。

据报道，东京政客也对结果感到极大失望，但是

pages.en:
Ta Mei Wan Pao of July 25 :-

WANG CHING-WEI FORMS THE CHINA PEACE AND NATIONAL
SALVATION ASSOCIATION

According to reliable information from
foreign circles, the Japanese Government has allotted
Yen 1,500,000 to Wang Ching-wei to enable him to secure
the support of local residents for his policy of
co-operation with Japan. When Wang Ching-wei accepted
this subsidy from the Japanese, he promised to start
immediate activities in Shanghai and it is believed
that before October his work will be crowned with success.
In addition, he has established a "China Peace and
National Salvation Association" with headquarters at
the residence of Wang Pah-chung (王伯群) on Yu Yuen
Road.

It is said that the following three points
have been settled between Wang Ching-wei and the Japanese
authorities:-
(1) To secure the support of veteran
Kuomintang members in Shanghai.
(2) To secure the co-operation of local
bankers who have large undertakings in Shanghai.
(3) To endeavour to secure the assistance
of overseas Chinese and to make use of their contributions
in furthering the peace movement.

The new organization will have a Central
Publication Department to handle the publication of
newspapers in the English and Chinese languages. In
case of necessity, papers in other foreign languages
will be published.

The new organization will undertake the
following measures to attain its objects:-
(1) To endeavour to bribe persons to
enter its service.
(2) To adopt strong measures against those
who are unwilling to work for the Association.

If local bankers refuse to co-operate
with Wang Ching-wei, either strong pressure will be
brought to bear upon them or else measures will be
adopted to make their stay in Shanghai impossible. These
means will also be applied against those veteran
Kuomintang members in Shanghai who are unwilling to
co-operate with the Association.

No information is, however, available
as to whether Wang Ching-wei will personally take charge
of this Association. It is possible that Ling Fah-sen
(林柏生), a close follower of Wang Ching-wei, will be
in charge.

C

pages.zh:
7月25日《大美晚报》：

汪精卫组建中国和平救国协会

据外国圈子可靠消息，日本政府已拨给
汪精卫150万日元，使他能够为其
与日本合作的政策争取当地居民的支持。当汪精卫接受
这笔来自日本的津贴时，他承诺立即在上海开展
活动，据信在十月之前他的工作将取得成功。
此外，他还成立了“中国和平
救国协会”，总部设在
愚园路王伯群（Wang Pah-chung）的寓所。

据说汪精卫与日本
当局之间已就以下三点达成一致：
(1) 争取上海资深
国民党党员的支持。
(2) 争取在上海拥有大型企业的当地
银行家的合作。
(3) 努力争取海外华侨的援助，并利用他们的捐款
来推进和平运动。

新组织将设立中央出版部，负责处理
中英文报纸的出版事宜。如有
必要，还将出版其他外文的报纸。

新组织将采取以下措施以实现其目标：
(1) 努力贿赂人员为其服务。
(2) 对不愿为该协会工作的人采取强硬措施。

如果当地银行家拒绝与汪精卫合作，要么对他们施加
巨大压力，要么采取措施使他们在上海无法立足。这些
手段也将适用于上海那些不愿与协会合作的资深
国民党党员。

然而，目前没有关于汪精卫是否会亲自掌管
该协会的消息。有可能由汪精卫的亲信林柏生
（Ling Fah-sen）负责。

C
(

pages.en:
July 13, 1939.
Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Wan Pao published the following Tientsin telegram
on July 12 :-

TSINGTAO CONFERENCE OPENS

According to information received from Tsingtao,
representatives of the "Reformed Government" in Nanking
and the "Provisional Government" in Peiping yesterday
commenced the so-called 5th Joint Conference at Tsingtao.
According to foreign residents at Tsingtao,
the conference apparently has some connection with the
formation of a new "Central Government" but the puppet
authorities have definitely denied this report.
It is learned that after the conference,
measures governing the control of economics in North
China and a limit to foreign exchange will be put into
force in Central China. If this is done, the business
of third Power nationals in Shanghai will inevitably be
affected.

**〔此处转录不清〕**

1939年7月13日。
晨间译文。

《大美晚报》于7月12日刊登了以下天津电报：

青岛会议召开

据从青岛收到的消息，南京“维新政府”和北平“临时政府”的代表昨天在青岛开始了所谓的第五次联席会议。据青岛的外国居民称，这次会议显然与组建新的“中央政府”有关，但傀儡当局明确否认了这一报道。
据悉，会议结束后，将实施管制华北经济的措施，并在华中地区限制外汇。如果这样做，在上海的第三国国民的商业活动将不可避免地受到影响。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. ............
S.2 Special Branch ............
REPORT
Date August 2 1939.

Subject. Alleged object of Waung Chin Wei's mission to Canton.

Made by. ............ and Forwarded by. Supt. Tan Shao Liang

〔左侧批注及印章区域〕
（批：SMP 3/8）
（批：CONFIDENTIAL）
（批：To See - C G）
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 2 - AUG. 1933）
（签名：Jno Robertson）
（批：E. / - / W.S.C.G. / - / 26<sup>?</sup> / 2/8）

Further enquiries have been made amongst pro-Japanese circles as to the reasons why Mr. Waung Ching Wei has left for Canton. It is now ascertained that realizing the lack of support from the Provisional Government of Peiping and the Reformed Government of Nanking, Waung has decided to proceed to the South and endeavour to collect his followers and colleagues formerly connected with the South Western Political Council with the object of establishing a Government at Canton and building up his influence in the South.

Followers of Mr. Waung Ching Wei in Shanghai believe that the political leader has received the support of influential Japanese and is likely to succeed. This does not mean, however, that Waung will take up the leadership of the Canton Government. He will leave this position for one of his followers and will wait for a chance to enter the Federal Government which when inaugurated he hopes will exercise control over all Governments.

D. C. (Special Branch)

（签名：Tan Shao Liang）
Superintendent.

（签名：Jno Robertson）
（批：E. / - / W.S.C.G. / - / 26<sup>?</sup> / 2/8）

已在亲日圈子中进一步调查汪精卫先生前往广州的原因。现已查明，汪意识到缺乏北平临时政府和南京维新政府的支持，决定南下，努力召集以前与西南政务委员会有关的追随者和同事，目的是在广州建立政府，并在南方建立其影响力。

汪精卫先生在上海的追随者认为，这位政治领袖已获得有影响力的日本人的支持，可能会成功。然而，这并不意味着汪将担任广州政府的领导职务。他将把这一职位留给其一名追随者，并等待机会进入联邦政府，他希望该政府成立后能控制所有政府。

副总监（特务科）

（签名：谭绍良）
警督。

广州的原因。现已查明，汪意识到缺乏北平临时政府和南京维新政府的支持，决定南下，努力召集以前与东南政务委员会（South Eastern Political Council）有关的追随者和同事，目的是在广州建立政府，并在南方建立其影响力。

汪精卫先生在上海的追随者认为，这位政治领袖已获得有影响力的日本人的支持，可能会成功。然而，这并不意味着汪将担任广州政府的领导职务。他将把这一职位留给其一名追随者，并等待机会进入联邦政府，他希望该政府成立后能控制所有政府。

According to information, Wang Ching-wei or part
of his family is now residing in the French Concession.
About 100 arms licences, it is stated, have been issued
by the French Police to Wang's adherents for his
protection.

He is experiencing much difficulty in carrying
out his pacification plan owing to the obstructive
attitude of certain Japanese Commanders in North China
and the Peiping Provisional Government under Wang Keh-
min (王克敏), which is strongly opposed to his demand
for the dissolution of the Provisional Governments,
although Liang Hung-tse (梁鸿志) of the "Reformed
Government" at Nanking is reported to be willing to
dissolve his government on the inauguration of the new
Chinese Central Government under Wang Ching-wei.

The Japanese military authorities are demanding

not in favour of this proposal.

Rumour also has it that Dr. Chu Min-nyi (褚民谊),
Director of the Institut Technique Franco-Chinois at No.
1195 Rue Lafayette, will be appointed Mayor of Shanghai
if and when Wang's new Government is inaugurated at
Nanking.

who is alleged to control little money other than that

由于华北某些日军指挥官以及王克敏（Wang Keh-min）领导下的北平临时政府采取阻挠态度，汪在实施其绥靖计划时面临诸多困难。该临时政府强烈反对汪提出的解散各临时政府的要求，尽管据报道，南京“维新政府”的梁鸿志（Liang Hung-tse）愿意在汪精卫领导的新中国中央政府成立时解散其政府。

日本军方要求，如果保留青天白日旗，则必须在青天之上放置一个黄色三角形，据称这是反共产国际的象征。据称，汪的许多追随者并不赞成这一提议。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
1948
1930

Chinese People Urged By
Wang Ching-wei To Help
Him To Bring Back Peace

Chiang Kai-shek Is Accused Of Leading Country To
Destruction At Bidding Of The Communists;
Long Address Broadcast In Mandarin

GOOD NEIGHBOURLINESS, ECONOMIC
TEAM WORK, FIGHT ON REDS

Accusing General Chiang Kai-shek of leading China to destruction at the bidding of the Communists, Mr. Wang Ching-wei, ousted Deputy Executive of the Kuomintang, last night called upon the Chinese people to support him in his efforts to secure Sino-Japanese peace.

In a broadcast address, made in Mandarin at 9.10 o'clock, and in Cantonese an hour later, the veteran Chinese statesman gave a detailed expose of his views regarding Japanese proposals for peace embodying the three principles of good neighbourliness, anti-Communism, and economic co-operation.

Mr. Wang said: "The late Dr. Sun Yat-sen told us that the success of the Chinese revolution would depend upon Japan's understanding. This sentence has great significance. Japan is an oriental Power, whose economic system, military science and culture are well in advance of ours. It may even be said that in the last several decades, Eastern Asia existed because Japan was there.

"China, although backward, is a nation with a long history, a vast territory and a huge population. Japan could not escape the influence that a powerful China would exert. Naturally, it is essential for Japan to know whether or not a powerful China would be to her advantage. If to her advantage, Japan would be anxious to see a powerful and prosperous China, which she could call her friend. If to her disadvantage, Japan would have to regard China resolutely as her enemy and seek to destroy the means whereby China would become strong and prosperous.

Who Will Be Victor?

"In a contest between a nation like China, just attempting to make herself strong and prosperous, and one like Japan, already powerful and prosperous, it is unnecessary to question who shall win. For this reason, if the Chinese wish attain the fruits of their revolution, it is necessary to make Japan understand that a successful Chinese revolution will be advantageous to Japan. This is not a plot nor a subterfuge, but a sincere statement. Now how could it be advantageous to Japan? It will be first necessary for Chinese and Japanese diplomacy to adopt the same policy, for their military to take the same stand. Further, with mutual benefit and equality as our principles, we should attempt to attain economic co-operation. In such an event, the strength and the prosperity of the Chinese nation will prove of advantage and not harmful to Japan.

《字林西报》（SHANGHAI TIMES）。
1948
1930

汪精卫呼吁中国人民
帮助他恢复和平

蒋介石被指控受共产党指使将国家引向毁灭；
长篇普通话广播讲话

睦邻友好，经济合作，剿共

被开除的国民党副总裁汪精卫先生昨晚指责蒋介石将军受共产党指使将中国引向毁灭，并呼吁中国人民支持他为争取中日和平所作的努力。

这位资深中国政治家在晚上9点10分用普通话、一小时后用广东语发表的广播讲话中，详细阐述了他对日本和平提案的看法，这些提案体现了睦邻友好、反共和经济合作三大原则。

汪先生说：“已故孙中山博士告诉我们，中国革命的成功取决于日本的理解。这句话意义重大。日本是一个东方强国，其经济体系、军事科学和文化都远远领先于我们。甚至可以说，在过去几十年里，东亚之所以存在，是因为有日本。

“中国虽然落后，但是一个历史悠久、幅员辽阔、人口众多的国家。日本无法逃避强大中国所产生的影响。自然，日本必须知道一个强大的中国是否对其有利。如果有利，日本将乐于看到一个强大繁荣的中国，并可以称之为朋友。如果不利，日本将不得不坚决视中国为敌人，并寻求摧毁使中国变得强大和繁荣的手段。

谁将是胜利者？

“在一个像中国这样刚刚试图使自己强大和繁荣的国家，与一个像日本这样已经强大和繁荣的国家之间的竞争中，无需质疑谁将获胜。因此，如果中国人希望获得革命的成果，就必须让日本明白，成功的中国革命将对日本有利。这不是阴谋或诡计，而是真诚的陈述。那么，这对日本如何有利呢？首先，中日外交必须采取相同的政策，军事必须采取相同的立场。此外，以互利和平等为原则，我们应努力实现经济合作。在这种情况下，中华民族的力量和繁荣将证明对日本有利而非有害。

"Would this not be endangering
Chinese sovereignty and integrity?
No, absolutely not. For a nation
to join with another with which
her interests do not conflict cannot
be considered as endangering her
sovereignty or integrity.

Interests Of Third Powers

"Then, would it endanger the
just rights and privileges of third
nations? Absolutely not. For a
union between Japan and China
would be aimed at preserving their
integrity and prosperity without
the idea of endangering the just
rights and interests of third
nations.

"In the 13th year of the Chinese
Republic (1924), the late Dr. Sun
in Canton personally laid down
the principles for the founding of
the Kuomintang Government. At
that time, the relations between
Japan and China were being gov-
erned in the manner described
above. During the 14th year of
the Republic, Dr. Sun died. I took
up his ideas and assumed the con-
duct of the Kuomintang Govern-
ment. I dared not change the
above principles and observed them
with care. During the 17th year
of the Republic (1928), the situa-
tion became different. The Tsinan
Incident started a deterioration of
Sino-Japanese relations. But en-
mity should be dispelled instead of
aggravated. At this time, China
should have tried to endure to the
best of her ability and to have
endeavoured to restore to normal-
ity the already deteriorated part
in Sino-Japanese relations.

The Outbreak In 1931

"It is regrettable that the Kuo-
mintang Government, at that time,
did not adopt such a wise policy.
Instead, bad feeling between Japan
and China was allowed to become
aggravated, culminating in the out-
break of September 18, (1931).

"In saying so, I have not the
slightest intention to blame the
people at the helm of the Kuo-
mintang Government at that time.
I am a member of the Kuomintang
and a man who has had relations
with the Kuomintang Government.
Therefore, for such a mistake, I
should share responsibility with
the others. But, at the same time,
my readers should recall that at
the time I was a "criminal"
against whom an arrest warrant
had been issued by the Kuomintang
Government. I was travelling
abroad then, and it was not until
January 28 of the 21st year of the
Republic (1932) that I returned to
Nanking to assume the presidency
of the Executive Yuan. Later I
acted concurrently as Foreign Min-
ister. At the time, I propounded
the idea that we should resist, on
the one hand, and negotiate, on
the other. My purpose was to
placate the opinion of those who
opposed direct negotiation.

Shanghai, Tangku Truce Pacts

"Under my direction, the Shang-
hai and Tangku truce agreements
were signed. At this time, I was
still doing so under the conviction
that enmity should not be promoted
but dispelled. I was endeavouring
to start with a local and tempor-
ary settlement in order to achieve
permanent peace for the entire
nation. I did not achieve my objec-
tive in four years. For this I
blame not others, but my insufficient
ability and influence.
pages.zh:
1049

“这难道不会危及
中国的主权和完整吗？
不，绝对不会。一个国家
与另一个与其利益不冲突的国家
联合，不能被视为危及其
主权或完整。

第三国的利益

“那么，这会危及
第三国的正当权利和特权吗？
绝对不会。因为日中
联合旨在维护其
完整和繁荣，而不带有
危及第三国正当
权利和利益的意图。

“在中华民国十三年
（1924年），已故孙博士
在广州亲自制定了
组建国民党政府的原则。当时，
日中关系正按照
上述方式治理。在民国
十四年，孙博士去世。我继承
了他的思想，并承担
了国民党政府的
管理工作。我不敢改变上述
原则，并谨慎遵守。在民国
十七年（1928年），局势
发生了变化。济南事件导致
中日关系恶化。但仇恨
应当消除而不是加剧。此时，
中国本应尽力忍耐，并
努力使中日关系中
已经恶化的部分恢复正常。

1931年的爆发

“遗憾的是，当时的国
民党政府没有采取如此明智的政策。
相反，日中之间的不良情绪
被允许加剧，最终导致了
九月十八日（1931年）事变的爆发。

“这样说，我丝毫无意
责备当时掌管国民党
政府的人。我是国民党
的一员，也是一个与国民党
政府有过关系的人。
因此，对于这样的错误，我
应与其他人共同承担责任。但
同时，我的读者应该回想，当时
我是一个‘罪犯’，国民党
政府已对我发出逮捕令。
我当时正在国外旅行，直到
民国二十一年（1932年）1月
28日才回到南京就任行政
院院长。后来我兼任外交部
长。当时，我提出了一面抵抗、
一面谈判的主张。我的目的是
安抚那些反对直接谈判的人
的意见。

上海、塘沽停战协定

“在我的指导下，签署了
上海和塘沽停战协定。当时，
我这样做仍然是基于仇恨
不应助长而应消除的信念。我
正努力从局部和暂时的
解决开始，以实现整个
国家的永久和平。我在四年内
未能实现我的目标。对此我
不怪别人，只怪自己能力
和影响力不足。

pages.en:
"I am firmly opposed to the
opinion of those who advocated war
at that time. What would be the
result, in the long run, I would ask
myself, of a war between a coun-
try like ours, just seeking strength
and prosperity, and one like Japan,
already strong and wealthy. It
would be tantamount to playing with
the nation and the people.
"At the outset I believed that
General Chiang Kai-shek maintained
the same ideas as I did. I gained
this belief from his public state-
ment following his resignation from
the chairmanship of the Kuomin-
tang Government in December of
the 20th year of the Republic
(1931).
"For this reason I co-operated
with him heartily and sincerely.
But after four years of effort, I
gradually felt and noticed that I
had been mistaken. On November
1 of the 24th year of the Republic
(1935) I received three wounds,
after being seriously ill, and my
health did not permit me to re-
main in office any longer. I was
abroad throughout the 25th year of
the Republic (1935) and returned
after the Sian Affair had occurred.
The situation was definitely worse.
"At that time I was fully con-
vinced that the suppression of the
Communists should not, and could
not, be suspended, for the Com-
munists thought only of the Third
Internationale and not of China.
Acting on secret orders of the Third
Internationale they discarded their
slogan of class struggle and instead
hoisted a banner of anti-Japanism,
utilizing the sentiment prevailing
among the Chinese people for the
last several years to stir up a Sino-
Japanese war. This kind of suffer-
ing should never have occurred had
we not been fooled into doing so.
Peace Proposals
"At that time, I spent much time
drawing attention to this point.
Since the outbreak of the Loukou-
chiao Affair, I have had no means
to stop the Sino-Japanese conflict,
but I have been constantly thinking
to bring about a turning point in
the trend of events. Not for a single
minute did I halt studying means
to stop the dangerous ideas and
plans of the Communists and to
let the public know about them
until the very last moment of my
departure from Chungking on De-
cember 18. On December 29, I made
my statement on peace proposals.
"My proposals for peace are in
agreement with the statement made
by Prince Konoye of Japan. This
is because I am still convinced that
the enmity towards Japan should
be dispelled rather than aggravat-
ed. After fighting for 1½ years, the
power of Japan and the will of
the Chinese people have been well
demonstrated. Since Japan has al-
ready stated that she has no terri-
torial designs upon China and has
even extended her hand in quest
of co-operation with joint objec-
tives in view, why cannot China also
extend her hand to bring this dis-
pute to an end like a quarrel be-
tween brothers, who embraced them-
selves, crying, after a fight? How
sad is such a scene, but also how
joyful its end. If General Chiang
could understand that Sino-Japan-
ese relations have now reached a
new stage and bravely, and with
determination, say so, the road to
peace between China and Japan
will be readily opened. General
negotiations, based upon three prin-
ciples, could be then initiated to
the mutual benefit of both nations.
Permanent peace in East Asia
could then be settled at once,
with the two nations destined to
live and prosper together.

1950
pages.zh:
“我坚决反对那些当时主张战争的人的观点。我不禁自问，像我们这样一个正寻求富强繁荣的国家，与像日本那样已经强盛富裕的国家之间发生战争，长远来看结果会如何？这无异于拿国家和人民当儿戏。

“起初，我相信蒋介石将军持有与我相同的想法。这一信念源于他在民国二十年（1931年）十二月辞去国民政府主席职务后发表的公开声明。

“因此，我全心全意、真诚地与他合作。但经过四年的努力，我逐渐感到并察觉到自己错了。民国二十四年（1935年）十一月一日，我在大病初愈后遭受三处枪伤，健康状况已不允许我继续留任。民国二十五年（1936年）我全程在国外，直到西安事变发生后回国。局势显然更加恶化。

“当时我深信，对共产党的镇压不应、也不能停止，因为共产党只考虑第三国际，而不考虑中国。他们按照第三国际的秘密指令，放弃了阶级斗争的口号，转而举起反日主义的旗帜，利用过去几年在中国民众中普遍存在的情绪，煽动中日战争。如果我们没有被愚弄而陷入其中，这种苦难本不该发生。

和平提议

“当时，我花费大量时间提请人们注意这一点。自卢沟桥事变爆发以来，我已无法阻止中日冲突，但我一直在思考如何扭转事态发展的趋势。直到十二月十八日离开重庆前的最后一刻，我从未停止研究遏制共产党危险思想和计划的方法，并向公众揭露这些内容。十二月二十九日，我发表了关于和平提议的声明。

“我的和平提议与日本近卫公爵的声明一致。这是因为我也坚信，对日本的敌意应当消除而非加剧。经过一年半的战斗，日本的实力和中国人民的意志已得到充分展现。既然日本已声明对中国没有领土野心，甚至为了共同目标伸出手寻求合作，中国为何不能也伸出援手，像兄弟打架后相拥而泣那样结束这场争端？这样的场景虽令人悲伤，但其结局却令人欣慰。如果蒋介石将军能认识到中日关系现已进入新阶段，并勇敢且坚定地予以承认，那么中日之间的和平之路将 readily 敞开。基于三项原则的全面谈判随后可随之启动，以造福两国。东亚的永久和平便可立即确立，两国注定将共同生活与繁荣。

1950

pages.en:
51

Danger Of Drift
"It is unfortunate indeed that
General Chiang fails to follow this
course and, on the contrary, is re-
jecting the Japanese proposals. He
further cruelly oppresses those who
talk of peace in the ranks of the
party and the country at large.
Drifting already for six months, the
situation is rapidly deteriorating.
"The three principles of good
neighbourliness, a joint anti-Com-
munist front and economic co-
operation, clearly set forth in the
Konoye statement, were already
discussed several years previously.
Mr. Ariyoshi, then Ambassador to
China, calling on General Chiang
on November 11 of the 24th year
of the Republic (1935), proposed
to improve Sino-Japanese relations
with these three principles as a
basis. General Chiang agreed to
the proposals and added that he
had no counter-proposals to make.
Later, he suddenly changed his
mind. First, he claimed that he
had been talking in his capacity
as chairman of the Military
Affairs Commission and not as
President of the Executive Yuan.
Therefore, he contended, his views
were not binding upon the Gov-
ernment. Secondly, he asserted
that he had been talking in a per-
sonal and not in an official capa-
city. Thirdly, he declared, that he
had accepted the three principles
as a basis for discussion without
necessarily accepting the principles
themselves. Fourthly, he contend-
ed that he had said that he had
no counter proposals to make re-
garding the operation of the three
principles, without agreeing to them
unconditionally.
Suspension of Negotiations
"This was the reason responsible
for the suspension of the Sino-
Japanese negotiations during the
whole of the 25th year of the Re-
public (1936). And this was also
the main reason leading to the out-
break of the Sino-Japanese hostili-
ties of the 26th year of the Republic
(1937). We, after reading over the
record of diplomatic talks, have
only sighs. In the period between
December of the 26th year (1937)
and January of the 27th year of
the Republic (1938), when Dr. Traut-
mann, German Ambassador, mediat-
ed for peace, the terms presented
by him from the Japanese Govern-
ment were again based on the three
principles. In my statement entitled
"Taking An Example," I have dis-
cussed it already, so I shall not
do so again here. As to Prince
Konoye's statement, it was based
upon established Japanese princi-
ples, which were put by him into
an orderly fashion and fully ex-
plained as to points that China
entertains doubts. For instance,
regarding anti-Communism, because
China fears that it will interfere
with military and domestic affairs,
he has explained by taking the
Japanese-German-Italian anti-Com-
munist Pact as representing the
spirit in which a Sino-Japanese anti-
Communist pact could be negotiated.
pages.zh:
51

 drifting 的危险

“不幸的是，蒋介石将军并未遵循此道，反而拒绝日本的提议。他还残酷地压制党内及全国范围内谈论和平的人士。局势已 drifting 六个月，正在迅速恶化。

“近卫声明中明确提出的善邻友好、共同防共和经济合作这三项原则，早在几年前就已讨论过。民国二十四年（1935年）十一月十一日，时任驻华大使的有吉明先生拜访蒋介石将军，提议以这三项原则为基础改善中日关系。蒋介石将军同意了该提议，并表示没有反提案。后来，他突然改变了主意。首先，他声称自己是以军事委员会委员长的身份而非行政院院长的身份谈话的。因此，他认为他的观点对政府没有约束力。其次，他断言自己是以个人而非官方身份谈话的。第三，他宣称，他接受这三项原则作为讨论的基础，并不一定意味着接受原则本身。第四，他辩称，他说的是对于这三项原则的实施没有反提案，但这并不等于无条件同意它们。

谈判中止

“这就是导致民国二十五年（1936年）全年中日谈判中止的原因。这也是导致民国二十六年（1937年）中日敌对行动爆发的主要原因。我们在查阅外交会谈记录后，唯有叹息。在民国二十六年（1937年）十二月至民国二十七年（1938年）一月期间，德国大使陶德曼博士进行和平调停时，他代表日本政府提出的条件再次基于这三项原则。我在题为《举一个例子》的声明中已经讨论过此事，故此处不再赘述。至于近卫公爵的声明，它是基于既定的日本原则，他将这些原则条理化，并就中国存有疑虑的要点进行了充分解释。例如，关于反共问题，由于中国担心这会干涉其军事和内政事务，他以日德意反共协定为范例，解释了中日反共协定可以以此精神进行谈判。

pages.en:
195。

Economic Co-operation
"As to economic co-operation, because China feels that the political situation is not yet settled, he explained that Japan undertook to observe Chinese sovereignty and independence and her administrative integrity. He also said that Japan did not intend to monopolize China economically nor did she seek to limit the interests of third Powers.
"With such a careful and clear statement, the enforcement of the three principles would not be dangerous to China's independence. Moreover, it would bear fruit by removing the threat of Communism and economic aggression.
"Responsibilities in this regard are also great, Japan, in expecting China to share these responsibilities, must realize that China must be free and independent to do so. Consequently, in agreeing with Prince Konoye's statement, we are not seeking an ephemeral peace. What we are aiming at is the permanent peace of East Asia. Why should we be opposed to such a course?"
Mr. Wang took exception to alleged propaganda claims in the territory under the control of General Chiang that Japan was using her entire strength to destroy China, with the three Konoye principles as a screen.
This argument, the former Deputy Executive of the Kuomintang said, was fallacious because
1.—If Japan intended to destroy China, all she had to do was to continue fighting.
2.—The Konoye principles were not new, having been proposed several years ago.
3.—China and Japan have a mutual goal.
4.—Sino-Japanese relations deteriorated because of a vicious circle of mutual recriminations.
In conclusion, Mr. Wang said: "I feel that there are two courses open to us to-day. One is to follow General Chiang with his cry of resistance to the end. But his present forces are insufficient to resist Japan as well as opposing the Communists. Under present circumstances, even if he does not wish to follow the lead of the Communists, he will find it impossible. If we follow General Chiang along this course, we shall sacrifice the entire nation and people for the sake of the Communists.
"Another course is to revive the teachings of the late Dr. Sun and to reinforce them with the realization that enmity should be dispelled and not fostered. We should try hard to treat Japan as a friend.
"First we shall restore Sino-Japanese peace.
"Secondly, we shall establish lasting peace in East Asia.
"Of the two courses open to us, one will destroy China and the Chinese race. The other will restore the prosperity of China and of East Asia.
"I have decided to follow the second route. I shall unite with persons of all parties and affiliations, as well as those without party ties but who are anxious for the fate of China, to march forward along this route."—Domei.
pages.zh:
195。

经济合作

“关于经济合作，由于中国感到政治局势尚未稳定，他解释说，日本承诺尊重中国的主权、独立及其行政完整。他还表示，日本无意在经济上垄断中国，也不寻求限制第三国的利益。

“有了如此谨慎和清晰的声明，实施这三项原则并不会危及中国的独立。此外，通过消除共产主义威胁和经济侵略，这将结出硕果。

“这方面的责任也很重大，日本在期望中国分担这些责任时，必须认识到中国必须拥有自由和独立才能做到这一点。因此，在同意近卫公爵的声明时，我们追求的并非短暂的和平。我们的目标是东亚的永久和平。我们为什么要反对这样的道路呢？”

汪先生对蒋介石将军控制区域内所谓的宣传说法提出异议，该说法称日本正以近卫三原则为幌子，竭尽全力摧毁中国。

这位国民党前执行委员称，这种论点是错误的，因为：
1.——如果日本意图摧毁中国，她只需继续战斗即可。
2.——近卫原则并非新事物，早在几年前就已提出。
3.——中日两国拥有共同目标。
4.——中日关系恶化是因为相互指责的恶性循环。

最后，汪先生说：“我觉得今天我们有两条路可走。一条是跟随蒋介石将军，高呼抵抗到底。但他目前的兵力不足以既抵抗日本又对抗共产党。在目前的情况下，即使他不想追随共产党的领导，他也会发现这是不可能的。如果我们跟随蒋介石将军走这条路，我们将为了共产党而牺牲整个国家和人民。

“另一条路是复兴已故孙博士的教诲，并加强一种认识，即敌意应当消除而非助长。我们应该努力将日本视为朋友。

“首先，我们将恢复中日和平。
“其次，我们将建立东亚的持久和平。
“在我们面临的两条道路中，一条将毁灭中国和中华民族。另一条将恢复中国和东亚的繁荣。
“我已决定走第二条路。我将联合各党派人士以及无党派但关心中国命运的人士，沿着这条道路前进。”——同盟社。

CONFIDENTIAL
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. 8220
S. 5, Special Branch,
REPORT
Date July 10, 1939.
Subject Wang Ching-wei and activities of his partisans in Shanghai
Made by C. A. Loh Sih-kya Forwarded by [Signature], D.S.

Since his arrival in Shanghai last month, Wang Ching-
wei has been keeping his movements secret. His partisans
here are actively engaged in corrupting journalists,
compositors, pressmen, etc. in the employ of local Chinese
newspapers as well as responsible members of public bodies,
schools etc.

According to information obtained from his partisans,
Wang Ching-wei's peace movement is intended to promote the
welfare of China and the people. He has already secured the
agreement of the Japanese Government to the following three
conditions:-
1) That the new Chinese Central Government be still called
"The National Government."
2) That the blue sky flag be retained as the national flag.
3) That the Kuomintang be allowed to exist after its
reorganization.

The new Government will be formally inaugurated within
three months. Both the "Provisional Government" at Peking
and the "Reformed Government" at Nanking will be dissolved,
although the Commanders of the Japanese military and naval
forces in China and the officials of these two Governments are
strongly opposing Wang's plans. After the inauguration of
the new Government, the Yangtze River will be reopened to
navigation and the people will not be required to apply for
permits to return to their native homes in the interior.

Loh Sih Kya
Clerical Assistant.

机密
上海公共租界工部局警务处。
档案编号 8220
S. 5, 特别分部，
报告
日期 1939年7月10日。
主题 汪精卫及其党羽在上海的活动
制作人 C. A. 罗思嘉 (Loh Sih-kya) 转呈人 [签名], D.S.

自从上个月抵达上海以来，汪精卫一直对其行踪保密。他在上海的党羽正积极腐蚀受雇于当地中文报纸的记者、排字工人、印刷工人等，以及公共机构、学校等的负责成员。

根据从其党羽处获得的情报，汪精卫的和平运动旨在促进中国和人民的福祉。他已获得日本政府对以下三个条件的同意：-
1) 新的中国中央政府仍称为“国民政府”。
2) 保留青天白日旗为国旗。
3) 允许国民党在改组后继续存在。

新政府将在三个月内正式成立。北京的“临时政府”和南京的“维新政府”均将被解散，尽管在华日本海陆军指挥官及这两个政府的官员强烈反对汪的计划。新政府成立后，长江将重新开放航行，人民返回内地家乡无需申请许可证。

CHINA PRESS.
JUN 6 1939

**〔此处转录不清〕**

A Shanghai Base

WANG Ching-wei's associates in Shanghai are trying hard these days to make this city their major base of operation. Thus far they have found that the going has been extremely rough, but the Wang clan has not given up its activities here by any means.

Latest of their efforts is to buy a Chinese newspaper in Shanghai through which they can expound their "peace at any price" views and to convince Shanghailanders that the best thing they can do is to swing along with Wang Ching-wei. Our informant, who claimed that he got his report from 100 per cent reliable sources, said that Wang and his friends have been trying to buy a well-known local Chinese paper which, before it was banned, was published under British registration. In fact, our informant went so far as to say that the newspaper-buying deal was almost signed, sealed and delivered until the last minute hitch when the Chinese staff of the sheet put up a big walla walla.

At the moment, the chances are just 50-50 as to whether or not Wang would get his big-name Chinese paper in Shanghai.

Talking about Wang Ching-wei, we noticed that the exclusive story published by THE CHINA PRESS regarding his arrival here was translated and given a big play by every Chinese paper in town. We are glad that they all gave Ta Loh Pao the credit.

《大美晚报》 (CHINA PRESS).
1939年6月6日

**〔此处转录不清〕**

上海基地

汪精卫在上海的同伙近日正竭力使本市成为其主要行动基地。到目前为止，他们发现进展极其艰难，但汪氏家族绝未在此放弃活动。

他们最新的努力是通过收购上海的一家中文报纸，借此阐述其“不惜任何代价求和平”的观点，并说服上海外侨认为最好的做法是顺应汪精卫。我们的线人声称其报告来自百分之百可靠的来源，他说汪及其朋友一直试图收购一家知名的本地中文报纸，该报在被禁之前是在英国注册出版的。事实上，我们的线人甚至表示，购买报纸的交易几乎已签字盖章并交付，直到最后一刻出现波折，该报的中方员工大吵大闹 (put up a big walla walla)。

目前，汪能否在上海得到他那家大名鼎鼎的中文报纸，几率各占一半。

谈到汪精卫，我们注意到，《大美晚报》刊登的关于他抵达此地的独家报道被市内每家中文报纸翻译并大幅刊载。我们很高兴他们都归功于《大罗报》(Ta Loh Pao)。

（左侧椭圆印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 17 JULY 1939）

It is reported that in order to ensure the
safety of Wang Ching Wei, who is stated to be
endeavouring to inaugurate a new Federal Government,
the Japanese Military Special Service Section
instructed the Shanghai City Government to recruit
a total of 1,000 bodyguards to be used in his
protection. At present 500 men have enlisted
in this new unit which is now stationed in Kiangwan.
These men, who are armed with Mauser pistols, are
under the command of one Hung Tseng (洪正), a
Cantonese of 30 years of age, formerly a super-
intendent of the now defunct Police Bureau of the
Shanghai City Government. He is assisted by
a deputy, one named Moen Chi Wei (滿琪蔚), also
a Cantonese of 28 years of age and formerly a
Sub-Inspector of the Tungkadoo Police Station of
the Police Bureau in Lootung.

E.

Information has been received to the effect that
House 31, Lane 1136, Yu Yuen Road, C.C.L., will be made
the local residence of Wang Ching Wei and some of his
influential henchmen.

The premises are at present undergoing renovation.
Four brick observation towers are being constructed

Subject Reported arrival in Shanghai of Mr. Waung Ching Wei and the
secret pact with Tokio proposed by him.

Made by and Forwarded by. Supt. Tan Shao Liang

With reference to attached reports in the
Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury of May 12, 1939, enquiries
have failed to confirm that Mr. Waung Ching Wei had arrived
in Shanghai and left for Tokio in company with Fu Siao En.
From information received from a very reliable source,
it appears that Mrs. Waung has arrived with a few followers
of the deposed Kuomintang leader and is staying at 570 Rue
Joseph Kreulpt, French Concession. The followers have
leased a house at 726 Yu Yuen Road.

According to information from the same source,
Mr. Waung who is now still at Hanoi, will not join the
Japanese service until the Nanking Reformed Government
and the Peking Provisional Government have both been abolished.
It seems premature to talk of any proposals to Tokio.

Madame Waung will be leaving for Hanoi to accompany
her husband to Shanghai.

It is also reported that the Japanese Military
Authorities have returned to Madame Waung the residence
at No. 11/200 Amherst Avenue which they had seized since 1938.

（印：SHANGHAI COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 19 MAY 1939）

Tan Shaoliang

主题：据报道汪精卫先生抵达上海及其提出的与东京的秘密协定。

由谭绍良（Tan Shao Liang）巡官撰写并转呈

关于附带的1939年5月12日《上海晚邮与信使报》（Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury）中的报道，经查询未能证实汪精卫先生已抵达上海并与傅筱庵（Fu Siao En）一同前往东京。根据从非常可靠的消息来源获得的信息，汪夫人似乎已与几位被罢黜的国民党领导人的追随者抵达，并住在法租界约瑟夫·克鲁普特路（Rue Joseph Kreulpt，即今重庆南路一带，原文拼写有误，通常指Route Joseph Jrelupt或类似）570号。这些追随者在愚园路726号租赁了一所房屋。

根据同一消息来源的信息，目前仍在河内的汪先生，只有在南京维新政府和北京临时政府均被废除后，才会加入日本方面服务。谈论任何向东京提出的提议似乎为时过早。

汪夫人将前往河内，陪同其丈夫来上海。

另据报道，日本军方当局已将自1938年以来没收的爱麦虞厄路（Amherst Avenue，即今淮海中路）11/200号的住宅归还给汪夫人。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
68925

MAY 1 2 1939

Wang Declared /
Forming Regime

Deposed Party Leader
Claimed Residing
In Shanghai

Following negotiations with the
Japanese in Shanghai on April 24,
Mr. Wang Ching-wei left for
Tokyo aboard a Japanese warship
on April 27, to enter into further
discussions with Tokyo govern-
ment circles on a proposed secret
pact proposed by him, says a
Hongkong Chinese message to the
Morning Leader.

Mr. Wang, who was accom-
panied by Mr. Fu Siao-en, "Mayor
of Greater Shanghai," and a num-
ber of Japanese to Tokyo, return-
ed to Shanghai last Wednesday,
the report adds. Tokyo govern-
ment circles, the report alleges,
have "approved" Mr. Wang's pro-
posed secret pact, which embraces
the inauguration of an "Anti-
Chiang Kai-shek Movement," the
organization of a "Federal Cen-
tral Government," to obtain
formal recognition by Italy, Ger-
many, France, Britain and the
United States, and the forma-
tion of an anti-Chiang army, with
Mr. Wang Ching-wei as the
Commander-in-Chief.

All these proposed measures are
contingent on the abolition of the
"Provisional Government," which
will be converted into a "North
China Federal Autonomous Gov-
ernment." It is proposed that the
Japanese Government defray a
monthly sum of $30,000,000 for
the administrative expenditure of
the "Central Government," to be
secured by consolidation taxes
within its jurisdiction, the Morn-
ing Leader concludes.

Mr. Wang's close followers in-
cluding Mr. Chow Fu-hai, former
Minister of Publicity of the Kuo-
mintang, Mr. Kao Tsung-wu,
until recently director of the De-
partment of Asiatic Affairs of the
Foreign Ministry, and Mr. Li
Shen-wu, formerly Secretary-Gen-
eral of the Foreign Ministry and
publisher of the "Far Eastern
Miscellany," are reported to have
left Hongkong for Shanghai on
May 5, under instructions from
Mr. Wang, says another Hong-
kong Chinese message.

汪宣称/
组建政权

被罢黜的党派领导人
声称居住
在上海

据一份发给《晨导报》（Morning Leader）的香港中文消息称，在4月24日与日本人在上海进行谈判后，汪精卫先生于4月27日乘坐日本军舰前往东京，就其提出的秘密协定与东京政府圈子进行进一步讨论。

报道补充说，汪先生在“大上海市长”傅筱庵先生和数名日本人陪同下前往东京，于上周三返回上海。报道声称，东京政府圈子已“批准”汪先生提出的秘密协定，其中包括发起“反蒋介石运动”，组织“联邦中央政府”以获得意大利、德国、法国、英国和美国的正式承认，并组建一支反蒋军队，由汪精卫先生担任总司令。

报道总结称，所有这些拟议措施均有赖于废除“临时政府”，该政府将被改组为“华北联邦自治政府”。据提议，日本政府每月支付3,000万美元作为“中央政府”的行政开支，由其辖区内的统税作为担保。

另一则香港中文消息称，据报汪先生的亲密追随者，包括国民党前宣传部长周佛海先生、最近才卸任的外交部亚洲司司长高宗武先生，以及前外交部秘书长兼《远东杂志》（Far Eastern Miscellany）出版人李圣五先生，已遵照汪先生的指示，于5月5日离开香港前往上海。

May 10, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

Kuo Chi Jih Pao publishes the following letter:

WANG CHING-WEI TO PUBLISH MAGAZINE IN SHANGHAI

To the Editor,
In the "Lih Pao" (立報) of Hongkong of April 29, I read an article written by one Mr. Wong San (王三先生), stating that rebel Wang Ching-wei will order his followers to publish in Shanghai a magazine to be known as the "Tsu Yeu Yi Luen" ("Free Speech" 自由言論).
The following is the article written by Mr. Wong San:-
"The other day, 'stinking-sock-poet' (臭袜子诗人) came from Shanghai to receive manuscripts for a publication entitled 'Tsu Yeu Yi Luen' which is being established by traitors of Wang Ching-wei's clique. The magazine is printed in Shanghai and the 'stinking-sock-poet' is responsible for the printing. For fear that the manuscripts, if mailed to Shanghai from Hongkong, might go astray, he came personally to Hongkong to take delivery of them.
"Lieu Sha (流沙) and another writer are responsible for the editing of the magazine. The capital of the magazine is $2,500 Hongkong currency. This was supplied by rebel Wang Ching-wei and was paid to Lieu Sha through Ling Pah-sun (林柏生). On this account, Lieu Sha and another writer have become well-to-do.
"This author the other day wrote a letter to a certain literary body, stating that he had not done anything to secure manuscripts for the publication. The literary body concerned will take certain steps after the publication makes its appearance."
According to the above article, rebel Wang Ching-wei is planning to order his followers to publish in Shanghai a magazine to be called the "Tsu Yau Yi Luen". I hope that printers, news vendors, bookstore owners and readers will pay attention to this matter.
A reader named Wong Kung-ch-eng (王國常). dated May 8, 1939.

1939年5月10日。下午翻译。

《国际日报》（Kuo Chi Jih Pao）刊登以下信件：

汪精卫将在上海出版杂志

致编辑：
我在4月29日的香港《立报》上读到一篇由王三先生撰写的文章，称叛逆汪精卫将命令其追随者在上海出版一本名为《自由言论》（Tsu Yeu Yi Luen）的杂志。
以下是王三先生的文章：-
“日前，‘臭袜子诗人’从上海来接收稿件，用于出版由汪精卫叛徒集团建立的名为《自由言论》的刊物。该杂志在上海印刷，‘臭袜子诗人’负责印刷事宜。因担心从香港邮寄到上海的稿件可能会丢失，他亲自来到香港收取稿件。
“流沙（Lieu Sha）和另一位作家负责该杂志的编辑工作。该杂志的资本为港币2,500元。这笔资金由叛逆汪精卫提供，并通过林柏生支付给流沙。因此，流沙和另一位作家变得富裕起来。
“笔者日前致信某文学团体，声明自己并未为该出版物做任何征集稿件的工作。相关文学团体将在该刊物出现后采取某些措施。”
根据上述文章，叛逆汪精卫正计划命令其追随者在上海出版一本名为《自由言论》的杂志。希望印刷商、报贩、书店老板和读者注意此事。
读者王国常（Wong Kung-ch-eng），日期：1939年5月8日。

are distributed only among soldiers who are in sympathy with

April 24, 1939.

WANG CHING WEI REPORTED COMING TO SHANGHAI.

The whereabouts of Mr. Wang Ching-wei has become a great puzzle to the public in the past week. According to information secured from a fairly well informed source, Mr. Wang early in April left Hanoi for Siam from where he boarded a waiting Japanese gunboat for Canton. He arrived in Canton on April 8th but stayed on board there. In the evening of April 13, he is said to have broadcast a speech on board the Japanese gunboat. On April 12, Genera. Doihara is reported to have left Shanghai by plane for Canton for a conference with Mr. Wang. Since then there was the rumour of his arrival in Shanghai on April 15, but this could not be confirmed. A few days ago, the Japanese authorities here made preparations for Mr. Wang Ching-wei to stay at an apartment house called the Ramos Apartments, 192-5B North Szechuen Road. It is regarded not likely that Mr. Wang has already arrived. But it is confidently expected that he is coming here in the near future. It is learned that preparations have been made by local Japanese authorities to convene a meeting of the leaders of the two regimes of Peking and Nanking as soon as Mr. Wang arrives in Shanghai to decide many major issues.

It is further learned that the recent attempted assassination at Hanoi was staged by a small group of Chinese blue-shirt agents under the personal supervision of their leader Gen. Tai Li who made a special visit to the French colony for the job. A few days ago an urgent order was issued by the Chungking authorities to the local Chinese secret service headquarters here to arrange for the assassination of Mr. Wang and that a reward of $100,000 has been offered for the job. 据报道汪精卫将来沪。

在过去的一周里，汪精卫先生的行踪成为公众的一大谜团。据从消息相当灵通的来源获得的情报，汪先生于4月初离开河内前往暹罗，并从那里登上了一艘等候着的日本炮艇前往广州。他于4月8日抵达广州，但停留在船上。据说4月13日晚，他在日本炮艇上广播了一篇演讲。据报道，土肥原将军于4月12日乘飞机离开上海前往广州，与汪先生举行会谈。此后便有谣言称他将于4月15日抵达上海，但这未能得到证实。几天前，此地的日本当局为汪精卫先生入住位于北四川路192-5B号的拉莫斯公寓（Ramos Apartments）做了准备。目前认为汪先生已经抵达的可能性不大。但可以确信的是，他将在不久的将来来到这里。据悉，当地日本当局已做好准备，一旦汪先生抵达上海，即召开北京和南京两个政权领导人的会议，以决定许多重大问题。

另悉，最近在河内发生的未遂刺杀事件是由一小群中国蓝衣社特工策划的，由其首领戴笠将军亲自监督，戴笠为此专门访问了法属殖民地。几天前，重庆当局向此地的中国秘密情报总部发出紧急命令，安排刺杀汪先生，并为此事悬赏10万美元。出现在黑名单上的汪精卫先生的追随者包括前行政院秘书长朱民谊先生、前立法委员梅思平先生、直至最近仍担任国民党中央宣传部副部长的周佛海先生、前立法委员凌伯生先生（最近在香港一次未遂刺杀中受伤）、前外交部总务司司长李圣五先生、前实业部部长陈公博先生、陈璧君小姐（汪精卫夫人）、前国民党中央执行委员、前《民报》编辑兼汪先生首席宣传家唐良礼先生，以及前外交部亚洲司司长高宗武先生。

Mr. Wang Ching-wei, dismissed

Mr. Wang, who was read out of

late last week. The first time Mr.

terday that the former Kuo-

Frenchtown was heavily guarded
by plainclothes and uniformed
policemen. Construction and re-
pair work was in progress evident-
ly with the purpose of further
fortifying the structure, which is
located at the corner of Route
Frelupt and Route Dufour.
"No Enthusiasm"
An informed source told THE
CHINA PRESS that Mr. Wang is
not at the present time living in
this guarded house. The same
source revealed that foreign autho-
rities here have indirectly expressed
their lack of enthusiasm in having
Mr. Wang reside in the areas
under their jurisdiction.
It was revealed that Mr. Wang
is not staying anywhere south of
the Soochow Creek, despite the fact
that his own house in Frenchtown
is being renovated.
A reporter who visited the Wang
residence at the corner of Route
Frelupt and Route Dufour found
nine members of the French Muni-
cipal Police, four in uniform and
five plainclothesmen, guarding the
house which is located well off the
two roads.

《字林西报》。
: 14081

1939年6月4日

汪在上海逗留
毋庸置疑

法租界住所
翻新，严密守卫

《字林西报》昨日从可靠来源获悉，被罢免的国民党副总裁汪精卫先生目前是上海的居民。
尽管一层神秘的面纱仍然笼罩着这位前国民政府官员在本市的确切行踪，但《字林西报》获得的报道毫无疑问地表明他目前在上海。
据报道，汪先生因主张与日本“和平”而被开除出党，据说他于上周晚些时候返回上海。报道披露，汪先生第一次秘密抵达本市是在5月初。
在确认汪先生返回上海的报道时，《字林西报》记者昨日发现，这位前国民党领导人在法租界的住所受到便衣和制服警察的严密守卫。施工和维修工作正在进行中，显然是为了进一步加固该建筑，该建筑位于弗雷吕普路和杜福尔路的拐角处。
“缺乏热情”
一位消息人士告诉《字林西报》，汪先生目前并不住在这栋受保护的房子里。同一消息源透露，此地的外国当局已间接表示对汪先生居住在其管辖区域内缺乏热情。
据悉，尽管汪先生在法租界的房子正在翻新，但他并没有住在苏州河以南的任何地方。
一位访问了位于弗雷吕普路和杜福尔路拐角处汪宅的记者发现，法国公董局警务处的九名成员，其中四名穿制服，五名便衣，正在守卫这栋远离两条道路的住宅。

pages.en:
.: 14032

Residence Fortified
Looking at the rear of the
two-story house from an ad-
joining large, vacant lot, THE
CHINA PRESS reporter saw
that the residence was still in
the process of being fortified.
Laborers were at work doubling
the height of the residence.
Large windows had been built
in until they became mere
narrow slots.
Sitting down under the shade of
shrubs within the vacant lot were
three Chinese plainclothesmen, two
of them reading books. They re-
fused to have their photographs
taken and, when the representa-
tive of THE CHINA PRESS snap-
ped two pictures of the residence
asked him whether he knew who
lived within the residence. Receiv-
ing the reply that it was believed
that Wang Ching-wei had made
his home there, they exchanged
glances, but remained silent.
"Maybe Russian!"
Questioned by THE CHINA
PRESS representative, an Anna-
mite constable on duty at the front
of the house stated that he did
not think that the inmates of the
house were Chinese. "Peutetre ils
sont Russe," he said in French.
Asked why he should be guard-
ing Russian residents, the const-
able smiled, shrugged.
According to the report received
by THE CHINA PRESS yesterday,
Mr. Wang Ching-wei arrived in
Shanghai Friday morning. He was
last reported to be in Japan, ne-
gotiating with Premier Baron
Kiichiro Hiranuma and War Min-
ister Baron Sadao Araki. It was
stated by informed sources that
Mr. Wang may shortly take an-
other trip to Tokyo.
pages.zh:
.: 14032

住宅加固
从相邻的大片空地上看向这栋两层楼房的后部，《字林西报》记者看到该住宅仍处于加固过程中。工人们正在将住宅的高度加倍。大窗户已被封死，只剩下狭窄的缝隙。
三名中国便衣警察坐在空地内的灌木丛荫下，其中两人在看书。他们拒绝被拍照，当《字林西报》代表拍摄了两张住宅照片时，他们问他是否知道谁住在住宅里。听到回答说 believed 汪精卫已在此安家，他们交换了一下眼神，但保持沉默。
“也许是俄国人！”
《字林西报》代表询问在房屋前面执勤的一名安南巡捕时，他表示他认为屋内住户不是中国人。“Peutetre ils sont Russe，”他用法语说道。当被问及为何要守卫俄国居民时，这名巡捕笑了笑，耸了耸肩。
根据《字林西报》昨天收到的报道，汪精卫先生于周五上午抵达上海。上次据报道他在日本，与首相近卫文麿男爵和陆军大臣荒木贞夫男爵进行谈判。消息人士称，汪先生可能不久后将再次前往东京。

JUN 4. 1939.
Wang Ching-wei Friends
Not Arrested
Japanese Reports Denied
In Chungking
Chungking, June 3.
The Chinese authorities here
officially deny the Japanese reports
on "wholesale arrests" on May 25 and
26 by the Chungking Garrison Com-
mander's Headquarters, of Mr. Wang
Ching-wei's former associates, includ-
ing Mr. Chen Shu-jen, Chairman of
the Overseas Commission, and Mr.
Peng Hsueh-pei, Vice-Minister of
Communications.
These two officials, they add, are
attending their offices as usual.
Mr. Yu Yu-jen, President of the
Control Yuan, they continue, when
interviewed regarding the Japanese
report that he was killed during the
bombing of Chungking on May 25,
"smoothed his long beard and laughed
heartily."—Reuter.

汪精卫的朋友
未被逮捕
否认日本报道
重庆
重庆，6月3日。
此地中国当局正式否认日本关于重庆卫戍司令部总部于5月25日和26日“大规模逮捕”汪精卫前同僚的报道，其中包括侨务委员会委员长陈树人先生和交通部次长彭学沛先生。
他们补充说，这两名官员照常上班办公。
他们继续说，监察院院长于右任先生在接受采访时，针对日本报道说他于5月25日在重庆轰炸中丧生的说法，“抚摸着他的长须，开怀大笑”。——路透社。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,

JUN 7 1939

Mr. Wang Ching-wei's
Government Plans

Canton Probably Will Adhere
To Proposed Regime
FROM OUR OWN CORRESPONDENT

Hongkong, May 27.
Emissaries of the "Reformed Gov-
ernment" in Nanking are somewhere
in Hongkong and South China to con-
tact leading followers of Mr. Wang
Ching-wei in order to induce them
to go to the former capital to become
Cabinet Ministers or to accept other
lucrative posts. It is learned that
several of Wang's important followers
including Mr. Chen Kung-po are
still in South China.
The lesser lights are reported to
have left Hongkong for Shanghai last
week following the alleged return
of Mr. Wang Ching-wei from Japan
as reported in a Chungking dispatch.
It is said that he might shortly head
a new government under Japanese
auspices.
It is expected that the so-called
Peace Maintenance Commission in
Canton will adhere to the new régime
under Mr. Wang Ching-wei.
"General" Lu Chun-yung, a member
of the Canton outfit, is on his way to
Shanghai to interview Mr. Wang
concerning Canton's relations with
his new organization. After that he
will proceed to Japan to present the
views of his Canton colleagues on pos-
sible co-operation with the new
régime.
To maintain his prestige, Mr. Wang
is said to have suggested that Japan-
ese troops in Canton should be
evacuated in favour of Chinese pro-
tective corps, which is in charge of
peace preservation, and the Japanese
may consider such proposal.

1939年6月7日

汪精卫先生的
政府计划

广州可能会依附拟议中的政权
本报特约记者

香港，5月27日。
南京“维新政府”的特使目前 somewhere 在香港和华南地区，以接触汪精卫先生的主要追随者，诱使他们前往旧都担任内阁部长或接受其他肥缺。据悉，汪的几位重要追随者，包括陈公博先生，仍留在华南。
据称，随着重庆电文报道汪精卫先生从日本返回，一些小角色上周已离开香港前往上海。据说他不久将在日本的庇护下领导一个新政府。
预计广州所谓的“治安维持委员会”将依附汪精卫先生领导的新政权。
广州方面的人物、“将军”卢春荣（Lu Chun-yung，音译）正前往上海，就广州与其新组织的关系问题会见汪先生。此后，他将前往日本，向其日本同事陈述关于与新政权可能合作的观点。
为了维护自己的声望，据说汪先生建议驻广州的日军撤出，改由中国负责维持和平的保护部队接替，日本方面可能会考虑这一提议。

Subject Present whereabouts of Wang Ching Wei.

Made by. D.I. Yuh Pao-hwa, Forwarded by C. Crawford.

With reference to the query of D.C. (Special Branch), I have to state that at the time of forwarding the last report, information was to hand to the effect that Wang Ching Wei had left for Tokyo at 7 a.m. May 26, leaving by air from the Kiangwan Aerodrome, for the purpose of conferring with the Japanese Premier, the War Minister and other prominent Government officials on the establishment of a New Central Government; the reorganization of the present Peiping Provisional Government; the Nanking Reformed Government; and terms for a possible Sino-Japanese armistice. The information was not included in the last report because it could not be confirmed.

Information now is that Wang returned by air from Tokyo on June 2, arriving at Kiangwan at 4 p.m. in company with two other persons (Mrs. Wang formed one of the party, it is reported). The party proceeded to Hongkew District and it is believed that they are living in the Broadway Mansions.

Following his return to Shanghai, Wang Ching Wei held a conference on June 3rd with Vice Admiral Oikawa, Commander of Japanese Navy, Colonel K. No. 3877/S dated April 19, 1939.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. & B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 8186

CONFIDENTIAL

Reaction of pro-Japanese Chinese
Governments to the activities
of the WANG CHING WEI group.

According to information secured from responsible
Chinese sources, representatives of Mr. WANG CHING WEI
negotiating with the Japanese authorities have made the
following demands of the Japanese:-

（批：Commr
Sd.
Information
for Protection
DC(SB)）

1. The abolition of the Reformed Government at Nanking
and the Peking Provisional Government.
2. The creation of a new Central Government at Nanking
under the presidency of WANG CHING WEI.

Although up to the present, the Japanese authorities
have never appeared willing to replace the two pro-
Japanese Governments already existing by a Central
Government, rumours now being circulated in regard to
the demands presented by Mr. WANG CHING WEI, are said
to have alarmed high officials of the Reformed organs.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 20 APR. 1939）

It is evident that if these demands were accepted -
a remote contingency, however - the majority of members
of the Nanking and Peking Governments would be obliged
to retire from the political arena. In order to avoid
this possibility, they are reported to be making
overtures to thwart the project which is attributed
to the ex-Fu Tsung Tsai of the Kuomintang.

It is said that with this end in mind, Mr. CHEN
CHUN, Minister of the Interior in the Reformed Government,
recently proceeded to North China where he conferred
with Mr. WANG KE MING, President of the Executive
Commission of the Peking Provisional Government on
steps to be taken to oppose the machinations of the
WANG CHING WEI clique.

（批：Desk
FILE
D.C.
P.A. to D.C. (So. Br.)
20/4.）

After having seen WANG KE MING, CHEN CHUN returned
to Nanking. On April 13, accompanied by Mr. WENG TSUNG

根据从可靠中方来源获得的信息，代表汪精卫先生与日本当局谈判的人员向日本提出了以下要求：

（批注： commissioner
签名。
供保护科

1. 废除南京维新政府和北平临时政府。
2. 在南京建立一个新的中央政府，由汪精卫担任主席。

尽管到目前为止，日本当局似乎从未愿意用中央政府取代现有的两个亲日政府，但现在流传的关于汪精卫先生所提要求的谣言，据说已引起维新机构高官的恐慌。

（印章：上海公共租界总办处 1939年4月20日）

显然，如果这些要求被接受——尽管这种可能性微乎其微——南京和北平政府的大多数成员将被迫退出政治舞台。为了避免这种可能性，据报道，他们正在采取行动，挫败这位前国民党副总裁所策划的计划。

据说，为此目的，维新政府内政部长陈群先生最近前往华北，与北平临时政府执行委员会主席王克敏先生会晤，商讨反对汪精卫派系阴谋的步骤。

（批注：文书科
归档

会见王克敏后，陈群返回南京。4月13日，他在翁宗

YAO, President of the Legislative Yuan in the
Reformed Government, he left Shanghai for Japan in
the s.s. "Nagasaki Maru."

During their stay in Tokyo, these high officials
of the Reformed Government, supported by Mr. WANG KE MING,
are attempting to show the Japanese authorities that
WANG CHING WEI no longer enjoys any influence, that he
has lost all his prestige and that he can never rely on
the support of the Chinese people. Thus they hope to
discredit sufficiently WANG CHING WEI's establishment
of a Central Government - in the event of such a move
being considered.

尧（Weng Tsung Yao，音译，维新政府立法院院长）的陪同下，乘坐“长崎丸”号轮船离开上海前往日本。

在东京期间，这些维新政府的高官在王克敏先生的支持下，试图向日本当局表明，汪精卫不再拥有任何影响力，他已经失去了所有的威望，并且永远无法依靠中国人民的支持。因此，他们希望充分破坏汪精卫建立中央政府的企图——万一日本方面考虑此举的话。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.B. Special Branch
REPORT
Date ____ April 5 ____ 1939.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY No. S. 86 Doff）

Subject .... Reported attempt of Wang Ching wei to become President of
puppet Central Government of China.
Made by .... and .... Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

（左侧手写批注：Commr Sei, Information of the Roberts D.C.(S)）

The murder of Tseng Chung Ling, ex-Vice Minister
of Railways, the right hand man of Mr. Wang Ching Wei, gave
rise to various speculations as to the attitude Mr. Wang would
adopt in the near future.

Enquiries have been made amongst ex-government
officials and pro-Japanese elements and from information gathered
it would appear too premature to assume that Mr. Wang, incensed
at the murder of Tseng, will immediately take up any position
with the Japanese. In view of the failure of his peace movement
and as he is still suffering from nervous debility Mr. Wang will
be very careful in choosing the right moment and will not
participate openly in the affairs of the puppet regime until
the Japanese have captured Honan and Hunan and cleared these
provinces of the guerillas.

It is believed in pro-Japanese sources that should
the Japanese military succeed in taking Honan and Hunan they will
temporarily cease their operations and confine their efforts in
fortifying defence works as well as carrying out mopping up
measures against guerillas in territory already occupied.

（左侧盖章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 5 APR. 1939）

With the object of assisting Japanese in the guerilla warfare
the Reformed Government has, it is reported, recruited over
100,000 men, Chinese of course. These recruits are equipped with
rifles and machine guns and after being trained by Japanese
instructors they will be put under the command of General Jen Yuen
Dau (任援道), the Minister of Pacification in the Reformed
Government (There is no Ministry of War in the Reformed Government).
It is said that these Chinese soldiers when leaving their barracks
on errand will be supervised by Japanese or Koreans.

（左侧盖章/批注：FILE P.A. to D.C. (Sp. Br.)）

D.C. (Special Branch)

Tan Shaoliang
Superintendent.

日期 1939年4月5日 ____ 。

（印章：上海公共租界工部局特别处登记处 编号 S. 86 Doff）

主题 ____ 据报道汪精卫企图成为中国傀儡中央政府主席。
制作人 ____ 和 ____ 转呈人：谭绍良巡官

（左侧手写批注：Commissioner Sei, Roberts 副督察(特别处)的情报）

前铁道部次长、汪精卫先生的得力助手曾仲鸣的被杀，引发了人们对汪先生在不久的将来会采取何种态度的各种猜测。

向前政府官员和亲日分子进行的询问以及收集到的信息表明，现在假设汪先生因曾仲鸣被杀而愤怒，并立即在日本占据任何职位还为时过早。鉴于他的和平运动失败，且他仍患有神经衰弱，汪先生在选择合适时机时会非常谨慎，在日本占领河南和湖南并清除这些省份的游击队之前，他不会公开参与傀儡政权的事务。

亲日方面的消息人士认为，如果日本军队成功占领河南和湖南，他们将暂时停止作战行动，将其努力集中在巩固防御工事以及对已占领领土内的游击队进行扫荡措施上。

（左侧盖章：上海公共租界工部局总办处 1939年4月5日）

据报道，为了协助日本人进行游击战，维新政府招募了超过10万名中国人。这些新兵配备了步枪和机枪，在经过日本教官训练后，将由维新政府绥靖部部长任援道将军指挥（维新政府没有陆军部）。据说，这些中国士兵外出办事时，会受到日本人或朝鲜人的监视。

Morning Leader (Hongkong telegram) :-

WANG CHING-WEI TO BECOME PRESIDENT OF BOGUS
CENTRAL GOVERNMENT

On March 31, Wang Ching-wei issued a
statement on the death of Tseng Chung-ming, in the course
of which he made certain allegations against the National
Government and indicates that he would not proceed to
Europe.

According to reliable information,
Wang Ching-wei is making preparations to become a puppet
and if the Japanese War Office agrees to the formation
of a bogus Central Government, he will become its
President.

It is reported that the Japanese War
Office intends to form a bogus Central Government after
the whole of the Canton-Hankow Railway has been seized.

Standard (Evening Edition) published the following comment
on April 2 :-

Wang Ching-wei has, on many occasions,
made suggestions for surrender, for this he is being
cursed by the people. This time, he has misinterpreted
the policy of the National Government in order to
support his absurd ideas.

For the past 20 months, the National
Government has been firmly carrying on the war of
resistance. The false allegations made by Wang Ching-
wei will have no effect.

《晨导报》（香港电报）：

汪精卫将成为伪中央政府主席

3月31日，汪精卫就曾仲铭之死发表声明，其间他对国民政府提出某些指控，并表示他不会前往欧洲。

根据可靠消息，
汪精卫正在准备成为傀儡，如果日本陆军省同意组建一个伪中央政府，他将成为其主席。

据报道，日本陆军省打算在整个粤汉铁路被占领后组建一个伪中央政府。

《标准晚报》于4月2日发表了以下评论：

汪精卫曾多次提出投降建议，因此受到民众的咒骂。这一次，他曲解了国民政府的政策，以支持其荒谬的观点。

在过去20个月里，国民政府一直坚定地继续进行抗战。汪精卫的虚假指控不会产生任何影响。

S. 2 Special Branch,
January 25, 1939.

Actual influence of Mr. Waung Ching Wei as summarised by a
political observer.

The influence, enjoyed by Mr. Waung Ching Wei, until
recently the Chairman of the Central Political Council, at
the time of his departure from Chungking was, according to
an independent political observer, nothing in comparison
with that wielded by him in 1932 when he was reinstated in
the Government service at the termination of the peace
conference in Shanghai. In this connection it may be
interesting to review his activities during the past few
years.

In 1932 he was the Chief of the Reorganization Party
of the Kuomintang and was backed up not only by a number
of civilians but by military leaders of the Kwangtung and
Kwangsi cliques including General Chen Ming Chu and General
Chen Fah Kwe. Mr. Waung had then a large following due to
the influence of several of his principal adherents having
obtained high positions in the Nanking Government such as
Chen Kung Po as Minister of Industry, Koo Meng Yu as Minister
of Railways, Tseng Chung Ming as Vice Minister of Railways,
Dr. Chu Ming Nyi as Chief Secretary of the Executive Yuan and
Chen Pih Chun (Madame Waung) as a member of the Central
Committee of the Kuomintang.

Mr. Waung soon lost the sympathy of the Southern
political leaders when he adopted an indifferent attitude
towards the Fukien rebellion which was started by Commanders
of the former 19th. Route Army; he further betrayed them by
issuing orders for their arrest after the failure of the
rebellion.

The pro-Japanese policy followed by Mr. Waung when he
was chief of the Executive Yuan having proved a failure and
incurred severe criticism especially over the conclusion of

一位政治观察家总结的汪精卫先生的实际影响力。

据一位独立政治观察家称，汪精卫先生（最近曾任中央政治委员会主席）在离开重庆时所享有的影响力，与1932年上海和平会议结束时他复职政府服务时所拥有的影响力相比，简直微不足道。在这方面，回顾他过去几年的活动或许很有趣。

1932年，他是国民党改组派的领袖，不仅得到许多文人的支持，还得到包括陈铭枢将军和陈济棠将军在内的粤系和桂系军事领导人的支持。当时，汪先生拥有大量的追随者，这是因为他的几位主要 adherents 在南京政府中获得了高位，如陈公博任实业部长，顾孟余任铁道部长，曾仲鸣任铁道部次长，褚民谊博士任行政院秘书长，以及陈璧君（汪夫人）任国民党中央委员。

当汪先生对由原第十九路军指挥官发起的福建事变采取冷漠态度时，他很快失去了南方政治领导人的同情；在事变失败后，他进一步背叛了他们，下令逮捕他们。

汪先生在担任行政院长期间推行的亲日政策已被证明是失败的，并招致严厉批评，特别是在缔结

pages.en:
- 2 -

the Umetsu-Ho (Ying Ching) Agreement at Tientsin, strife
broke out amongst members of his clique and this resulted
in several of his followers going over to side of Chiang
Kai-shek whilst others were removed from their positions
one after the other.

An attempt was made on his life at Nanking on November
1, 1935. The investigation that followed revealed that the
would-be assassin was in the pay of Southern political
leaders including General Chen Ming Chu, his principal
supporter in 1932. Mr. Wang became so disheartened that
he gave up his position and went for a trip abroad. His
principal followers Chen Kung Po, Tseng Chung Ming, and
others went with him. They remained idle until the Sian
Coup in December 1936 when Mr. Wang hurried back to China
in the hope of regaining his political influence. When he
arrived in China in January 1937, he found to his disappoint-
ment that General Chiang Kai-shek had been released. He was,
however, invited to Nanking and was given a position in the
Central Tangpu but his followers were not accorded the
favourable treatment they received in 1932.

Although he and Sun Fo served as the Southern delegates
in the peace conference in 1932 they were in complete dis-
agreement over the question of diplomatic policy, Wang being
pro-Japanese whilst Sun was pro-Soviet. A few of the Kuoming-
tang members who had received Japanese education supported Mr.
Wang recently in the "peace" movement, these including
General Ho Yin Chin and General Hsiung Shih Hwe, but although
agreed to Wang's policy they were not his loyal supporters,
for they have changed their attitude upon finding that Mr.
Wang had left Chungking.

Only Wang's principal adherents have left their posts
to join him, these being Chen Kung Po, Tseng Chung Ming, Ko
Meng Yu, Kao Chung Wu and Mai Yu Ping.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

在天津签订《梅津-何（应钦）协定》后，其派系内部发生争斗，导致其部分追随者转投蒋介石一方，而其他人则相继被免职。

1935年11月1日，他在南京遭遇暗杀未遂。随后的调查表明，行刺者受南方政治领袖收买，其中包括陈铭枢将军，后者曾是他在1932年的主要支持者。汪先生因此心灰意冷，辞去职务并出国游历。其主要追随者陈公博、曾仲明等人随行。他们一直赋闲，直到1936年12月西安事变爆发，汪先生匆忙返回中国，希望能重获政治影响力。然而，当他于1937年1月抵达中国时，失望地发现蒋介石已被释放。尽管如此，他仍被邀请前往南京，并在中央党部获得职位，但其追随者并未享受到他们在1932年所获得的优待。

虽然他和孙科在1932年的和平会议上均担任南方代表，但两人在外交政策问题上存在严重分歧，汪主张亲日，而孙主张亲苏。最近，少数受过日本教育的国民党成员在“和平”运动中支持汪先生，其中包括何应钦将军和熊式辉将军，但他们虽然同意汪的政策，却并非其忠诚支持者，因为在发现汪先生离开重庆后，他们已改变了态度。

只有汪的主要 adherents 离职加入了他，这些人包括陈公博、曾仲明、顾孟余、高宗武和梅育平。

On his way to Hanoi, Mr. Waung is alleged to have
made an attempt to induce General Lung Yuen, the Military
and Civil Governor of Yunnan, to join him in the peace
movement but the latter secretly telegraphed to Generalissimo
Chiang Kai-shek exposing Waung's intrigues.

Of the other military leaders in the South, it is
beyond doubt that Generals Li Chung Jen and Pei Chung Hsi
will not change their war policy as they were the first and
the strongest faction to advocate hostilities.

As for Szechuen Gen **〔此处转录不清〕** hey have always maintained
a neutral attitude in the quarrels between Mr. Waung and the
Government and will continue in this policy so long as their
military power is unimpaired.

There is, however, some danger attached to the attitude
of General Chen Yi, Governor of Fukien who has a Japanese
wife and General Chang Fah Kwei, Commander of the Southern
troops in Kwangtung who was originally a subordinate of Mr,
Waung and according to information from pro-Japanese sources
steps are being taken by Japanese agents to induce them to
join in the organization of a Southern Government at Canton
with Mr. Waung Ching Wei as Chief and the two Generals as his
supporters. It is as yet premature to say how far these
attempts will be successful but with the foreign loans and
the general situation favourable to the Chungking Government
it is unlikely that the two Southern generals will join Mr.
Waung.

Mr. Waung is regarded as the worst enemy by the
communists whom he betrayed during the split between the
Kuomintang and Communists in 1927.

Mr. T.V. Soong has been sent to Hanoi where Mr. Waung
is believed to be still in hiding, with the object of
persuading him to cease his peace activities and to go to

据称，汪先生在前往河内的途中，试图诱使云南军政长官龙云将军加入其和平运动，但龙云秘密致电蒋介石委员长，揭露了汪的阴谋。

至于南方的其他军事领袖，毫无疑问，李宗仁将军和白崇禧将军不会改变其抗战政策，因为他们是最早且最强烈主张抗战的派系。

至于四川将领 **〔此处转录不清〕** ，他们在汪先生与政府之间的争端中始终保持中立态度，只要其军事实力不受损，他们将继续维持这一政策。

然而，福建省主席陈仪将军（其妻为日本人）以及广东南方部队指挥官张发奎将军（原为汪先生的下属）的态度存在一定的危险性。根据亲日方面的情报，日本特工正采取措施，诱使他们参与在广州组织以汪精卫为首、两位将军为支持的南方政府。目前断言这些尝试能在多大程度上取得成功还为时过早，但鉴于外国贷款及总体局势有利于重庆政府，这两位南方将军加入汪先生一方的可能性不大。

汪先生被共产党视为最危险的敌人，因为他在1927年国共分裂期间背叛了共产党。

宋子文先生已被派往河内，据信汪先生仍藏匿于此，目的是劝说他停止和平活动，并在中国政府提供资金的情况下出国。由于据说宋先生与汪先生关系友好，此间的朋友坚信他将成功完成使命。

1935年11月1日，他在南京遭遇暗杀未遂。随后的调查表明，行刺者受南方政治领袖收买，其中包括陈铭枢将军，后者曾是他在1932年的主要支持者。汪先生因此心灰意冷，辞去职务并出国游历。其主要追随者陈公博、曾仲鸣等人随行。他们一直赋闲，直到1936年12月西安事变爆发，汪先生匆忙返回中国，希望能重获政治影响力。然而，当他于1937年1月抵达中国时，失望地发现蒋介石已被释放。尽管如此，他仍被邀请前往南京，并在中央党部获得职位，但其追随者并未享受到他们在1932年所获得的优待。
虽然他和孙科在1932年的和平会议上均担任南方代表，但两人在外交政策问题上存在严重分歧，汪主张亲日，而孙主张亲苏。最近，少数受过日本教育的国民党成员在“和平”运动中支持汪先生，其中包括何应钦将军和熊式辉将军，但他们虽然同意汪的政策，却并非其忠诚支持者，因为在发现汪先生离开重庆后，他们已改变了态度。
只有汪的主要追随者离职加入了他，这些人包括陈公博、曾仲鸣、顾孟余、高宗武和梅育平。

    On his way to Hanoi, Mr. Waung is alleged to have
made an attempt to induce General Lung Yuen, the Military
and Civil Governor of Yunnan, to join him in the peace movement
but the latter secretly telegraphed to Generalissimo Chiang
Kai Shek exposing Waung's intrigues.
    Of the other military leaders in the South, it is
beyond doubt that Generals Li Chung Jen and Lei Chung Hsi will
not change their war policy as they were the first and the
strongest faction to advocate hostilities.
    As for the Szechuen Generals they have always main-
tained a neutral attitude in the quarrels between Mr. Waung
and the Government and will continue in this policy so long as
their military power is unimpaired.
    There is, however, some danger attached to the
attitude of General Chen Yi, Governor of Fukien who has a
Japanese wife and General Chang Fah Kwei, Commander of the
Southern troops in Kwangtung who was originally a subordinate
of Mr. Waung and according to information from pro-Japanese
sources steps are being taken by Japanese agents to induce
them to join in the organization of a Southern Government at
Canton with Mr. Waung Ching Wei as Chief and the two generals
as his supporters. It is as yet premature to say how far
these attempts will be successful but with the foreign loans
and the general situation favourable to the Chungking Govern-
ment it is unlikely that the two Southern generals will join
Mr. Waung.
    Mr. Waung is regarded as the worst enemy by the
communists whom he betrayed during the split between the
Kuomintang and Communists in 1927.

    据称，汪先生在前往河内的途中，试图诱使云南军政长官龙云将军加入其和平运动，但龙云秘密致电蒋介石委员长，揭露了汪的阴谋。
    至于南方的其他军事领袖，毫无疑问，李宗仁将军和白崇禧将军不会改变其抗战政策，因为他们是最早且最强烈主张抗战的派系。
    至于四川将领，他们在汪先生与政府之间的争端中始终保持中立态度，只要其军事实力不受损，他们将继续维持这一政策。
    然而，福建省主席陈仪将军（其妻为日本人）以及广东南方部队指挥官张发奎将军（原为汪先生的下属）的态度存在一定的危险性。根据亲日方面的情报，日本特工正采取措施，诱使他们参与在广州组织以汪精卫为首、两位将军为支持的南方政府。目前断言这些尝试能在多大程度上取得成功还为时过早，但鉴于外国贷款及总体局势有利于重庆政府，这两位南方将军加入汪先生一方的可能性不大。
    汪先生被共产党视为最危险的敌人，因为他在1927年国共分裂期间背叛了共产党。
