Subject Propaganda Advocating Peace in Western District, U.O.L.

Made by D.S.I. Liao Chung-chien Forwarded by C. Crawford. O.J.

On January 21, 1939, copies of a handbill and a poster advocating peace were found posted on walls and notice boards in the vicinity of the various sections and sub-sections of the Police Bureau in the extra-Settlement roads in the Western District. The handbill quotes a telegram issued by Mr. Wang Ching Wei advocating peace with Japan and bears a photograph of Mr. Wang. It is exactly similar to those dropped from an airplane flying over the Settlement on January 5, 1939. The poster (a copy of which is attached herewith) contains the following three points, which were embodied in the announcement made by the Premier of Japan on December 22, 1938:-

1. Japan has no territorial ambition in China and will demand no indemnity from the latter. She hopes that the three countries, Japan, Manchukuo and China will unite and build a new order in East Asia. She also hopes that Japan and China will conclude an anti-Comintern Pact and effectively carry out economic cooperation.

2. Japan will respect China's integrity. Furthermore she wishes to see an independent state established in China.

3. Japan will abolish the extraterritorial rights she enjoys in China in order to enable China to build up a new rule. Simultaneously Japan will give the restoration of her concessions to China serious consideration.

（左侧手写批注：3/2 24.1.39.）
（左下角印章及手写字：FILE / D.B. / D.C. (Sp. Br.) / D.C. (Special Branch) / 24/1）

D. S. I.

由 副督察 廖仲坚 制作 经由 C. Crawford. O.J. 转呈

1939年1月21日，在西区越界筑路地段各警察分局及分驻所附近的墙壁和布告栏上，发现了张贴的倡导和平的传单和海报副本。该传单引用了汪精卫先生发出的主张与日本和平的电文，并附有汪先生的照片。这与1939年1月5日从飞越租界的飞机上撒下的传单完全相同。海报（副本附后）包含以下三点，这三点体现在日本首相于1938年12月22日发表的声明中：-

1. 日本对中国没有领土野心，也不会向中国索取赔款。日本希望日本、满洲国和中国三国联合，在东亚建立新秩序。日本还希望日本与中国缔结反共产国际协定，并切实开展经济合作。

2. 日本将尊重中国的完整。此外，日本希望看到一个独立的中国国家建立起来。

3. 日本将废除其在中国享有的治外法权，以便中国建立新的统治。同时，日本将认真考虑将其租界归还中国。

（左侧手写批注：3/2 24.1.39.）
（左下角印章及手写字：FILE / D.B. / D.C. (Sp. Br.) / D.C. (Special Branch) / 24/1）

REPORT

Subject Slogans written in black characters on red papers were posted
on electric poles on Robison Road near Kiaochow Road.

Made by D.S.I. Burton. Forwarded by J. S. Farlane inspt. i/c.

Sir,

At 11.30 a.m. on the 22.1.39., C.P.C. 391 reported
to the station per street telephone Box No. 12 Robison and
Kiaochow Roads corner that slogans written in black characters
on red papers were posted on electric poles at the above
place.

C.D.C. 256 proceeded to the point where he copied
down the characters which read as follows:-

1. Down with Chiang Kai Shek's Political Control.
(打倒政權)。

2. To up-hold Wong Ching Wei's peace proposal.
(擁護汪精衛和平主張)。

3. Every one will be glad if peace occurs soon.
(和平早現人皆喜)。

4. To co-operate with your good neighbour, Japan.
(與仁善鄰日合作)。

5. All commerce will become prosperous when
businesses and residences have become re-establish-
ed.
(安居樂業新業將興)。

Enquiries were made in the vicinity and it was learnt
that the pamphlets had been posted by the Tan Tao Police.

A tour of the district was made but no other slogans
were found. Slogans washed off by station coolie.

D.S.I.
SR. dated 22/1/39
D.D.O. "B" Division.

REPORT
Date January 16 1939

Subject. Plans for establishment of Provincial Government in
South China.

Made by and Forwarded by Insp. Papp

According to information received from a fairly
reliable source, the Japanese Special Service Authorities
firmly believe that Mr. Wang Ching Wei (汪精衛) is supported
in his peace movement by Mr. Chu Cheng (居正), President of
the Judicial Yuan, General Tang Chan Su (王纘緒), powerful
warlord of Szechuen, General Lung Yun (龍雲), Chairman of
the Yunnan Provincial Government, Mr. Chen Lih Fu (陳立夫)
and Mr. Chen Kuo Fu (陳果夫), leaders of the so-called C.C.
Clique, and a number of generals in Kwangtung and Kwangsi.

They further believe that there are approximately
300,000 troops on the side of Mr. Wang who, if reinforced
with the Japanese Air Force and modern war equipment, can well
match General Chiang's forces which are estimated to be about
400,000 in number and the Communist Army with an estimated
strength of over 300,000 troops. The Japanese are hoping
that Mr. Wang will in the near future assume leadership of the
proposed South China Provincial Government in Canton. When
this plan is realized the Japanese would make necessary
concessions such as the withdrawal of troops from the occupied
areas in South China so as to give Mr. Wang enough prestige to
command public influence. They also would give Mr. Wang suffi-
cient financial backing to enable him to carry on all kinds
of pro-Japanese activities.

The foregoing views are held by the Japanese Special
Service and the actual intentions of Mr. Wang Ching Wei are not
yet known. On the other hand, information received from other
sources does not exclude the possibility that Mr. Wang may depart
for Europe, especially owing to the negative results his peace
overtures seem to have achieved.

由 督察 Papp 制作并转呈

根据从相当可靠来源获得的情报，日本特务机关坚信，汪精卫先生（汪精衛）的和平运动得到了司法院院长居正先生（居正）、四川实力派军阀唐灿苏将军（王纘緒）[注：原文英文为Tang Chan Su，括号内中文为王缵绪，此处依原文括号内中文译出]、云南省政府主席龙云将军（龍雲）、所谓CC系领袖陈立夫先生（陳立夫）和陈果夫先生（陳果夫），以及广东和广西的一些将军的支持。

他们进一步相信，汪先生一方约有30万军队，如果得到日本空军和现代战争装备的增援，完全可以与估计约为40万人的蒋介石部队以及估计兵力超过30万人的共产党军队相抗衡。日本人希望汪先生在不久的将来出任拟议中的广州华南省政府领导人。当这一计划实现时，日本人将作出必要的让步，例如从华南占领区撤军，以使汪先生拥有足够的威望来指挥公众影响力。他们还将给予汪先生足够的财政支持，使他能够开展各种亲日活动。

上述观点为日本特务机关所持，汪精卫先生的真实意图尚不清楚。另一方面，从其他来源获得的情报并不排除汪先生可能前往欧洲的可能性，特别是鉴于他的和平试探似乎取得了负面结果。

WANG CHING-WEI'S TELEGRAM TO CENTRAL KUOMINTANG HEADQUARTERS
SUGGESTING OPENING OF PEACE NEGOTIATIONS WITH JAPAN (Hua Mei
Chen Pao, Hongkong telegram, December 30)

Mr. Wang Ching-wei has sent the following telegram
to the Central Kuomintang Headquarters :-
In April this year, the National Congress issued a
manifesto explaining China's war of resistance as follows :-
" Since the Tangku Agreement, we have been
forbearing when dealing with Japan, our object being
to try by peaceful means to safeguard the provinces
in the North and to find a just solution of the question
of the Four North-Eastern Provinces. Politically,
our minimum desire is to preserve China's sovereign
rights and economy, we want mutual benefit and
equality."
Following the occurrence of the Lukouchiao Incident
in July, 1937, China was compelled to fight a war of
resistance. I have now read a statement issued by the
Japanese Government on December 22 dealing with fundamentals
for a readjustment of Sino-Japanese relations; it contains
the following three points :-
(1) GOOD NEIGHBOURS - Japan has no territorial
designs on China nor will she demand compensation for
military expenses. Japan not only will respect the
sovereign rights of China, but she will return her
Concessions to China and abolish extraterritoriality so
that China may obtain complete independence.
Since the Japanese Government has issued such a
statement, we shall be in a position to protect the
Northern provinces, recover all territories lost during
the operations and preserve China's sovereign rights and
administrative integrity by peaceful means. Thus, we
may find a reasonable solution of the problem of the Four
North-Eastern Provinces according to the manifesto issued
by the National Congress.
(2) JOINT ANTI-COMMUNISM - A few years ago,
Japan made such a suggestion on many occasions. We did not
accept it because we feared that our military and civil
affairs might be interfered with. Now the Japanese
Government has clearly stated that a Sino-Japanese Anti-
Communist Agreement should be signed in the spirit of the
Japan-Italo-German Anti-Communist Pact. The object of
guarding against Communists is to suppress plots for
disturbances by the Communists; it will have no adverse
effect upon the relations between China and Soviet Russia.
Since the members of the Chinese Communist Party have
expressed their willingness to fight for the Three
Principles of the People, they should give up their
organization and propaganda and abolish their army and
subject themselves completely to the law of China.
Anything that is done against the Three Principles of the
People, the supreme principle for the foundation of the
Republic of China, must be suppressed.
(3) ECONOMIC RAPPROCHEMENT - This point has
been repeatedly suggested by Japan to China during the

汪精卫致国民党中央总部建议与日本开启和平谈判的电报（《华美晨报》，香港电，12月30日）

汪精卫先生已向国民党中央总部发出如下电报：-

今年四月，全国代表大会发布宣言，阐述中国的抗战如下：-
“自《塘沽协定》以来，我们在对日交涉中一直采取克制态度，目的是试图通过和平手段保卫北方各省，并寻求东北四省问题的公正解决。在政治上，我们最低的愿望是维护中国的主权和经济，我们要互利和平等。”

继1937年7月发生卢沟桥事变后，中国被迫进行抗战。我现已阅悉日本政府于12月22日发表的关于调整中日关系基本原则的声明；该声明包含以下三点：-

(1) 善邻友好 - 日本对中国没有领土野心，也不会要求赔偿军费。日本不仅将尊重中国的主权，而且会将她的租界归还中国，并废除治外法权，从而使中国获得完全独立。

既然日本政府发表了这样的声明，我们将有能力通过和平手段保护北方各省，收复作战期间失去的所有领土，并维护中国的主权和行政完整。因此，我们可以根据全国代表大会发布的宣言，为东北四省问题找到合理的解决方案。

(2) 共同防共 - 几年前，日本曾多次提出此类建议。我们当时未予接受，因为我们担心我们的军事和民事事务可能会受到干涉。现在日本政府已明确表示，应本着《日意德反共产国际协定》的精神签署中日防共协定。防范共产主义者的目的是镇压共产主义者制造的动乱阴谋；这不会对中苏关系产生不利影响。鉴于中国共产党成员已表示愿意为三民主义而战，他们应当放弃其组织和宣传，解散其军队，并完全服从中国法律。任何违背作为中华民国建国最高原则的三民主义的行为，都必须予以镇压。

(3) 经济提携 - 这一点在过去几年中已被日本多次向中国提出。

past few years. Now the Japanese Government clearly
declares that Japan will respect China's sovereign rights
and her administrative integrity and that Japan has no
desire to have sole control of economics in China nor has
she a desire to request China to restrict the interests
of any third Power in China. She desires economic
rapprochement on the principles of equality. Therefore,
we should accept this suggestion.
After careful consideration, I am of the
opinion that the National Government should adopt the
above three points as a basis for a sincere exchange of
views with the Japanese Government in an effort to restore
peace. The statement of the Japanese Government of
November 3 modifies the attitude as outlined in the
declaration of January 16. If the National Government
enters into peace talks on the basis of the foregoing
three points, then the door to peace parleys has been
opened. The object of China's war of resistance is to
secure the independence and existence of the nation.
The war has lasted over a year and China's sufferings have
been great. If China can end the war by an equitable
peace with her existence and independence assured, her
object will have been attained. The aforementioned
three points should form the basic principles of any peace
talk. Careful consideration, however, should be given
to the conditions attached to these three points: the
withdrawal of all the Japanese forces from China which
should be acceptable should be effected quickly and should
be made to cover all places. If permission were to be
given for the stationing of troops in specially designated
areas during the life of the so-called anti-Comintern pact,
such areas should be limited only to the vicinity of Inner
Mongolia; if done in any other way, it would affect the
integrity of China's sovereign and administrative rights.
After this China can devote her energy to reconstruction
as a modern nation. Careful study should be made to
ascertain the causes of rupture in districts bordering on
China and Japan and each party should be made aware of its
responsibilities. Hereafter, China should adopt friendly
relations, while Japan in particular should instruct her
people to abandon their traditional thoughts of aggression
on China and should adopt an attitude of friendship to
China in her educational policy. This will set up the
foundations of a permanent peace between the two countries.
All of us should strive hard for the welfare of the Orient
and should co-operate with other nations for the
establishment of a lasting peace and order on the Pacific
and in the world. I respectfully make this suggestion
for consideration and in the hope that it will be accepted.*

现在日本政府明确宣布，日本将尊重中国的主权和行政完整，日本无意独占中国的经济，也不希望要求中国限制任何第三国在华利益。她希望在平等原则基础上实现经济提携。因此，我们应该接受这一建议。

经过慎重考虑，我认为国民政府应以以上三点为基础，与日本政府真诚交换意见，以努力恢复和平。日本政府11月3日的声明修正了1月16日宣言中概述的态度。如果国民政府以前述三点为基础进行和平谈判，那么和平谈判的大门就已经打开。中国抗战的目的是确保国家的独立和生存。战争已持续一年多，中国遭受了巨大的苦难。如果中国能以公平的和平结束战争，并确保其生存和独立，那么她的目标就已达成。上述三点应构成任何和平谈判的基本原则。然而，应仔细考虑附属于这三点的条件：所有日军撤出中国这一可接受的条件应迅速实施，并应涵盖所有地区。如果在所谓的《反共产国际协定》有效期间允许在特别指定区域驻军，这些区域应仅限于内蒙古附近；若以其他方式处理，将会影响中国主权和行政权利的完整性。此后，中国可以致力于作为一个现代国家的重建。应仔细研究导致中日毗邻地区关系破裂的原因，并使各方意识到其责任。今后，中国应采取友好关系，而日本尤其应在其教育政策中指示其人民放弃传统的侵华思想，并对中国采取友好态度。这将为两国之间的永久和平奠定基础。我们都应为东方的福祉而努力，并与其他国家合作，在太平洋和世界范围内建立持久的和平与秩序。我谨提出此建议供考虑，并希望其被接受。*

Peace terms put forward for consideration by
Ambassadors of the National Government in
European and American countries.

Telegram dated 28-12-38.

Telegraphic despatches of a confidential nature have
just been received by the Kuomintang Government from Mr. Quo
Tai-chi, Dr. Wellington V.K. Koo and Dr. Hu Shih, Chinese
Ambassadors to the Court of St. James, France and the United
States of America respectively, giving their individual
opinions in regard to the terms for a basis for peace negotia-
tions. The essential points contained in these despatches
are as follows :-

1. Insistence on Chinese territorial integrity.

2. Manchuria, being the life line of another party, is not a
part of China Proper, and because of this reason, the
existing regime in Manchuria should be recognized.

3. The livelihood of the people will be rendered still more
precarious should the present state of affairs be allowed to
continue. Besides, the U.S.S.R. is only waiting an opportunity
to capitalize the present situation at the expense of others.
Chinese culture is by no means compatible with the application
of Communist doctrines, which in itself is feared even more by
the other party. It is rather to China's benefit that she
sever relations with that nation once and for all.

4. The Settlements and Concessions in China are nothing but abysses
of evil and they should be done away with without delay. This
is also the opinion of many enlightened foreigners. The
proposal of the other party in this regard should therefore be
accepted. Extraterritoriality should at the same time be
abrogated. The question of residence of the nationals of
the other party in China, can be solved when the legal and
political aspects of the case are satisfactorily cleared up.

5. The existence of the National Government should be insisted
upon since it is the supreme organ of the country recognized
by foreign nations.

驻欧美各国国民政府大使提出的供考虑的和平条款。

日期为38年12月28日的电报。

国民党政府刚刚收到中国驻圣詹姆斯宫朝廷（英国）、法国和美利坚合众国大使郭泰祺先生、顾维钧博士和胡适博士发来的机密性质电报，他们就作为和平谈判基础的条款各自发表了意见。这些电报中包含的要点如下：-

1. 坚持中国领土完整。

2. 满洲是另一方的生命线，不属于中国本部，基于此原因，应承认满洲现有的政权。

3. 如果允许目前的局势继续下去，人民的生计将更加岌岌可危。此外，苏联只是在等待机会，利用当前局势损人利己。中国文化绝不兼容共产主义教义的应用，而另一方甚至更害怕这一点。与中国彻底断绝与该国的关系反而对中国有利。

4. 中国的租界和租借地不过是罪恶的深渊，应立即予以废除。这也是许多开明外国人的意见。因此，应接受另一方在此方面的提议。同时应废除治外法权。另一方国民在华居住的问题，可以在令人满意地厘清案件的法律和政治方面后得到解决。

5. 应坚持国民政府的存在，因为它是外国承认的国家最高机构。

to capitalize the present situation at the expense of others.
Chinese culture is by no means compatible with the application
of Communist doctrines, which in itself is feared even more by
the other party. It is rather to China's benefit that she
sever relations with that nation once and for all.

4. The Settlements and Concessions in China are nothing but abysses
of evil and they should be done away with without delay. This
is also the opinion of many enlightened foreigners. The
proposal of the other party in this regard should therefore be
accepted. Extraterritoriality should at the same time be
abrogated. The question of residence of the nationals of
the other party in China, can be solved when the legal and
political aspects of the case are satisfactorily cleared up.

5. The existence of the National Government should be insisted
upon since it is the supreme organ of the country recognized
by foreign nations.

驻欧美各国国民政府大使提出的供考虑的和平条款。

日期为38年12月28日的电报。

国民党政府刚刚收到中国驻圣詹姆斯宫朝廷（英国）、法国和美利坚合众国大使郭泰祺先生、顾维钧博士和胡适博士发来的机密性质电报，他们就作为和平谈判基础的条款各自发表了意见。这些电报中包含的要点如下：-

1. 坚持中国领土完整。

2. 满洲是另一方的生命线，不属于中国本部，基于此原因，应承认满洲现有的政权。

3. 如果允许目前的局势继续下去，人民的生计将更加岌岌可危。此外，苏联只是在等待机会，利用当前局势损人利己。中国文化绝不兼容共产主义教义的应用，而另一方甚至更害怕这一点。与中国彻底断绝与该国的关系反而对中国有利。

4. 中国的租界和租借地不过是罪恶的深渊，应立即予以废除。这也是许多开明外国人的意见。因此，应接受另一方在此方面的提议。同时应废除治外法权。另一方国民在华居住的问题，可以在令人满意地厘清案件的法律和政治方面后得到解决。

5. 应坚持国民政府的存在，因为它是外国承认的国家最高机构。

WANG CHING-WEI'S TELEGRAM TO CENTRAL KUOMINTANG HEADQUARTERS
SUGGESTING OPENING OF PEACE NEGOTIATIONS WITH JAPAN (Hwa Mei
Chen Pao, Hongkong telegram, December 30)

Mr. Wang Ching-wei has sent the following telegram
to the Central Kuomintang Headquarters :-
In April this year, the National Congress issued a
manifesto explaining China's war of resistance as follows :-
" Since the Tangku Agreement, we have been
forbearing when dealing with Japan, our object being
to try by peaceful means to safeguard the provinces
in the North and to find a just solution of the question
of the Four North-Eastern Provinces. Politically,
our minimum desire is to preserve China's sovereign
rights and economy, we want mutual benefit and
equality."
Following the occurrence of the Lukuochiao Incident
in July, 1937, China was compelled to fight a war of
resistance. I have now read a statement issued by the
Japanese Government on December 22 dealing with fundamentals
for a readjustment of Sino-Japanese relations; it contains
the following three points :-
(1) GOOD NEIGHBOURS - Japan has no territorial
designs on China nor will she demand compensation for
military expenses. Japan not only will respect the
sovereign rights of China, but she will return her
Concessions to China and abolish extraterritoriality so
that China may obtain complete independence.
Since the Japanese Government has issued such a
statement, we shall be in a position to protect the
Northern provinces, recover all territories lost during
the operations and preserve China's sovereign rights and
administrative integrity by peaceful means. Thus, we
may find a reasonable solution of the problem of the Four
North-Eastern Provinces according to the manifesto issued
by the National Congress.
(2) JOINT ANTI-COMMUNISM - A few years ago,
Japan made such a suggestion on many occasions. We did not
accept it because we feared that our military and civil
affairs might be interfered with. Now the Japanese
Government has clearly stated that a Sino-Japanese Anti-
Communist Agreement should be signed in the spirit of the
Japan-Italo-German Anti-Communist Pact. The object of
guarding against Communists is to suppress plots for
disturbances by the Communists; it will have no adverse
effect upon the relations between China and Soviet Russia.
Since the members of the Chinese Communist Party have
expressed their willingness to fight for the Three
Principles of the People, they should give up their
organization and propaganda and abolish their army and
subject themselves completely to the law of China.
Anything that is done against the Three Principles of the
People, the supreme principle for the foundation of the
Republic of China, must be suppressed.
(3) ECONOMIC RAPPROCHEMENT - This point has
been repeatedly suggested by Japan to China during the

汪精卫致国民党中央总部建议与日本开启和平谈判的电报（《华美晨报》，香港电，12月30日）

汪精卫先生已向国民党中央总部发出如下电报：-
今年四月，全国代表大会发表宣言，阐述中国的抗战如下：-
“自《塘沽协定》以来，我们在对日交涉中一直采取克制态度，目的是试图通过和平手段保卫北方各省，并为东北四省问题寻求公正的解决方案。在政治上，我们最低的愿望是维护中国的主权和经济，我们要互利平等。”
继1937年7月发生卢沟桥事变后，中国被迫进行抗战。我现已阅悉日本政府于12月22日发表的关于调整中日关系基本原则的声明；该声明包含以下三点：-
(1) 善邻友好 - 日本对中国没有领土野心，也不会要求赔偿军费。日本不仅将尊重中国的主权，而且将把其租界归还中国，并废除治外法权，从而使中国获得完全独立。
既然日本政府发表了这样的声明，我们将有能力通过和平手段保护北方各省，收复作战期间失去的所有领土，并维护中国的主权和行政完整。因此，我们可以根据全国代表大会发表的宣言，为东北四省问题找到合理的解决方案。
(2) 共同防共 - 几年前，日本曾多次提出此类建议。我们未予接受，因为我们担心我们的军事和民政事务可能会受到干涉。现在日本政府已明确表示，应本着《日意德反共协定》的精神签署《中日反共协定》。防范共产党的目的是镇压共产党人的扰乱阴谋；这不会对中苏关系产生不利影响。鉴于中国共产党党员已表示愿意为三民主义而战，他们应当放弃其组织和宣传，解散其军队，并完全服从中国法律。任何违背作为中华民国建国最高原则的三民主义的行为，都必须予以镇压。
(3) 经济提携 - 这一点在过去几年中已被日本多次向中国提出。

pages.en:
- 2 -

past few years. Now the Japanese Government clearly
declares that Japan will respect China's sovereign rights
and her administrative integrity and that Japan has no
desire to have sole control of economics in China nor has
she a desire to request China to restrict the interests
of any third Power in China. She desires economic
rapprochement on the principles of equality. Therefore,
we should accept this suggestion.
After careful consideration, I am of the
opinion that the National Government should adopt the
above three points as a basis for a sincere exchange of
views with the Japanese Government in an effort to restore
peace. The statement of the Japanese Government of
November 3 modifies the attitude as outlined in the
declaration of January 16. If the National Government
enters into peace talks on the basis of the foregoing
three points, then the door to peace parleys has been
opened. The object of China's war of resistance is to
secure the independence and existence of the nation.
The war has lasted over a year and China's sufferings have
been great. If China can end the war by an equitable
peace with her existence and independence assured, her
object will have been attained. The aforementioned
three points should form the basic principles of any peace
talk. Careful consideration, however, should be given
to the conditions attached to these three points: the
withdrawal of all the Japanese forces from China which
should be acceptable should be effected quickly and should
be made to cover all places. If permission were to be
given for the stationing of troops in specially designated
areas during the life of the so-called anti-Comintern pact,
such areas should be limited only to the vicinity of Inner
Mongolia; if done in any other way, it would affect the
integrity of China's sovereign and administrative rights.
After this China can devote her energy to reconstruction
as a modern nation. Careful study should be made to
ascertain the causes of rupture in districts bordering on
China and Japan and each party should be made aware of its
responsibilities. Hereafter, China should adopt friendly
relations, while Japan in particular should instruct her
people to abandon their traditional thoughts of aggression
on China and should adopt an attitude of friendship to
China in her educational policy. This will set up the
foundations of a permanent peace between the two countries.
All of us should strive hard for the welfare of the Orient
and should co-operate with other nations for the
establishment of a lasting peace and order on the Pacific
and in the world. I respectfully make this suggestion
for consideration and in the hope that it will be accepted."
pages.zh:
- 2 -

现在日本政府明确宣布，日本将尊重中国的主权及其行政完整，日本无意独占中国的经济，也无意要求中国限制任何第三国在华利益。她希望在平等原则基础上实现经济提携。因此，我们应该接受这一建议。
经过慎重考虑，我认为国民政府应以以上三点为基础，与日本政府真诚交换意见，以努力恢复和平。日本政府11月3日的声明修正了1月16日宣言中概述的态度。如果国民政府以前述三点为基础进入和平谈判，那么和平会谈的大门就已经打开。中国抗战的目的是确保国家的独立和生存。战争已持续一年多，中国遭受了巨大的苦难。如果中国能以公平的和平结束战争，并确保其生存和独立，其目标就已达成。上述三点应构成任何和平谈判的基本原则。然而，应仔细考虑附属于这三点的条件：所有日军撤出中国，这一条是可以接受的，应迅速实施，并涵盖所有地区。如果在所谓的《反共产国际协定》有效期间允许在特别指定区域驻军，这些区域应仅限于内蒙古附近；如果以其他方式处理，将会影响中国主权和行政权利的完整性。此后，中国可以致力于作为一个现代国家的重建。应仔细研究导致中日边境地区关系破裂的原因，并使各方意识到其责任。今后，中国应采取友好关系，而日本尤其应在其教育政策中指示其人民放弃传统的侵华思想，并对中国采取友好态度。这将为两国之间的永久和平奠定基础。我们都应为东方的福祉而努力，并与其他国家合作，在太平洋和世界范围内建立持久的和平与秩序。我谨提出此建议供考虑，并希望其被接受。”

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    Misc. File No. 14/39.

REPORT    Louza Station,
Date Jan. 5th, 19 39.

Subject (in full) Distribution of Pro-Japanese pamphlets from an aeroplane.

Made by D.S.I. Black.    Forwarded by

Sir,

At 10 a.m. 5-1-39 an aeroplane flying over Louza District
distributed a large number of various coloured pamphlets.
These pamphlets on perusal were found to be pro-Japanese
and also lauded the action of Wong Ching Wei (汪精衛) in
connection with the Japanese.

According to eye-witnesses the aeroplane bore the
Japanese army distinguishing marks.

D.S.I.

Sen. Det. 1/C.

L.J.O. "A".

据目击者称，该飞机带有日本军队的识别标志。

At approximately 9.50 a.m. on the 5th January 1939,

relate to the statement of Mr. Wang Ching Wei re negotiations
for peace with Japan.

to establishing peace negotiations and save the

Chief Director Chiang, the General Executive, Central
Executive and Central Supervisory Committees of the
Kuomintang,

In the manifesto issued by the emergency

dealing with the reasons for the present war of
resistance and containing the following passage:

The reason why, after the conclusion of all
humiliation, to negotiate with Japan is because we
desired to avoid military action and carry out by
peaceful means the double task, to assure the security
of the northern provinces and then to bring about a
reasonable solution of the question of the four north-
eastern provinces.

Politically our minimum conditions include
the inviolability of our sovereign rights and main-
tenance of our administrative independence and

The third point is economic cooperation.

Likewise, this has repeatedly been proposed by
the Government of Japan during the past few years.
Hitherto we have taken the view that as long as the

The object of China's armed resistance is to secure
its national existence and independence.

In the course of the present war, which already
has lasted more than a year, great suffering has been
inflicted upon the country.

If we are able to re-establish peace in conformity
with justice, then the existence and independence of the
nation may be maintained and the aim of armed resistance
is reached.

These three points constitute the principles of
peace.

As to the terms of peace, we must take them into
careful consideration in order to assure their
appropriateness.

Of special importance is the point that the with-
drawal from China of the Japanese Army in its totality
must be prompt and universal in all directions.

Furthermore the so-called specified areas where
Japanese troops may be stationed for a period concurrent
with the contemplated anti-Comintern pact must be
restricted to the vicinity of Inner Mongolia only.

This affects China's sovereignty and administrative
independence and integrity and only by this restriction
will China be able to carry out the work of post-war
rehabilitation and reconstruction of a modern state.

In view of our proximity, good neighbourliness and
amicable relationship between China and Japan are but
natural and necessary.

中国武装抵抗的目的是确保其国家生存和独立。

在已经持续一年多的当前战争过程中，国家遭受了巨大的苦难。

如果我们能够按照正义重建和平，那么国家的生存和独立便可得以维持，武装抵抗的目标也就达到了。

这三点构成了和平的原则。

至于和平条款，我们必须仔细考虑，以确保其适当性。

特别重要的一点是，日本军队全部撤出中国必须是迅速且全面的。

此外，所谓允许日军驻扎的特定区域，其期限应与拟议的防共协定同期，且必须仅限于内蒙古附近地区。

这关系到中国的主权、行政独立和领土完整，只有加以此种限制，中国才能开展战后复兴和现代国家重建的工作。

鉴于我们地缘相近，中日之间的善邻友好关系是自然且必要的。

中国文明不适应共产主义，日本也视其为毒蛇猛兽。为了防止永久性的毁灭，最好放弃共产主义。
(4) 外国租界是一切罪恶的根源，甚至西方智识人士也主张废除它们。既然日本现在提出此点，我们应同意接受。顺便提及，治外法权也将予以废除。至于移民问题，可以起草措施使其符合我们的法律和政治原则。
(5) 国民政府的名称应予以保留，因为这涉及重要的国际关系问题。

WANG CHING-WEI'S TELEGRAM TO CENTRAL KUOMINTANG HEADQUARTERS
SUGGESTING OPENING OF PEACE NEGOTIATIONS WITH JAPAN (Hwa Mei
Chen Pao, Hongkong telegram, December 30)

Mr. Wang Ching-wei has sent the following telegram
to the Central Kuomintang Headquarters :-
In April this year, the National Congress issued a
manifesto explaining China's war of resistance as follows :-
" Since the Tangku Agreement, we have been
forbearing when dealing with Japan, our object being
to try by peaceful means to safeguard the provinces
in the North and to find a just solution of the question
of the Four North-Eastern Provinces. Politically,
our minimum desire is to preserve China's sovereign
rights and economy, we want mutual benefit and
equality."
Following the occurrence of the Lukouchiao Incident
in July, 1937, China was compelled to fight a war of
resistance. I have now read a statement issued by the
Japanese Government on December 22 dealing with fundamentals
for a readjustment of Sino-Japanese relations; it contains
the following three points :-
(1) GOOD NEIGHBOURS - Japan has no territorial
designs on China nor will she demand compensation for
military expenses. Japan not only will respect the
sovereign rights of China, but she will return her
Concessions to China and abolish extraterritoriality so
that China may obtain complete independence.
Since the Japanese Government has issued such a
statement, we shall be in a position to protect the
Northern provinces, recover all territories lost during
the operations and preserve China's sovereign rights and
administrative integrity by peaceful means. Thus, we
may find a reasonable solution of the problem of the Four
North-Eastern Provinces according to the manifesto issued
by the National Congress.
(2) JOINT ANTI-COMMUNISM - A few years ago,
Japan made such a suggestion on many occasions. We did not
accept it because we feared that our military and civil
affairs might be interfered with. Now the Japanese
Government has clearly stated that a Sino-Japanese Anti-
Communist Agreement should be signed in the spirit of the
Japan-Italo-German Anti-Communist Pact. The object of
guarding against Communists is to suppress plots for
disturbances by the Communists; it will have no adverse
effect upon the relations between China and Soviet Russia.
Since the members of the Chinese Communist Party have
expressed their willingness to fight for the Three
Principles of the People, they should give up their
organization and propaganda and abolish their army and
subject themselves completely to the law of China.
Anything that is done against the Three Principles of the
People, the supreme principle for the foundation of the
Republic of China, must be suppressed.
(3) ECONOMIC RAPPROCHEMENT - This point has
been repeatedly suggested by Japan to China during the

汪精卫致国民党中央总部建议开启对日和平谈判的电报（香港《华美晨报》电，12月30日）

汪精卫先生向国民党中央总部发出如下电报：-
今年四月，全国代表大会发表宣言，阐述中国的抗战如下：-
“自《塘沽协定》以来，我们对日一直采取忍让态度，目的是试图以和平手段保卫北方各省，并寻求东北四省问题的公正解决。在政治上，我们的最低愿望是保全中国的主权；在经济上，我们要互惠平等。”
继1937年7月卢沟桥事变发生后，中国被迫进行抗战。我现在阅读了日本政府12月22日发表的关于调整中日关系基本原则的声明；其中包含以下三点：-
(1) 善邻友好 - 日本对中国没有领土野心，也不会要求军事费用赔偿。日本不仅将尊重中国的主权，而且将把她的租界归还中国，并废除治外法权，使中国获得完全独立。
既然日本政府发表了这样的声明，我们将能够通过和平手段保护北方各省，收复作战期间失去的所有领土，并保全中国的主权和行政完整。从而，我们可以根据全国代表大会发表的宣言，为东北四省问题找到合理的解决方案。
(2) 共同防共 - 几年前，日本曾多次提出此类建议。我们当时未予接受，因为我们担心我们的军事和民政事务可能受到干涉。现在日本政府明确表示，应按照《日意德防共协定》的精神签署《中日防共协定》。防范共产党的目的是镇压共产党人的扰乱阴谋；这不会对中苏关系产生不利影响。鉴于中国共产党成员已表示愿意为三民主义而战，他们应放弃其组织和宣传，解散其军队，并完全服从中国法律。任何违背作为中华民国建国最高原则的三民主义的行为，都必须予以镇压。
(3) 经济提携 - 这一点在过去几年中已被日本多次向中国提出。现在

pages.en:
- 2 -

past few years. Now the Japanese Government clearly
declares that Japan will respect China's sovereign rights
and her administrative integrity and that Japan has no
desire to have sole control of economics in China nor has
she a desire to request China to restrict the interests
of any third Power in China. She desires economic
rapprochement on the principles of equality. Therefore,
we should accept this suggestion.
After careful consideration, I am of the
opinion that the National Government should adopt the
above three points as a basis for a sincere exchange of
views with the Japanese Government in an effort to restore
peace. The statement of the Japanese Government of
November 3 modifies the attitude as outlined in the
declaration of January 16. If the National Government
enters into peace talks on the basis of the foregoing
three points, then the door to peace parleys has been
opened. The object of China's war of resistance is to
secure the independence and existence of the nation.
The war has lasted over a year and China's sufferings have
been great. If China can end the war by an equitable
peace with her existence and independence assured, her
object will have been attained. The aforementioned
three points should form the basic principles of any peace
talk. Careful consideration, however, should be given
to the conditions attached to these three points: the
withdrawal of all the Japanese forces from China which
should be acceptable should be effected quickly and should
be made to cover all places. If permission were to be
given for the stationing of troops in specially designated
areas during the life of the so-called anti-Comintern pact,
such areas should be limited only to the vicinity of Inner
Mongolia; if done in any other way, it would affect the
integrity of China's sovereign and administrative rights.
After this China can devote her energy to reconstruction
as a modern nation. Careful study should be made to
ascertain the causes of rupture in districts bordering on
China and Japan and each party should be made aware of its
responsibilities. Hereafter, China should adopt friendly
relations, while Japan in particular should instruct her
people to abandon their traditional thoughts of aggression
on China and should adopt an attitude of friendship to
China in her educational policy. This will set up the
foundations of a permanent peace between the two countries.
All of us should strive hard for the welfare of the Orient
and should co-operate with other nations for the
establishment of a lasting peace and order on the Pacific
and in the world. I respectfully make this suggestion
for consideration and in the hope that it will be accepted."

- 2 -

日本政府明确宣布，日本将尊重中国的主权和行政完整，日本无意独占中国经济，也不要求中国限制任何第三国在华利益。她希望在平等原则基础上进行经济提携。因此，我们应该接受这一建议。
经过慎重考虑，我认为国民政府应以以上三点为基础，与日本政府真诚交换意见，努力恢复和平。日本政府11月3日的声明修改了1月16日宣言中概述的态度。如果国民政府以前述三点为基础进入和平谈判，那么和平对话的大门就已经打开。中国抗战的目的是确保国家的独立和生存。战争已持续一年多，中国遭受了巨大的苦难。如果中国能以公平的和平结束战争，并确保其生存和独立，其目标就已达成。上述三点应构成任何和平谈判的基本原则。然而，应仔细考虑附属于这三点的条件：所有日军撤出中国，这一条应被接受，且应迅速执行并涵盖所有地区。如果在所谓的《防共协定》有效期内允许在特定区域驻军，这些区域应仅限于内蒙古附近；若以其他方式处理，将影响中国主权和行政权利的完整。此后，中国可以致力于作为一个现代国家的重建。应仔细研究导致中日边境地区破裂的原因，并使各方意识到其责任。今后，中国应采取友好关系，而日本尤其应在其教育政策中指示其人民放弃传统的侵华思想，并对中国采取友好态度。这将为两国永久和平奠定基础。我们都应为东方的福祉而努力，并与其他国家合作，在太平洋和世界范围内建立持久的和平与秩序。我谨提出此建议供考虑，并希望其被接受。”

2. 满洲是另一方的生命线，不属于中国本部，因此，应承认满洲现有的政权。
3. 如果允许目前的局势继续下去，人民的生活将更加艰难。此外，苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟（苏联）只是在等待机会，利用当前局势损害中国以谋私利。中国文化与共产主义教义的施行绝不相容，而这一点也是另一方更为恐惧的。与中国断绝关系对中国反而有利。
4. 中国的租界和租借地不过是罪恶的渊薮，应立即予以废除。这也是许多开明外国人的意见。因此，应接受另一方在此方面的提议。同时应废除治外法权。至于另一方国民在中国居住的问题，可以在法律和政治局势得到满意澄清后解决。

应坚持国民政府的存在，因为它是被外国承认的国家最高机关。

REPORT
Date December 28, 1938.
Subject Departure of Mr. Waung Ching-wei (汪精衛) from Chungking.
Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

Referring to the report which appeared in the Eastern
Times of December 23, 1938, enquiries have been made amongst
friends and relatives of Mr. Waung Ching-wei in Shanghai as to
the real cause of his sudden departure from Chungking.
Mr. Zia Yau (謝耀), one of Mr. Waung's secretaries who is in
charge of his personal affairs in Shanghai, gave the following
account of the disagreement between Mr. Waung and other political
leaders in Chungking especially over the question of making
peace with Japan which would appear to have been the cause of
the departure of Mr. Waung from Szechuen. According to the
informant, Mr. Waung Ching-wei attended an important conference
in Chungking about 20 days ago when amongst other things discuss-
ed was the necessity of evacuating a portion of the population
of Chungking as a precaution against air raids. Mr. Waung, it
is alleged, hinted that in view of the sufferings of the people,
it might be possible to discuss peace terms with Japan. His
proposal was, it is reported, supported by General Ho Ying-ching,
Chang Chun and Dr. Wang Chung-hui, the present Minister of
Foreign Affairs, but was bitterly criticised by other Kuomintang
and Communist leaders. Mr. Waung left the conference much
discouraged and rumours were rife since then that extremists
of the Communist Party were contemplating an attempt upon his
life. The opposition against Mr. Waung grew stronger amongst
the radical elements when news reached Chungking of the foreign
loans granted by Britain and U.S.A. inflicting a severe blow on
the clique advocating peace. Mr. Waung Ching-wei became nervous
and confined himself to his house for several days. On Dec. 19
he suddenly left for Kwenming by aeroplane. Mr. Chen Kung Po
(陳公博), a trusted follower of Mr. Waung, was summoned by

鉴于1938年12月23日《字林西报》刊登的相关报道，已就汪精卫先生突然离开重庆的真正原因，向其在上海的亲友进行了查询。
汪先生的一位秘书谢耀（Zia Yau，音译）先生负责其在上海的个人事务，他就汪先生与重庆其他政治领袖之间的分歧提供了以下说明，尤其是关于与日本议和的问题，这似乎是汪先生离开四川的原因。据线人称，大约20天前，汪精卫先生在重庆参加了一次重要会议，会上除其他事项外，还讨论了为防备空袭而疏散部分重庆人口的必要性。据称，汪先生暗示，鉴于民众遭受的苦难，或许可以与日本讨论和平条款。据报道，他的提议得到了何应钦将军、张群和王宠惠博士（现任外交部长）的支持，但遭到了其他国民党和共产党领导人的严厉批评。汪先生怀着极大的沮丧离开了会议，此后谣言四起，称共产党极端分子正策划暗杀他。当英国和美国提供贷款的消息传到重庆，给主张和平的派系以沉重打击时，激进分子对汪先生的反对情绪愈发强烈。汪精卫先生变得神经紧张，将自己关在家中数日。12月19日，他突然乘飞机前往昆明。汪先生的亲信追随者陈公博先生被召至

Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek who upon being informed
of the departure was greatly shocked. Chen was instructed to
proceed to Hanoi to persuade Mr. Waung to return.

It would appear from the latest information at hand
that the efforts of Mr. Chen have not met with any success
and that he may accompany Mr. Waung to Hongkong and then go
abroad.

The secretary further stated that the split between
Mr. Waung and other political leaders in Chungking was due
to differences of opinion but that this would not affect the
war situation.

Mr. Waung has no followers amongst the military
leaders with the exception perhaps of General Chang Fa Kwei
who is in command of the forces in Kwangtung. It is, however,
not likely that Mr. Waung will start any kind of movement in
the South nor will he work for the Japanese as a puppet official.
As he is in poor health Mr. Waung will probably go abroad for
a rest.

It is alleged by certain followers of Generalissimo
Chiang Kai-shek that the Generalissimo has been much embarrassed
by the departure of Mr. Waung Ching-wei as at heart he is in
agreement with the latter for a cessation of hostilities provided
the peace terms are acceptable. At the same time, however, he
cannot ignore the strong opposition of the communists because
split amongst the Chinese forces would be inevitable if peace
negotiations are entered into with Japan at present. Therefore
Generalissimo Chiang has made a statement refuting all peace
talks whilst at the same time he is endeavouring to retain
Mr. Waung.

据蒋介石委员长的一些追随者称，汪精卫先生的出走令委员长十分尴尬，因为如果和平条件可以接受，他在内心是同意停止敌对行动的。但与此同时，他不能忽视共产党的强烈反对，因为如果此时与日本进行和平谈判，中国军队内部的分裂将不可避免。因此，蒋介石委员长发表声明驳斥所有和平言论，同时也在努力挽留汪先生。

Enquiries made in both Chinese and Japanese circles reveal that a peace movement is in progress behind the scenes under the leadership of Mr. Wang Ching Wei through his followers in Hongkong and Shanghai. Dr. Chu Ming Yi, formerly Chief Secretary of the Executive Yuan under Mr. Wang, is said to be in charge of the peace campaign in Shanghai. About a fortnight ago Dr. Chu was reported to have received a large sum of money for this purpose from Madame Wang (nee Miss Chen Pi Chiun(陳璧君)), a member of the Central Executive Committee of Kuomintang in Hongkong.

Dr. Chu had a secret conference with Mr. Tani, the former Japanese Ambassador-at-Large, last week at the latter's official residence on Route Pichon. It is claimed that during the conference Dr. Chu has informed the Japanese diplomat that Mr. Wang was working for the cause of peace by trying to frustrate with every possible means the co-operation between the Kuomintang and the Communist Party. Mr. Tani is said to have expressed his great satisfaction with the plan and to have promised that his government would assist Mr. Wang to establish a Fascist government in China with Mr. Wang as its leader.

Subject Mr. Wang Ching Wei Working for Peace in Shanghai.

Made by ____ and ____ Forwarded by Inspector Papp.

In spite of Mr. Wang Ching Wei's public opposition to Japan's aggression announced at Chungking on December 7, 1938, it is learned from fairly reliable sources that Mr. Wang and his group are continuing their endeavours to reach some understanding with Japan. Recently Mr. Wang sent one Mr. Ling Po Sheng (林柏生), a trusted subordinate and member of the Legislative Yuan to Shanghai with a view to making connections with local pro-Japanese political agents. It is learned to facilitate his activities a secret organ has been established at the old site of the Chung Hwa Daily News (中華日報), 303 Honan Road. Furthermore, Mr. Ling has bought over two news agencies for Mr. Wang at the price of $4,000.- They are the Hwa Tung News Agency (華東通訊社) and the Hsin Sheng News Agency (新聲通訊社), and they will be utilized for the dissemination of information making receptive the mind of the public for peace.

At the same time, Dr. Chu Ming Yi (褚民誼), formerly secretary-general of the Executive Yuan under Mr. Wang, has been working on the establishment of a new society which would propagate Mr. Wang's political views, advocating the necessity of reaching a peaceful settlement with Japan. Preparations for the founding of such a society had been made at the Sino-French Technical Institute (中法工学院) of which Dr. Chu is the president. It is now contemplated to establish the society, which will be called the "Tsin She" (社) or the "Nan Tsin Society" (南潯同鄉會), somewhere in the vicinity of Jinkee and Szechuen Roads.

                          Date November 23, 19 38.

Subject Activities of Peace Agents in Shanghai.

Made by/....................and....................Forwarded by Inspector Papp.

It is learned from a fairly reliable source
that in spite of the National Government's determination to
resist Japan until final victory was achieved and in spite of
General Chiang Kai Shek's declaration not to compromise with
Japan under any circumstances, attempts are still being made
secretly in support of a peace movement in Shanghai. It was
revealed that towards the end of October, 1938, one Mr. Peng
Hsueh Pei (彭學沛) until recently vice-Minister of Interior
and a leading member of the Re-organizationist Group, was
recently in Shanghai and conferred secretly with Dr. Chu Ming
Yi (褚民誼) who is said to be Mr. Wang Ching Wei's un-
official representative in Shanghai, concerning the steps to
be taken in realizing the plan for peace negotiations with
Japan. While in town, Mr. Peng used the offices of the Chung
Hwa Daily News (中華日報), 303 Honan Road, as his communication
address but stayed in a secret place. He had a secret
conference with Mr. Wen Tsung Yao, President of the Legislative
Yuan of the Reformed Government at Dr. Chu's residence at 1195
Rue Lafayette, where it was decided that the Reformed Government
will endeavour to obtain the co-operation of the Japanese
Government for a plan, which would make Mr. Wang the new leader
of the National Government in place of General Chiang, who
would be asked to resign in order to remove the obstacles of
peace. It was also decided to distribute large sums of money
with the purpose to buying over some leading Chinese newspapers
so as to create an atmosphere favourable to the peace movement.
After having completed these arrangements, Mr. Peng returned
to Chungking at the beginning of November travelling via Indo-
China.

                          日期 1938年11月23日。

主题：上海和平代理人的活动。

制作人/ ____ 和 ____ 由帕普（Papp）督察转呈。

据相当可靠的消息来源获悉，尽管国民政府决心抵抗日本直至取得最终胜利，且蒋介石将军声明在任何情况下均不与日本妥协，但在上海仍有人秘密尝试支持和平运动。据悉，1938年10月底，前内政部次长、改组派主要成员彭学沛先生近期在上海，并与据称是汪精卫先生在上海的非官方代表褚民谊博士秘密会晤，商讨实现与日本和平谈判计划的步骤。彭先生在沪期间，使用河南路303号《中华日报》社作为通讯地址，但居住在秘密地点。他在褚民谊位于拉斐特路1195号的寓所内，与维新政府立法院院长温宗尧先生举行了秘密会议，会上决定维新政府将努力争取日本政府合作实施一项计划，该计划旨在让汪先生取代蒋介石将军成为国民政府的新领袖，并将要求蒋辞职以消除和平障碍。会议还决定分发巨额资金，目的是收买一些主要的中文报纸，从而营造有利于和平运动的氛围。完成这些安排后，彭先生于11月初经印度支那返回重庆。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / B / 1938年11月23日 / 副本）

SECRET REPORT
S. D. 6, Special Branch Registry
No. S. R. 8 / Dxxxxx
Date November 8, 1938.

Subject Chinese Groups Seeking Peace.

Made by and Forwarded by Inspector P. P.

It is learned from a fairly well informed source
that the loss of Canton is part of the scheme of the
Political Science Group (政学系) and the Re-organization
Group (改组派). Both of these groups never supported
whole-heartedly the idea of armed resistance against Japan
and always advocated a policy of friendship and understanding
with Japan. Moreover, they have worked for peace with
Japan ever since the outbreak of the hostilities.

The Political Science Group is reported to be under
the leadership of General Chang Chun (张群), formerly
Foreign Minister and now Director of General Chiang's Military
Headquarters in Szechuen. The other government leaders in
this group are General Ho Ying Ching, Minister of War, Mr.
Ong Wen Hao, Minister of Economic Affairs, General Wu Teh
Chen, Chairman of the Kwangtung Provincial Government,
General Yu Han Mou, Pacification Commissioner of Kwangtung,
General Hsiung Hsi Hui, Chairman of the Kiangsi Provincial
Government, General Chen Yi, Chairman of the Fukien Provincial
Government, and many others.

The Re-organization Group is under the leadership of
Mr. Wang Ching Wei, who for the sake of political expediency,
joined hands with the other group.

The present defensive war of China opened the road
for other political groups, especially it enabled the
Communist Party to co-operate with the Kuomintang Government
and thereby dealt a heavy blow to the influence and stability
of the Political Science Group, whose policy is to co-
operate with Japan.

日期 1938年11月8日。

主题：寻求和平的中国团体。

制作人及转呈人 P. P. 督察。

据消息灵通人士透露，广州的失守是政学系和改组派阴谋的一部分。这两个团体从未全心全意支持武装抗日的主张，而是一直倡导与日本友好和理解的政策。此外，自战事爆发以来，他们一直致力于对日和平。

据报道，政学系由前外交部长、现任蒋介石将军四川军事总部主任张群将军领导。该系的其他政府领导人包括：军政部长何应钦将军、经济部长翁文皓先生、广东省政府主席吴铁城将军、广东绥靖主任余汉谋将军、江西省政府主席熊式辉将军、福建省政府主席陈仪将军等许多人。

改组派由汪精卫先生领导，他出于政治权宜之计，与另一派系联手。

中国目前的防御性战争为其他政治团体打开了道路，特别是使共产党得以与国民党政府合作，从而沉重打击了主张与日本合作的政学系的影响力和稳定性。

               October 3,    39.

Subject.... Mr. T.V. Soong to be Minister of Finance.

Made by.................... Forwarded by....................

Rumours have been prevalent during the past
two days especially among the banking circles that
Mr. T.V. Soong will be appointed Minister of Finance.
This has resulted in a slight advance in the value of the
Chinese dollar. Whilst no confirmation can be obtained
regarding this appointment in Shanghai, information has
been received from one of his former secretaries that
the mission of the ex-Minister of Finance to Chungking
is to discuss the situation in China as the result of the
European crisis.

It is alleged that Soviet Russia is advising
China through Mr. Sun Fo to cease hostilities against
Japan and to enter into negotiations for the conclusion
of a Five-Power Non-Aggression Pact (Germany, Russia, Italy
Japan and China). Mr. T.V. Soong is said to have opposed
the conclusion of peace with Japan which will interfere
with the independence of China and which will also impair
her relations with Great Britain and America.

It is reported that Dr. Wang Chung Hui, Minister
of Foreign Affairs, is in favour of effecting immediate
peace with Japan in order to frustrate the efforts of
Wang Ching Wei in forming a Central Government in
opposition to Chungking.

Certified true copy.
〔此处转录不清〕

过去两天，尤其是在银行界，流传着宋子文先生将被任命为财政部长的谣言。这导致法币价值略有上升。虽然在上海无法证实这一任命，但从他的一位前秘书处获悉，前财政部长此次前往重庆的任务，是讨论因欧洲危机而导致的中国局势。

据称，苏俄正通过孙科先生建议中国停止对日敌对行动，并就缔结五国互不侵犯条约（德国、俄国、意大利、日本和中国）进行谈判。据说宋子文先生反对与日本达成和平，认为这将干涉中国的独立，并损害中国与英国和美国的关系。

据报道，外交部长王宠惠博士赞成立即与日本实现和平，以挫败汪精卫组建反对重庆的中央政府的企图。

认证无误副本。

Subject Alleged reasons for the departure of T.V.Soong from Hongkong

Made by. Forwarded by.

Referring to the recent departure of
Mr. T.V.Soong for Chungking, there are many speculations
for the reason why this distinguished financier visited
the capital during the present European crisis.
Information has been received that
Mr. Soong has been called to the capital to participate
in an important conference regarding the policy which
the Government should adopt in the present European war.
It is alleged that Sun Fo who is now in Moscow, has
reported to Chungking that Soviet Russia will give all
her assistance to China on condition that China break
all relations with Britain, France and U.S.A. It is
said that T.V. Soong does not approve of Sun Fo's
suggestion and strongly advises the Government to
adhere to its original policy of maintaining friendly
relations with Britain, France and U.S.A. and continue
the resistance against Japan.

Subject. Mr. T.V. Soong rumoured as Minister of Finance.

Made by. and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 28 JULY 1939 MB）

According to information received from a close follower of Mr. T.V. Soong, it is not likely that Mr. Soong, who is still in Hongkong, will take up the post of Minister of Finance and serve under Dr. H.H. Kung, President of the Executive Yuan.

It may be correct that Mr. Soong has been offered this position, but the usual reply to the Government is that he would be more useful to give advice and assistance in his private capacity.

It will be remembered that Mr. T.V. Soong was during 1932/1933 Acting President of the Executive Yuan and that he resigned in favour of his brother-in-law Dr. H.H. Kung.

It is believed that Mr. Soong will proceed soon to the U.S.A. if the object of his mission (to secure loans) is approved by the Chungking Government.

宋先生可能确实收到了这一职位的邀请，但他对政府的通常答复是，他以私人身份提供建议和协助会更有益处。

需指出的是，宋子文先生在1932/1933年间曾任行政院代院长，随后辞职，由其妹夫孔祥熙博士继任。

据信，如果其使命目标（争取贷款）得到重庆政府批准，宋先生将很快前往美国。

**T. V. Soong Rumoured As Minister Of Finance**

Persistent But Unconfirmed Reports Indicate That Chairman Of Bank Of China Directorate May Assume Command Of China's Finances

Rumours have gained wide currency in local Chinese circles to the effect that the appointment of Mr. T. V. Soong, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Bank of China, to the post of Chinese Minister of Finance, was only a matter of time, it was reliably reported yesterday.

Mr. Soong was previously reported to have left Hongkong for London, allegedly on an important Chinese Government mission. It was then alleged that Mr. Soong had been instructed to cement closer contacts with London financial circles, to discuss measures for bringing economic pressure upon Japan, and to hold discussions on further measures for the stabilisation of China's national currency, and for the strengthening of China's international credit position.

However, latest reports to hand stated that Mr. Soong was still in Hongkong, but information emanating from circles close to him in Hongkong neither denied nor confirmed the reported Chinese Government economic mission to London.

Local Chinese circles were inclined to believe that if such an economic mission to London was contemplated, Mr. Soong was not likely to head it, it being generally felt that his presence in China is indispensable for purposes of consultations from time to time.

In fact, it was stated in these same circles, the appointment of Mr. Soong to the post of Finance Minister had been widely rumoured for months back. If the rumoured appointment should materialise, they stated, it would relieve Dr. H. H. Kung, the present Finance Minister, from heavy pressure of official duties, in view of the fact that Dr. Kung is holding the concurrent post of President of the Executive Yuan, a position equivalent to that of premier in foreign countries.

**Has Big Following**

More than anyone else in China, Mr. Soong commands a large following among Chinese and business financial circles in the country, and moreover, he also enjoys the great confidence of large sections of influential foreign circles both in China and abroad, these circles pointed out.

In view of the valuable experience and his other qualities, Mr. Soong has long been called a "financial wizard" in China. His appointment to the post of Finance Minister was regarded as not improbable in these same circles, especially, it was pointed out, when the present complicated financial problems in China demands close collaboration with responsible British and American financial circles and calls for astute statesmanship, these circles stated.

Official confirmation of the rumours of the impending appointment of Mr. Soong to the new post was still lacking in local Chinese circles, although reports to hand stated that Mr. Soong is scheduled to be appointed to an "important post," which appeared to have caused the present speculations, it was stated.

**盛传宋子文将出任财政部长**

持续但未经证实的消息表明，中国银行董事会主席可能执掌中国财政大权

据昨日可靠消息报道，当地华人圈子中广泛流传着一种说法，即中国银行董事会主席宋子文先生被任命为中国财政部长只是时间问题。

此前有报道称，宋子文先生已离开香港前往伦敦，据称是执行一项重要的中国政府使命。当时有说法称，宋子文先生奉命加强与伦敦金融界的紧密联系，讨论对日本施加经济压力的措施，并就进一步稳定中国法币及加强中国国际信用地位的措施进行讨论。

然而，最新收到的报告称，宋子文先生仍留在香港，但来自香港他身边圈子的信息既未否认也未确认有关其赴伦敦执行中国政府经济使命的报道。

当地华人圈子倾向于认为，如果确实计划派遣这样一个经济使团前往伦敦，宋子文先生不太可能担任团长，因为普遍感觉为了不时进行磋商，他必须留在中国。

事实上，这些圈子的人士指出，关于任命宋子文先生为财政部长的传闻已流传数月。他们表示，如果这一传闻中的任命成真，鉴于孔祥熙博士目前兼任行政院院长（相当于外国的总理职位），这将减轻现任财政部长孔祥熙博士繁重的公务压力。

**拥有众多追随者**

这些圈子的人士指出，在中国，宋子文先生比任何人都更能在国内华人和商业金融界赢得大量追随者，而且他还深受国内外广大有影响力的外籍人士圈子的极大信任。

鉴于其宝贵的经验和其他素质，宋子文先生在中国长期被称为“金融奇才”。这些圈子的人士表示，他的财政部任命被视为并非不可能，特别是当中国目前复杂的财政问题需要与负责的英美金融界密切合作并需要精明的政治家风范时。

尽管收到的报告称宋子文先生预定将被任命为一个“重要职位”，这似乎引起了目前的猜测，但在当地华人圈子中，仍缺乏关于宋子文先生即将出任新职的传闻的官方证实。

S. B, Special Branch.
REPORT
Date Jan. 19, 1939.

Subject Attempt on the life of Ling Pah-sun.

Made by/ and Forwarded by D. S. McKeown.

With reference to the attached translation of a telegraphic report on the attempted assassination of Ling Pah-sun (林柏生) at Hongkong on January 17, enquiries made by C.A. Loh Sih-kya amongst local Chinese journalists show that the cause is due to his activities in propagating Wang Ching-wei's peace movement. It was Ling Pah-sun who sent copies of Wang Ching-wei's peace movement telegrams to Chinese press for publication.

Prior to the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities, Ling Pah-sun used to be publisher of the "Chung Hwa Jih Pao" ("Central China Daily News" 中華日報), a Chinese language daily, with offices at No. 303 Honan Road. This paper suspended publication on November 29, 1937, after the withdrawal of Chinese forces from Shanghai. Afterwards, he went to Hongkong where he worked as managing-director of the "Nan Hwa Jih Pao" ("South China Daily News" 南華日報) in the interests of Wang Ching-wei.

Prior to Wang Ching-wei's peace movement, Ling Pah-sun was a member of the Legislative Yuan but was dismissed from this post soon after Wang Ching-wei's flight from Chungking to Hanoi.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 20. JAN. 1939）

关于附件中1月17日在香港发生的林柏生（林柏生）遇刺未遂事件的电报报告译文，经C.A. Loh Sih-kya向当地中国记者查询显示，起因是由于他宣传汪精卫的和平运动。正是林柏生将汪精卫和平运动的电报副本发送给中国报界刊登。

在中日敌对行动爆发之前，林柏生曾是中文日报《中华日报》（"Central China Daily News" 中華日報）的发行人，报社位于河南路303号。该报在中国军队撤离上海后，于1937年11月29日停刊。此后，他前往香港，在《南华日报》（"South China Daily News" 南華日報）担任总经理，为汪精卫的利益服务。

在汪精卫发起和平运动之前，林柏生是立法院成员，但在汪精卫从重庆逃往河内后不久，他被免去了这一职务。

Ta kei teo and other local newspapers (Hongkong telegram) :-

Attack on Wang's Follower in Hongkong

Ling Pah-sen (林柏生), managing
director of the "Nan Hwa Jih Pao" (南華日報) in Hongkong,
an official organ of wang Ching-wei, whilst walking on the
streets on January 17, was attacked by two Chinese, one
carrying an iron hook and the other a hammer. he was
seriously injured and is at present undergoing treatment
in hospital. One of the assailants was arrested on the
spot, but the other made good his escape.
It is said that the Hongkong Police are
paying much attention to this affair.

S. 1 Special Branch
September 28, 1940.

Recruiting of Special Service Agents in the Settlement

At noon on September 26, a Chinese aged about 30,
short and small build, and dressed in foreign style appear-
ed in the Doo Tsung Koh ( 薈春閣 ) Tea Shop, 462 Chekiang Road.
He claimed to come from a "Wang Ching-wei organ" on Yenping
Road, O.O.L. He intimated to the loafers then in the tea
shop that the "organ" was recruiting new members, and invited
those people to join the organization. He informed them that
new members would receive $40 a month and boarding and lodging,
but would not be allowed to leave the premises, whereupon
twenty-four of those loafers left the tea shop with their
informant.

It has also been learned that some 40 loafers were
recruited on September 27, from the vicinity of Canton, Pakhoi
and Swatow Roads.

According to the information received these people
will either be incorporated in a unit of the Peace & National
Salvation Army under one Ting Sih San ( 丁錫山 ) or employed
as special service agents.

Certified true copy.

J. F. Kennedy

1940年9月28日。

在租界内招募特种服务人员

9月26日中午，一名约30岁、身材矮小、穿着西式服装的中国男子
出现在浙江路462号的荟春阁（薈春閣）茶馆。
他声称来自欧战路（O.O.L.）延平路的一个“汪精卫机关”。
他向当时在茶馆里的闲散人员暗示，该“机关”正在招募新成员，并邀请这些人加入该组织。他告诉他们，新成员每月将获得40美元薪金及食宿，但不允许离开驻地，随后二十四名闲散人员随同该线人离开了茶馆。

另获悉，9月27日，约有40名闲散人员在广东路、北海路和汕头路附近被招募。

根据收到的信息，这些人要么被编入丁锡山（丁錫山）领导下的和平救国军的一个单位，要么被雇用为特种服务人员。

认证真实副本。

J. F. Kennedy

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.I., Special Branch.
REPORT
Date May 14, 1940.

Subject Reported Arrest of Two Bodyguards of Wang Ching Wei.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pin, Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.

With reference to the attached newspaper cutting dated May 11, 1940, regarding the arrest of two body-guards of Mr. Wang Ching Wei, extensive enquiries have been instituted and the following facts ascertained.

The two arrested officers are Meng Chi Wei (滿其蔚) and Dung Fah Nyoch (鄧伯玉), attached to Wang Ching Wei's bodyguards corps as vice-commander and secretary respectively. As they were not on good terms with their commander Hoong Tsung (洪振), Dung Fah Nyoch submitted a report to the Military Affairs Commission of the New Central Government accusing him of corrupt practice. Subsequently Yih Boong (葉蓬), a member of the Military Affairs Commission, instructed Loo Ying (盧英), Commissioner of the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau, to conduct confidential inquiries regarding the allegations. As a result of enquiries made by Loo Ying's representative in Nanking, Meng Chi Wei and Dung Fah Nyoch were placed under arrest on suspicion of being guilty of false accusation. They were flown to Shanghai on May 7, 1940, and after lengthy questioning by the detectives of the S.M.P.S.B., Meng Chi Wei was released on May 8 due to lack of evidence whilst Dung Fah Nyoch is still detained pending further enquiries.

The bodyguards corps in question is said to be originally formed by Loo Ying, Commissioner of S.C.G.P.B.

Pan Lien-pin
D. I.

主题：关于逮捕汪精卫两名保镖的报告。

由督察潘连彬（Pan Lien-pin）撰写，由督察克劳福德（Crawford）转呈。

鉴于附上的1940年5月11日报纸剪报，内容涉及逮捕汪精卫先生的两名保镖，已展开广泛调查，并查明以下事实。

被捕的两名官员是满其蔚（Meng Chi Wei）和邓伯玉（Dung Fah Nyoch），分别担任汪精卫保镖队的副指挥官和秘书。由于他们与指挥官洪振（Hoong Tsung）关系不和，邓伯玉向新中央政府军事委员会提交报告，指控其有腐败行为。随后，军事委员会委员叶蓬（Yih Boong）指示上海市政府警察局局长卢英（Loo Ying）就这些指控进行秘密调查。经卢英的代表在南京进行调查后，满其蔚和邓伯玉因涉嫌诬告罪被逮捕。他们于1940年5月7日被飞抵上海，经过上海公共租界工部局警务处特科侦探的长时间讯问后，满其蔚因证据不足于5月8日获释，而邓伯玉仍在拘留中，以待进一步调查。

据悉，该保镖队最初由上海市政府警察局局长卢英组建。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.

**Bodyguards of Mr. Wang**
**Arrested**

**Two Men Believed to Have**
**Chungking Connections**

On suspicion that they have been giving intelligence reports to the Chinese government at Chungking, two leaders of the bodyguards of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, head of the new régime at Nanking, have been arrested in Shanghai and are being questioned by the Chinese police of the Shanghai Special Municipality, Chinese reports state.

The arrested men are Meng Chi-wei, described as the vice-commander of Mr. Wang's bodyguards, and Teng Beh-yu, secretary of the bodyguards. They were placed under arrest by the Chinese police in Shanghai four days ago after they had alighted from a train arriving from Nanking.

The reports do not mention as to whether or not they were arrested at the request of Mr. Wang himself, but it is stated that the fate of the two arrested officers will depend on instructions from Mr. Wang. Just why they were arrested remains a mystery, but it is alleged that they may be affiliated with the military authorities in Chungking, doing intelligence or other work.

据中文报道，南京新政权首脑汪精卫先生的两名保镖头目在上海被捕，正由上海特别市中国警察讯问，嫌疑是他们一直向重庆的中国政府提供情报报告。

被捕者为孟其蔚（Meng Chi-wei），据称是汪先生保镖队的副指挥官，以及邓伯玉（Teng Beh-yu），保镖队秘书。四天前，他们在从南京抵达的火车上下车后，被上海中国警察逮捕。

报道未提及他们是否应汪先生本人的要求被捕，但称这两名被捕官员的命运将取决于汪先生的指示。他们为何被捕仍是个谜，但有指控称他们可能与重庆的军事当局有牵连，从事情报或其他工作。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.2 Special Branch. xxxxxx
REPORT
Date March 15, 1940.
Subject. Political significance seen in the arrival of Cheng Kung Po
in Shanghai.
Made by....................................................Forwarded by........................................

Information has been received from a reliable
source that Mr. Chen Kung Po (陳公博), ex-Minister of
Industry and a former adherent of Wang Ching Wei, has
arrived in Shanghai with his wife and is staying in the
house of Ho Ping Yi (何炳彝), former Director of the
Bureau of Foreign Trade, in the Rte Prelupt, French
Concession.

It will be remembered that although Chen Kung Po
deserted from the government service at Chungking simul-
taneously with Wang Ching Wei on December 19, 1938, yet
he hesitated to join the latter in the peace movement
and remained all the time in Hongkong awaiting develop-
ments. He did not make up his mind until recently when
seeing the likelihood of the success of Wang Ching Wei
in the formation of the new Central Government, he
accepted the invitation of the leader to come to Shanghai.

Chen Kung Po had a distinguished career in the
past with the Nationalist Government and his timely
arrival in Shanghai is considered important by most
of Wang Ching Wei's followers. It is alleged that
whilst in Hongkong, numerous attempts were made by
Chungking agents to win him over.

It is also reported that Wang Ching Wei has met
Chen Kung Po and as a result has decided to leave for
Nanking by the end of this month.

Chen is a native of Canton born in 1890 and
a returned student from the U.S.A.

J. F. Maxwell

日期：1940年3月15日。
主题：陈公博抵达上海所见之政治意义。
撰写人 ____ 转呈人 ____ 

从可靠消息来源获悉，前工业部长、汪精卫的前追随者陈公博（Chen Kung Po）先生已携夫人抵达上海，现居住在法租界蒲石路（Rte Prelupt）前对外贸易局局长何炳彝（Ho Ping Yi）家中。

需指出的是，虽然陈公博于1938年12月19日与汪精卫同时脱离重庆政府职务，但他犹豫是否加入汪的和平运动，并一直留在香港观望事态发展。直到最近，看到汪精卫组建新中央政府可能成功，他才下定决心，接受领袖邀请来到上海。

陈公博过去在国民政府中有着杰出的职业生涯，他及时抵达上海被大多数汪精卫追随者视为重要事件。据称，他在香港期间，重庆方面特工曾多次试图拉拢他。

另有报道称，汪精卫已会见陈公博，并因此决定于本月底前往南京。

陈系广东人，生于1890年，曾留学美国。

J. F. Maxwell

Date March 6 1940.
Subject Rumoured resignation of Wong Keh Min, Chief of the
Provisional Government in Peiping.
Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

The report which appeared in the China
Press and Chinese newspapers regarding the resignation
of Wong Keh Min cannot be confirmed. According to
information from pro-Japanese sources Wong Keh Min
has now agreed to the abolition of the Provisional
Government on condition that his administrative
rights in the North will not be affected through the
change to a Political Council after the successful
establishment of the Wang Ching Wei Government
in the South. The compromise made by Wong Keh Min
was the result of mediation by Yang Yu Sung (杨毓),
the son-in-law of the late Yuan Shih Kai who recently
flew to Peiping to negotiate on behalf of Wang Ching Wei.

Tan Shaoliang
Superintendent.

February 27, 1940.
Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Wan Pao of February 26 :-

SPLIT BETWEEN WANG CHING-WEI AND WANG KEH-MIN

According to information from reliable sources, the split between Wang Ching-wei and Wang Keh-min is growing acute. Although the situation has not yet developed into an open conflict, it is believed that this underhand struggle will become public one day, and it is probable that an order recently issued by Wang Keh-min for the arrest of an important member of Wang Ching-wei's clique named Li (李) may prove to be the fuse to a conflict between Wang Ching-wei and Wang Keh-min.

It is said that Wang Ching-wei has always maintained an attitude of dissatisfaction towards the Provisional Government in North China, but he can do nothing further due to the Japanese support at the back of Wang Keh-min. In the pact concluded between Wang Ching-wei and Japan, the Japanese have made every endeavour to bolster up Wang Keh-min's position in such a manner as to make the North China regime independent from restrictions by the future puppet regime. Of course, it is impossible for Wang Ching-wei to raise any objection, but he has already viewed the actions of Wang Keh-min in North China as the sole obstacle to his new regime. Superficially he maintains friendly relations with Wang Keh-min, but in his heart he will not be satisfied until he has succeeded in ousting Wang Keh-min.

It is reported that about three months ago Wang Ching-wei detailed the son of one of his close followers named Li to join the North China puppet regime, in which Li succeeded in securing an important post with the Finance Department. Wang Ching-wei handed over $200,000 to his man as expenses to facilitate him in obtaining an accurate account of the financial position of the North China puppet regime and also to conduct surreptitiously an anti-Wang Keh-min movement, thereby undermining Wang Keh-min's position in North China.

It is said that Li was quite successful in his underhand activities, but before long Wang Keh-min knew about the affair and issued an order for the arrest of Li. Fortunately for Li, he knew of his impending danger and succeeded in making good his escape to Shanghai.

This secret information is not disclosed by either Wang Ching-wei or Wang Keh-min, but it is recalled by certain quarters that the sudden return to Peiping of Wang Keh-min, who had flown to Shanghai to participate in the Shanghai Conference held by Wang Ching-wei, might be connected with this affair.

2月26日《大美晚报》：-

汪精卫与王克敏之间的分裂

据可靠消息来源，汪精卫与王克敏之间的分裂日益加剧。虽然局势尚未发展为公开冲突，但相信这种暗中斗争终有一天会公开化，而王克敏最近下令逮捕汪精卫派系中一名姓李的重要成员，这可能成为汪精卫与王克敏之间冲突的导火索。

据说，汪精卫一直对华北临时政府持不满态度，但由于王克敏背后有日本支持，他无能为力。在汪精卫与日本签订的协定中，日本人竭力巩固王克敏的地位，使华北政权独立于未来傀儡政权的限制之外。当然，汪精卫不可能提出任何异议，但他已将王克敏在华北的行动视为其新政权的唯一障碍。表面上他与王克敏保持友好关系，但在内心，他不将王克敏赶下台是不会满意的。

据报道，大约三个月前，汪精卫派遣其一名亲信之子李某加入华北傀儡政权，李成功在财政部谋得要职。汪精卫交给其手下20万元作为活动经费，以便其获取华北傀儡政权财政状况的准确账目，并秘密开展反王克敏运动，从而削弱王克敏在华北的地位。

据说李在暗中活动中相当成功，但不久王克敏得知此事，并下令逮捕李。幸运的是，李预知危险临近，成功逃往上海。

这一秘密情报并未由汪精卫或王克敏任何一方披露，但某些方面回忆起，王克敏此前飞往上海参加汪精卫举行的上海会议后突然返回北平，可能与此事有关。

Date December 9 1939.

Subject Alleged entry of pro-Wang Ching wei army into fokien.

Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

The alleged success attained by forces
under General Huang Ta Wei appears to be very doubtful
and cannot be confirmed. General Huang, who was
formerly a follower of the late Marshal Li Yuen Hung,
was in Shanghai about three months ago. He interviewed
certain ex-generals of Hupeh and was given passage to
go to Hongkong. How this General collected an army
strong enough to attack Fokien within a short period
seems to be a mystery and the places mentioned to have
been captured are located in the vicinity of Swatow
in Kwangtung Province, their fall to pro-Japanese
forces, even it is correct, will appear to have no
important bearing on the Fokien situation.

（批：C 9）

Tan Shaoliang
Superintendent.

Chen Kwong Chung, former Chief of the 1st
Department of the Police Bureau Headquarters (Wu Te Chen's
regime), who together with Chiang Oo Chong (蒋北坪),
was arrested in his office in the building of the Bank
of Canton, Kiangse Road, on 9-6-39 and who was released
on 1-7-39 after being examined by the Japanese Gendarmes
on a charge of being associated with Chinese guerillas,
is reported to have joined Wang Ching Wei's group and
become a member of the Committee of the Central Tangpu.

of the Soochow Creek, Chen signed an undertaking to sever
his connection with the Chungking Government and to devote
his services to the new regime.

In an anonymous letter received by the Municipal
Police on September 8, 1939, several members of the
Wang Ching Wei Clique are alleged to be engaged in
perpetrating assassinations.

The persons mentioned have joined the Wang Ching
Wei Clique and participated in the so-called "6th
National Congress of the Chinese Kuomintang" (國民黨
第六屆中央執委會) held on August 28, 1939, at No.31
Lane 1136 Yu Yuen Road. There is no information,
however, that they are concerned in assassinations.

Brief particulars of the persons mentioned in
the anonymous letter are given hereunder :-

(1) a. Wang Hsiang Kuo (黃青谷)

Born at Sungkiang, Kiangsu, about 1904.
Committee member of the French Concession
Branch of the local Kuomintang and of the
Shanghai 2nd Special District Citizens'
Federation, between 1928 and 1937. was chief
of the Propaganda Department of the local
Kuomintang headquarters from 1931 to the end
of 1937, and participated in the activities of
national salvation bodies between 1936 and 1937.

Recently joined the Wang Ching Wei Clique.
Will be made Chief of the Organization
Department of a local Kuomintang headquarters
to be established in the Western District,
I.O.L., by the Wang Ching Wei Clique.

在1939年9月8日市政警察收到的一封匿名信中，指控汪精卫派系的几名成员从事暗杀活动。

提及的人员已加入汪精卫派系，并参加了1939年8月28日在愚园路1136弄31号举行的所谓“中国国民党第六次全国代表大会”（國民黨第六屆中央執委會）。然而，没有任何情报表明他们参与暗杀活动。

现将匿名信中提及人员的简要情况列述如下：-

(1) a. 黄青谷（Wang Hsiang Kuo）

约1904年生于江苏松江。
1928年至1937年间，任当地国民党法租界区支部委员及上海第二特区市民联合会委员。1931年至1937年底，任当地国民党总部宣传科科长，并于1936年至1937年间参与救国会体的活动。

最近加入汪精卫派系。
将被任命为由汪精卫派系在西区（I.O.L.）建立的当地国民党总部的组织科科长。

Subject. Persons serving on the Committee of the local Tangpu
(WANG CHING WEI's Organization)
Made by. ____ and Forwarded by. Supt. Tan Shao-liang

Through information given by several
ex-Kuomintang members to the Japanese Authorities,
a number of successful raids have been carried out
in the French Concession during the past two months.
This has resulted in a majority of the Kuomintang
members surrendering themselves to the WANG CHING
WEI's Clique at 76 Jessfield Road. During the
convention of the so-called 6th People Congress
one of the resolutions passed recently was to form
a local Kuomintang Headquarters in order to cope
with the situation. The following persons mostly
ex-members of local Tangpu are reported to have
been elected to serve on the Standing Committee :-

Name Antecedents
1. HUANG HSIANG KOH Ex-Chief of Propaganda
(黄香右) Department of local Tangpu;
Committee member of the
French Concession Ratepayers'
Association. Summoned to
Shanghai First Special
District Court on 6-3-34 and
released on $300 security in
the case of attempting to
blackmail CHI FU DOO.
Follower of TU YUEH SUNG,
leader of 2nd Special
District Citizens Federation.

2. CHANG KUH CHONG Clerk in Chinese Post Office;
(张克昌) member of Postal Workers'
Union; Figuring in strike of
postal workers 22-5-32.
Member of Shanghai Labourers

of CHU HSUEH VAN.

pages.en:
REPORT

Dissension amongst pro-Japanese elements.

It is reported that Mr. Alfred Sze Sao Ke,
former Chinese Minister to the U.S.A., was elected
a member of the Central Executive Committee at the
recent 6th Kuomintang Congress held at 76 Jessfield Road.
Mr. Sze is very active in endeavouring to secure the
position of Foreign Minister to the new Central Govern-
ment and as he is supported by Mr. Wang Ching Wei, it
is expected he will succeed.

It is also reported that Dr. Ho Shih Cheng,
former President of the Shanghai Special District Court,
and his men have failed to put in their appearance at
the conference as promised. This has incurred the
displeasure and hatred of Mr. Wang Ching Wei who has
reported the matter to the Japanese authorities.
Independent parties are endeavouring to mediate and
bring about a peaceful settlement between the two
leaders.

It is also reported that Chen Chung Fu,
the leader of the Sin Tung Meng Group, to which Ho Shih
Cheng is the prominent adherent, has arrived in Shanghai.
General Hsu Chung Chi (        ) is the
Hongkong representative of this party.

Information has just been received to the
effect that about 40 persons in two vans, said to be
followers of Li Chih Chuen of 76 Jessfield Road, made
a raid on the Chih Tse University, 359 Connaught Road,
at 7 a.m. September 13 and forcibly removed one cabinet
and drawers of a desk containing certain documents.
Ho Shih Cheng is the principal of this school.

True Certified Copy.

报告

亲日分子内部的分歧。

据报道，前驻美中国公使施肇基 ( Alfred Sze Sao Ke ) 先生在近期于极司菲尔路76号举行的第六届国民党代表大会上当选为中央执行委员会委员。施先生正积极活动，力求在新中央政府中获得外交部长的职位，鉴于他得到汪精卫先生的支持，预计他将成功。

另据报道，前上海特区地方法院院长何世桢 ( Dr. Ho Shih Cheng ) 博士及其手下未按承诺出席会议。此举招致了汪精卫先生的不满和憎恨，汪已将此事报告给日本当局。独立各方正努力调解，促使两位领导人之间达成和平解决。

还据报道，何世桢的主要依附者所属的新同盟集团领袖陈中孚 ( Chen Chung Fu ) 已抵达上海。徐重芝将军 ( General Hsu Chung Chi ) (        ) 是该党的香港代表。

刚收到消息，称9月13日上午7时，约40人分乘两辆货车，据称为极司菲尔路76号李之泉 ( Li Chih Chuen ) 的追随者，突袭了康纳脱路359号的志士大学，强行搬走一个文件柜及装有某些文件的办公桌抽屉。何世桢是该校校长。

真实核证副本。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No. ......
S.2 Special Branch XXXXXX,
REPORT
Date September 11, 1939.
Subject Attempt on life of Li Chi Chuen (李自全), 76 Jessfield Road,
on September 9, 1939.
Made by ...... and ...... Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

Enquiries confirm that on the morning
of September 9, five persons called at 76 Jessfield
Road and producing a name card with introduction,
demanded to see Li Chi Chuen. Three were permitted
to enter and shown to the waiting room, the two others
remained outside. Li who had seen these persons from
the verandah upstairs became suspicious and ordered
a search to be made of the persons who had entered.
This resulted in an automatic pistol and a revolver
being seized and the men arrested. The couple who had
waited outside made good their escape.

What has become of the captives, it
has not been able to ascertain, although it is rumoured
that they were roughly handled and put to death in
the compound of the building.

经查询证实，9月9日上午，五人前往极司菲尔路76号，出示带有引荐的名片，要求见李自全。其中三人被允许进入并带至等候室，另外两人留在外面。李在楼上阳台看到这些人后心生怀疑，命令对进入的人进行搜身。结果搜出一支自动手枪和一支左轮手枪，这些人随即被捕。在外面等候的那两人成功逃脱。

至于被捕者的下落，目前尚无法查明，尽管有谣言称他们在该建筑的大院内遭到粗暴对待并被处决。

Date September 8, 1939.
Subject Detention in Chungking of General HO CHIEN
Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao-liang

Further to report dated May 24, 1939 re
the activities of one Dr. LIU HWA JUI (劉華瑞)
alias LIU WEI KIU (劉穗九) in Shanghai as a
delegate of General HO CHIEN (何健), until
recently the Chairman of the Hunan Provincial
Assembly, information has been received from a
reliable source that General HO CHIEN has been
placed under arrest and is being detained in the
military prison to be court-martialled. General HO,
it will be remembered, displayed indifference during
the hostilities prior to the fall of the Wuhan
cities and in consequence he was transferred to
Chungking and replaced by General CHANG CHI CHUNG
(張治中), the present Governor.

It is presumed that Dr. LIU's association
with the Japanese in Shanghai has been made known
to the Chungking Government through their agents
here and that as a precaution against his possible
flight from the Chinese Capital to join WANG CHING
WEI, the order for his arrest was issued.

Tan Shaoliang
Superintendent

继1939年5月24日关于刘华瑞博士（别名刘穗九）作为何健将军代表在上海活动的报告之后，何健将军曾任湖南省议会主席，直至最近。现从可靠来源获悉，何健将军已被逮捕，并被关押在军事监狱中，将面临军法审判。众所周知，何将军在武汉三镇沦陷前的敌对行动中表现冷漠，因此被调往重庆，由现任省长张治中将军接替其职务。

据推测，刘博士在上海与日本人的勾结已通过我方特工告知重庆政府，且为防止其可能逃离中国首都去投奔汪精卫，故下达了逮捕令。

Date August 19 1939.

Subject    Reported detention at Peiping of Wang Ke Ming by Japanese and
           his resignation as Chairman of Provisional Government.

Made by.        and        Forwarded by. Supt. Tan Shao Liang

No information is available in Shanghai
regarding the dissension alleged to have broken out
between General Sugiyama, Commander-in-Chief of the
Japanese Expeditionary Forces in North China and Wang
Ke Ming, Chairman of the Provisional Government
which resulted in the latter being detained and forced
to send in his resignation.

Observers do not think it likely that
Wang Ke Ming would oppose General Sugiyama in any
anti-British movements in North China and go so far
as to sacrifice his profitable position.

It will be remembered that Wang Ke Ming used
to be a good friend of Mr. T.V.Soong who recommended
his reinstatement into Government service and appoint-
ment to the Peiping Military Council in 1933. Wang
surrendered to the Japanese at the outbreak of
hostilities.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.2 Special Branch
REPORT
Date August 10 19 39.
Subject Arrival in Shanghai of Messrs. Tang Leang Li and Sung Li Ping.
Made by. and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

Tang Leang Li (湯良禮), a Hakka Cantonese born in Java, editor of the People's Tribune, is reported to have arrived in Shanghai from Hongkong and is at present staying at 76 Jessfield Road. He is assisting in the peace propaganda movement of Wang Ching-wei, of whom he is a close follower. He is a returned student from England and possesses a comprehensive knowledge of the English language but does not read Chinese.

Col. Sung Li Ping (孫履平 ), B.Sc., whose arrival in Shanghai was reported on October 28, 1938, has been seen in Shanghai recently. According to his close friends he left Shanghai for Hongkong about six months ago and only returned here recently. He is apparently living on a subsidy from Chungking to collect matter of political intelligence. In this connection he is reported to have been going round the town interviewing foreigners and Chinese including Capt. Millar, British General Staff Officer, and Lieut. G. Bouvet of the French Defence Force. He is also reported, since his second visit, to have associated with followers of Wang Ching Wei because it was Wang who took him into the diplomatic service in 1932 when he (Wang) was Minister of Foreign Affairs. Sung is reported to be staying with his father at Passage 927, House 46, Avenue Joffre.

D.C. (Special Branch)
Superintendent.

据报，客籍广东人、生于爪哇、《人民论坛》编辑唐良礼已从香港抵达上海，目前住在极司菲尔路76号。他正在协助汪精卫的和平宣传运动，他是汪的亲密追随者。他是留英归国学生，精通英语，但不识中文。

孙履平上校，理学学士，其抵达上海一事曾于1938年10月28日报导，最近有人在上海见到他。据其密友称，他约六个月前离开上海前往香港，直至最近才返回此地。他显然依靠重庆方面的津贴生活，以收集政治情报。为此，据报他在城内四处走访，采访外国人和中国人，包括英国总参谋部军官米勒上尉和法国防卫部队G. Bouvet中尉。另据报，自第二次来访以来，他一直与汪精卫的追随者交往，因为汪在1932年担任外交部长时曾将他引入外交界。据报孙与其父住在霞飞路1136弄927号46室。

D.C. (特别处)
警司。

Ta Mei Wan Pao dated July 10:

WANG CHING-WEI WILL FORM "CENTRAL GOVERNMENT"
ON FOUR CONDITIONS

According to information from foreign sources,
the rebel Wang Ching-wei is said to have decided to leave
Shanghai for Tsingtao where he will preside over the
so-called 5th conference of the "Joint Committee".
It is said that during his sojourn in Japan,
Wang Ching-wei proposed to organize a new "Central
Government" and that he has also made the following four
requests to the Tokyo authorities:-
1) That after the inauguration of the new government,
the Provisional Government and the "Reformed
Government" be cancelled.
2) That the new government join the "Anti-Comintern Pact"
with the three Powers.
3) That an agreement regarding co-operation in economics
and culture between Japan and the proposed government
be made after its inauguration.
4) That after the inauguration of the proposed new
government, Japanese troops should withdraw except from
the front and from important towns. Their place
should be taken by the 24th Division of the "New Army."

It is learned that important members of the
puppet Nanking and Peiping governments are strongly
opposing Wang in his proposal for the organization of a
"Central Government."
It is also learned that at 9.10 p.m. yesterday
Wang gave a speech at the Greater Shanghai Radio
Broadcasting Station, which was of an anti-Chiang Kai-shek
and anti-Communist nature. It was first spoken in
Mandarin and later in Cantonese and lasted about 50
minutes.
