《大美晚报》7月10日讯：

汪精卫将在四个条件下组建“中央政府”

据外电消息，叛国者汪精卫已决定离开上海前往青岛，主持所谓的“联合委员会”第五次会议。据悉，汪精卫在日本逗留期间，提议组建一个新的“中央政府”，并向东京当局提出了以下四项要求：-
1) 新政府成立后，取消临时政府和“维新政府”。
2) 新政府与三国加入“反共产国际协定”。
3) 新政府成立后，日本与拟议中的政府就经济和文化合作达成协议。
4) 拟议的新政府成立后，除前线及重要城镇外，日军应撤出。其防务由“新军”第24师接替。

获悉，伪南京和北平政府的重要成员强烈反对汪精卫组建“中央政府”的提议。
又悉，昨晚9时10分，汪精卫在大上海广播电台发表演讲，内容具有反蒋介石和反共性质。演讲先以国语进行，后以粤语进行，持续约50分钟。

pages.en:
Journal de Shanghai. July 20, 1937

DIFFERENCES OF VIEWS IN PARTY CAMPS.

On July 10 Wang Ching Wei broadcasted an address in the course of which he announced his decision to co-operate with the Japanese in "establishing a durable peace in China and in East Asia."

The whole world knows that the Japanese desire to make Wang Ching Wei as President of the "New Central Government of China" which they are planning to establish at Nanking. At first the Japanese thought that it would be dangerous for them to establish a central government for they are well acquainted with the saying: divide et impera. They therefore resolved to create four or five governments in China and up to the present governments have already been formed at Peiping and Nanking and others will be formed at Hankow, Canton and elsewhere.

Unfortunately for the Japanese, the plan has not given any practical results. In North China, Wang Keh Min rules over a number of towns and villages with the aid of bayonets, but his authority does not extend into the interior. Many sub-prefectures and even magistracies are still being administered by nominees of the Chungking Government. As for Liang Hung Chih, the chief of the "Reformed Government" at Nanking, his authority is less than that of Wang Keh Min.

For a time, the Japanese thought of ameliorating the situation by placing Marshal Wu Pei Fu at the head of an army to fight Chiang Kai Shek, in the belief that this would give rise to defections among the ranks of the nationalists, but the Marshal declined the post for he clearly foresaw that such an army placed under his command would have no military value; furthermore, he had his great reputation to preserve.

This military "solution" having failed, the Bureau of China Affairs and the Japanese military leaders decided upon a "political" solution by utilizing Wang Ching Wei, the ex-President of the Executive Yuan of the Chungking Government, for they believed that Wang Ching Wei still retained sufficient influence and prestige to draw the Chinese people after him.

Now this plan is already facing many difficulties. The principal Chinese leaders who have adopted a pro-Japanese policy recently met to examine the plan of establishing a Wang Ching-wei Government at Nanking. From the very beginning, Wang Keh-min, the President of the Provisional Government at Peiping, had opposed the new system for he preferred to be his own chief and if he is to receive instructions or directions, he considered that those coming from the Japanese would be enough. He is too clever to reject the Japanese plan in its entirety; he has made it known that he will adhere to that part of Wang Ching-wei's declaration relating to peace and co-operation with Japan, but that he is not in accord with Wang Ching-wei's political programme.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1937年7月20日

党派阵营中的观点分歧。

7月10日，汪精卫发表广播讲话，宣布决定与日本人合作，“在中国和东亚建立持久和平”。

举世皆知，日本人希望让汪精卫担任他们计划在南京建立的“中国新中央政府”的主席。起初，日本人认为建立中央政府对他们来说是危险的，因为他们深知“分而治之”的道理。因此，他们决定在中国建立四五个政府，截至目前，北平和南京已经成立了政府，汉口、广州等地也将成立其他政府。

不幸的是，对日本人而言，该计划并未产生任何实际结果。在华北，王克敏在刺刀的帮助下统治着一些城镇和村庄，但他的权威并未延伸至内地。许多县甚至行政公署仍由重庆政府的任命人员管理。至于南京“维新政府”首脑梁鸿志，其权威不及王克敏。

有一段时间，日本人曾考虑通过让吴佩孚元帅统领一支军队来对抗蒋介石，以此改善局势，相信这会在国民党队伍中引发倒戈，但吴元帅拒绝了这一职位，因为他清楚地预见到，置于他指挥下的这样一支军队将毫无军事价值；此外，他还要保全自己的盛名。

这种军事“解决方案”失败后，对华事务局和日本军方领导人决定利用重庆政府前行政院院长汪精卫，采取一种“政治”解决方案，因为他们认为汪精卫仍保留着足够的影响力和威望，能够吸引中国人民追随他。

现在，这一计划正面临许多困难。近期采取亲日政策的中国主要领导人开会审议在南京建立汪精卫政府的计划。从一开始，北平临时政府主席王克敏就反对新体制，因为他更愿意自己做主，如果必须接受指令或指示，他认为来自日本人的就够了。他非常精明，没有完全拒绝日本的计划；他表示将坚持汪精卫宣言中关于与日本和平与合作的部分，但他不同意汪精卫的政治纲领。

On the other hand, Wang Ching-wei has just
secured the complete adherence of Liang Hung-chih who
is ready to receive Wang Ching-wei at Nanking as his

另一方面，汪精卫刚刚获得了梁鸿志的完全拥护，梁鸿志准备在南京迎接汪精卫作为他的领袖。梁鸿志准备向汪精卫宣誓效忠，以至于他在过度热情之下——幸好只是口头上的——开始了一场针对外国租界的运动。在此过程中，他显然忽略了他在这些“绿洲”中所获得的巨大个人利益，在这些地方，每个人都能在中国动荡的风暴中安居乐业。

July 20, 1939.
Afternoon Translation.

To Ying Yeh Pao dated July 19:

OPPOSITION TO WANG CHING-WEI'S APPOINTMENT & FORMATION
OF ARMED BODYGUARDS BY POLICE COMMISSIONER

After he had arrived at Shanghai recently, Wang
Ching-wei went to stay in the Broadway Mansions and
appointed Loo Ying (陸英), Commissioner of the Shanghai
City Government Police Bureau, to form a corps of several
hundred armed bodyguards to be chosen from among puppet
policemen.

Upon receipt of this appointment, Loo Ying made
Yeh Tsai-chang (葉再昌) chief of the corps, with Mou Chi-wei
(穆其偉) as deputy chief, Kuo Shao-yi (郭紹儀) as chief
staff officer, Shao Chia-jen (邵介人) as chief secretary,
Chen Kwang-yi (陳光義) as chief intelligence officer and
Yang Hai-vai (楊海帆) as quarter-master.

However, Wong Keh-min (王克敏) and Kita of the
Peiping Provisional Government are opposed to the appointment
of Wang Ching-wei as chief of a puppet government and have
issued a circular telegram announcing their unwillingness
to co-operate with him.

On receiving news of this opposition, Wang Ching-
wei became angered.

Loo Ying has advanced no less than $10,000 for
the formation of the corps of armed bodyguards for Wang
Ching-wei; he did so because he desired to seize the post
of Mayor of Shanghai after Wang had become the head of a
puppet government. Loo Ying has also felt the effect
of Wong Keh-min and Kita's disaffection.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 21 JULY 1939）

1939年7月20日。
下午译文。

致7月19日的《英业报》：

反对任命汪精卫及警察局长组建武装保镖队

汪精卫最近抵达上海后，住进百老汇大厦，并任命上海市政府警察局督察长陆英（Loo Ying，陸英）组建一支由数百名武装保镖组成的队伍，人选从伪警察中挑选。

接到这项任命后，陆英任命叶再昌（Yeh Tsai-chang，葉再昌）为队长，穆其伟（Mou Chi-wei，穆其偉）为副队长，郭绍仪（Kuo Shao-yi，郭紹儀）为参谋长，邵介人（Shao Chia-jen，邵介人）为秘书长，陈光义（Chen Kwang-yi，陳光義）为情报处长，杨海帆（Yang Hai-vai，楊海帆）为军需官。

然而，北平临时政府的王克敏（Wong Keh-min，王克敏）和喜多（Kita）反对任命汪精卫为伪政府首脑，并发布通电宣布不愿与他合作。

得知这一反对消息后，汪精卫大怒。

陆英为汪精卫组建武装保镖队垫付了不少于10,000元；他这样做是因为他希望汪精卫成为伪政府首脑后，自己能攫取上海市市长的职位。陆英也感受到了王克敏和喜多不满情绪的影响。

（印：上海公共租界工部局处长办公室 1939年7月21日）

It is true that Chow Fu Hai(周佛海), formerly attached to the Propaganda Department of the Chungking Central Kuomintang Headquarters and principal adherent of Waung Ching-wei, has arrived in Shanghai since April, 1939 and is actively carrying on propaganda on peace talks, his principal object being to buy over Chinese newspapers or writers. He seems to have plenty of money, most probably subsidies from the Japanese but it is difficult to confirm that he draws money from the gambling houses in the Western District.

The General Liu referred to is really General Yi Poong(葉蓬), former Defense Commissioner of Hupeh. He is a native of Huang Pee(黃陂), Hupeh, age about 40. He came to Shanghai with his family about three months ago staying in a large foreign style building at 18 Route Pere Robert. He runs a transportation company called the Lichwang & Co. at No.30 Tsing Yuan Li, Peking Road. It is suspected that he is in the pay of the Japanese quite handsomely and utilising the company which has branches in Hongkong, Haiphong, Kunming, Chungking, etc. has been undertaking espionage service for the latter. He is managing director of the above company with Li Lien Fang(李聯芳) as manager and Chu Ting(朱定), a Cantonese, as assistant manager.

Li Lien Fang is also known as Li Fang(李芳), ex-Consul-General at Novo-Sibirsk. He is also a native of Hupeh, speaks English, French and Russian. At one time he was attached to the Foreign Office of Chungking

（右上角印章及手写内容：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE. S.2 REGISTRY File No. S. B. 1).）

确实，原属重庆国民党中央总部宣传部、汪精卫的主要追随者周佛海（Chow Fu Hai，周佛海）自1939年4月以来已抵达上海，并积极进行和平谈判的宣传，其主要目的是收买中文报纸或作家。他似乎资金充裕，很可能是来自日本的津贴，但很难证实他从西区的赌馆中抽取资金。

文中提到的刘将军实际上是叶蓬将军（General Yi Poong，葉蓬），前湖北防卫专员。他是湖北黄陂（Huang Pee，黃陂）人，年龄约40岁。大约三个月前，他携家眷来到上海，住在罗伯特神父路18号的一栋大型西式建筑里。他在北京路庆元里30号经营一家名为“利旺公司”（Lichwang & Co.）的运输公司。有人怀疑他受雇于日本人，报酬丰厚，并利用这家在香港、海防、昆明、重庆等地设有分支机构的公司为日本人从事间谍活动。他是上述公司的董事总经理，李联芳（Li Lien Fang，李聯芳）任经理，广东人朱定（Chu Ting，朱定）任副经理。

李联芳又名李芳（Li Fang，李芳），曾任新西伯利亚总领事。他也是湖北人，会说英语、法语和俄语。他曾一度任职于重庆外交部

（右上角印章及手写内容：上海公共租界工部局警务处。S.2 登记处 档案号 S. B. 1).）

最后提到的这位是一名美国飞行员，他与另一名名为F.V. Wagner的美国人曾在1938年4月20日的D.8000号报告中被提及，称其于1938年4月20日离开上海前往香港，途中代表日本情报机关前往汉口工作。

关于另外两名外国人的背景，档案中并无记录，但毫无疑问，他们是亲日的，其行踪令人怀疑。

李芳显然人脉广泛，通过其以往的外交活动，在华人和外国人中拥有庞大的朋友圈，其中不乏极具声望者。据报，他或易将军（General Yi）与海防的法国当局关系良好，从而在这个重要通道上为货物运输制造困难和延误。

1939年6月，李芳经法国总领事馆介绍向法国警察申请手枪执照，后者将其转介至工部局警务处（C.3科），并附推荐信建议购买手枪。他获准购买两支手枪，尽管法国当局已签发此类执照，但其在本租界内携带手枪的申请仍被拒绝。

Authorities.
    I do not believe that Li Fang has under him a gang of armed men. This must refer to Li Chi Chuen (李自群) of 95/10 Edinburgh Road.
    Li Chi Chuen claims to have come from the family of the late Lord Li Hung Chang, but enquiries do not confirm this statement. He is believed to have had some connection with Chinese guerillas and through the introduction of a Japanese named Katayama he surrendered to the Japanese Military who is utilising his services to cope with Chinese Government terrorists in the Western District.
    Li Chi Chuen has about 100 armed followers and depends for their maintenance on a monthly subsidy from the Yung Sung Roulette Den at Kong Ka Jao, Connaught Road. He has also invested some money in the Shanghai Inland Water Navigation Company, North Soochow Road. It is reported that Li has offered the services of his men to Mr. Waung Ching Wei for his personal safety during his stay in Shanghai. Negotiations have been going on between Li and Chen Chung Li, nephew of Mr. Waung, but the offer has not yet been accepted.
    Li is strongly backed up by Katayama but Commandant Fujimo of the Japanese Gendarmerie has very little confidence in him. Li has, it is further reported, established an office at 36 Jessfield Road in the name of Mr. Waung Ching Wei as his house at 95/10 Edinburgh Road has once or twice come to the notice of the S.M.P.

    我不认为李芳手下有一帮武装人员。这指的必须是爱丁堡路95/10号的李自群（Li Chi Chuen）。
    李自群声称出自已故李鸿章爵爷家族，但调查并未证实这一说法。据信他曾与中国游击队有某种联系，并通过一名叫片山（Katayama）的日本人的介绍，向日军投降，日军正利用他的服务来对付西区的中国政府恐怖分子。
    李自群约有100名武装追随者，其给养依赖于康纳路（Connaught Road）孔家角（Kong Ka Jao）永盛轮盘赌馆每月提供的津贴。他还在北苏州路的上海内河航运公司投资了一些资金。据报，李已向汪精卫先生提出，在其逗留上海期间为其个人安全提供服务。李与汪先生的侄子陈仲礼（Chen Chung Li）之间一直在进行谈判，但该提议尚未被接受。
    李得到片山的强力支持，但日本宪兵队司令藤本（Fujimo）对他缺乏信心。另据报，李已在杰斯菲尔德路36号以汪精卫先生的名义设立办事处，因为他在爱丁堡路95/10号的住所曾一两次引起工部局警务处的注意。

Mr. C. Y. Li hereby engages R. E. Griffiths, John F. Trundello, and
Desire du Berrier as military air pilots on the following terms:—
As soon as the above named pilots agree to proceed to China, they shall
on or about April 15th report to General C. Y. Li at his
arrival in ____ or at any such other place as instructed by
C. Y. Li the undersigned pilots will be assigned and hereby consent to carry
out such duties as may be assigned to them at any time after their arrival
at ____.
The above named pilots hereby accept £10 only for their travelling expenses
and is only for immediate expenses in Hongkong, this last amount shall be
redeemed out of their salaries within three months under the directions of
Li Fang.
All parties to this agreement pledge their support and loyalty to the
Chinese Government.
The undersigned pilots agree to and guarantee that they will cease when they
may introduce into the service at later date small refrain from participation
in any political activities and in particular shall neither party be associated
with or engage in any communistic activities.
The pilots above named agree to participate in all military duties which may
be assigned to them such as scouting, observation from the air of parapets
and bombills, bombing, pursuit, long range flights and night flying.
The above named pilots shall be prepared to establish a flying training
school under the administration of C. Y. Li.
It is expressly understood and agreed upon that each one of the above named
pilots hereby engaged shall treat such engagement and any other matter con-
nected to him as absolutely confidential.
The above named pilots hereby undertake to maintain physical fitness through
physical exercises and aviation flying which shall be afforded them but which
they will not be considered as part of their active service flying and they
shall be at their own disposal during such period.
The above named pilots are expected to do all in their power to observe
the full term of their contract. The commencement of their
active service duties (whether on land or in the air) shall be determined solely
by their commanding officer, irrespective of the period of time which may be
required for their preliminary services and prior to active service flying the
above named pilots undertake not to resign and not to leave the service and
hereby mutually pledge the observance of this particular stipulation.
The above named pilots agree to accept a monthly salary of $300 National Cur-
rency as from April 15th, 1928 which salary is to be increased to $600 National
Currency when and as soon as active service duties commence and shall then be
subject to further increases at the discretion of their commanding officer in
whose fair treatment and fair play the said pilots confide their trust. In
addition to this salary and immediately upon arrival at ____ the above
pilots shall receive board and lodgings free of charge to themselves.
This agreement is binding and effective as of date and shall be ratified
according to terms herein stated and agreed upon and at the request of either
party to this agreement shall be superseded by a new detailed contract.

R. E. Griffiths [Signature]
John F. Trundello [Signature]      C. Y. Li [Signature]
Desire du Berrier [Signature]

C. Y. Li 先生 hereby 聘请 R. E. Griffiths、John F. Trundello 和 Desire du Berrier 为军事航空飞行员，条款如下：—
一旦上述飞行员同意前往中国，他们应于4月15日左右向 C. Y. Li 将军报到，地点为其抵达 ____ 之时，或由 C. Y. Li 指示的任何其他地方。下述飞行员将被分配任务，并在此同意在抵达 ____ 后的任何时间执行分配给他们的任务。
上述飞行员 hereby 仅接受10英镑作为旅费，该款项仅用于在香港的即时开销，此笔金额将在李芳的指导下，在三个月内从他们的薪水中扣除偿还。
本协议各方承诺支持并效忠中国政府。
下述飞行员同意并保证，他们将停止（原文此处语句不通顺，似有缺漏或错误：cease when they may introduce into the service at later date small refrain from participation in any political activities），特别是任何一方不得参与或从事任何共产主义活动。
上述飞行员同意参与分配给他们的一切军事任务，如侦察、从空中观察掩体和炸弹坑（bombills，原文如此）、轰炸、追击、长途飞行和夜间飞行。
上述飞行员应准备在 C. Y. Li 的管理下建立一所飞行训练学校。
双方明确理解并同意，上述每位受聘飞行员应将此聘用及与其相关的任何其他事项视为绝对机密。
上述飞行员 hereby 承诺通过体育锻炼和航空飞行保持身体健康，这些锻炼和飞行将提供给他们，但不被视为其现役飞行任务的一部分，在此期间由他们自行支配。
期望上述飞行员尽其所能遵守合同的全部期限。其现役职责（无论是陆地还是空中）的开始时间应完全由其指挥官决定，无论初步服务可能需要多长时间，且在开始现役飞行之前，上述飞行员承诺不辞职、不离开服役，并在此相互承诺遵守这一特定规定。
上述飞行员同意自1928年4月15日起接受每月300元国币的薪水，当现役职责开始时，薪水将增加至600元国币，此后是否进一步增加由其指挥官酌情决定，上述飞行员信任其指挥官的公平对待和公正行事。除上述薪水外，上述飞行员在抵达 ____ 后立即免费获得食宿。
本协议自签署之日起具有约束力并生效，应根据 herein 所述及同意的条款予以批准，并应本协议任何一方要求，由一份新的详细合同取代。

R. E. Griffiths [签名]
John F. Trundello [签名]      C. Y. Li [签名]
Desire du Berrier [签名]

CONFIDENTIAL

JAPANESE BUILDING FORTIFICATIONS AROUND
SHANGHAI
________________________________________

It is learned from a reliable source that recently the Japanese
Special Service Organ in Shanghai has made desperate efforts to hire one hundred
trucks to be engaged in transportation of materials for the construction of
fortifications around Shanghai. Approaches have been made by Japanese officials
to local truck hire agencies for the transaction but is not yet successful owing
to shortage of supply. Two hundred trucks have already been engaged in the
similar work and one hundred more is needed for the required job. Well-in-
formed circles in close touch with the Japanese secret service report that
extensive fortifications are being constructed in a place seven miles from the
North Station of the Shanghai-Nanking Railways. The location is believed to
be near Woosung and Paoshan. The informant pointed out to your agent that he
is sure that these fortifications are being built for the purpose of defending
Shanghai against the Western nations and not China. These fortifications will
require three years to complete as these trucks will be hired for such a long
period. Each truck will be required to work for twelve hours a day to trans-
port building materials from the North Station to the area which is being
fortified. A trip from the station to that secret place and return will re-
quire one hour and twenty minutes and a hired charge of $5.00 will be paid.
That means every truck will make about nine trips one day. This is but a
small angle of the situation, which the powers should be gravely concerned.
pages.zh:
机密

日本人在上海周围修建防御工事
___

从可靠消息来源获悉，最近日本驻上海的特务机关拼命努力雇佣一百辆卡车，用于运输在上海周围修建防御工事的材料。日本官员已接触当地卡车租赁机构以达成交易，但由于供应短缺，尚未成功。已有两百辆卡车从事类似工作，还需要一百辆来完成所需任务。与日本秘密服务部门密切联系的知情圈子报告称，在距沪宁铁路北站七英里的地方正在修建大规模防御工事。据信该地点位于吴淞和宝山附近。线人向你的特工指出，他确信这些防御工事的修建目的是为了保护上海免受西方国家的侵害，而非针对中国。这些防御工事需要三年才能完成，因为这些卡车将被雇佣如此长的时间。每辆卡车每天需要工作十二小时，将建筑材料从北站运送到正在设防的区域。从车站到那个秘密地点往返一次需要一小时二十分钟，支付租赁费用5.00美元。这意味着每辆卡车每天大约跑九趟。这只是局势的一个小侧面，列强应予以严重关注。

International Settlement and the French Concession;
the complications that must arise from time to time, it
is my intention to inaugurate a movement to be supported
by the people born in Shanghai, and also by those who
have been residing here for a period of years and have
their interests in Shanghai.-
At the present time this movement lends itself to
serious consideration and it is more than probable,
that the Favoured Powers, who are interested will
consider this movement as a solution to the more serious
complications that will arise. This movement would
eliminate all friction that at present exists and that
may increase to considerable disadvantage and proportion.-
The definition of the Free Port of Shanghai would mean;
that in a short period of time Shanghai would become the
greatest City in the world. Instead of anxiety and
uncertainty it will bring prosperity and freedom to
millions of people.-
The Free Port of Shanghai would abolish the Custom
House; by this move the whole of the population of this
Free Port will buy imported material at a considerable
saving; the present Custom House Building on the Bund
pages.zh:
上海自由港。

鉴于目前涉及国际租界和法租界的不确定性；
以及不时必然出现的复杂情况，
我打算发起一场运动，得到生于上海的人，
以及那些在此居住多年并在上海拥有利益的人的支持。-
目前，这场运动值得认真考虑，极有可能，
感兴趣的优待列强会将此运动视为解决
即将出现的更严重复杂局面的一种方案。这场运动将
消除目前存在的所有摩擦，否则这些摩擦可能会增加到
相当不利的程度和比例。-
上海自由港的定义意味着；
在短时间内，上海将成为
世界上最大的城市。它将带来繁荣和自由，
取代焦虑和不确定性，惠及
数百万人民。-
上海自由港将废除海关；
通过此举，这个自由港的所有居民将以
相当大的节省购买进口材料；目前外滩的海关大楼

pages.en:
2.-
to be utilized as the administration building of the
Free Port of Shanghai.-
Instead of a dozen or more Courts that now exist, there
will be only one Court of the Free City of Shanghai.-
The Dollar, in its present confusion, will receive the
connecting medium, it so badly needs at present, a
Dollar with a back bone to it - a Dollar backed up by
real Silver - a Dollar which will be a Dollar.
Merchants and financiers will welcome support to an
issue of notes against which Silver - of which there is
plenty in the market - can be exchanged at a fixed
rate. In other words the Silver Dollar of the Free Port
of Shanghai, will become a real Dollar, and take its
place, side by side, with stabilized currency.-
With tens of thousands of immigrants who are now in
Shanghai, and more to arrive, and the additional thousands
of foreigners, as well as the millions of people living
in this area will benefit by this movement, in as much
as they can become citizens of the Free Port of
Shanghai.-
The idea of the Free Port of Shanghai is not an idea in
that merchandise only might be imported free of duty, but
it is an idea to benefit millions of people, irrespective
of Nationality or Religion. It means that the Free Port
pages.zh:
2.-
将被用作上海自由港的行政大楼。-
代替现在存在的十几个或更多法院，
将只有一个上海自由市法院。-
美元，在目前混乱的情况下，将获得
它目前迫切需要的连接媒介，一种
有支撑的美元——一种由真银支撑的
美元——一种真正的美元。
商人和金融家将欢迎支持发行
票据，凭此票据可按固定汇率兑换
市场上充足的白银。换句话说，上海
自由港的银元将成为真正的美元，并与
稳定货币并列占据其地位。-
随着成千上万目前在上海的移民，
以及更多即将到来的移民，加上额外的数千名
外国人，以及生活在这个地区的数百万人民
都将从这场运动中受益，因为他们可以成为
上海自由港的公民。-
上海自由港的理念不仅仅是一个
商品可以免税进口的理念，而是一个
造福数百万人民的理念，无论
国籍或宗教如何。这意味着自由港

pages.en:
3.-
of Shanghai, is taken over by those born in the land,
irrespective of where their fore fathers come from.-
Heritage gives the right to every individual to have
a voice in the land where he was born, and as there are
hundreds of thousands of people, of every nationality,
born in Shanghai, they should be able, as a united body,
to accomplish this movement, and by so doing benefit
everybody concerned in this area as well as thousands
of others who have been unfortunate in other lands.-
Japan, America, Great Britain, and other favoured
Nations will be asked to act as guarantors for the Free
Port of Shanghai and to give the Free Port of Shanghai
the Security against attack or encirclement; which will
enable the Free Port of Shanghai to carry out its
project of a United, Free and Independent Centre.-
In short the creation of a new small nation: The Free
Port of Shanghai.-
This memo is an embryo of the idea of the Free Port of
Shanghai; a beginning which has great possibilities; a
cause which lends itself to realistic and constructive
accomplishment.

上海，由在这片土地上出生的人接管，
不论其祖先来自何处。-
遗产赋予每个人在他出生的土地上拥有
发言权的权利，鉴于有
数十万各种国籍的人
在上海出生，他们应该能够作为一个整体，
完成这一运动，并以此造福该地区的所有相关人员，以及成千上万在其他地方遭遇不幸的人。-
日本、美国、英国和其他受优待的
国家将被请求担任上海自由港的保证人，
并为上海自由港提供免受攻击或包围的安全保障；
这将使上海自由港能够实施其
建立一个统一、自由和独立中心的计划。-
简而言之，就是创建一个新的小国：上海自由港。-
本备忘录是上海自由港构想的雏形；
这是一个具有巨大可能性的开端；
这是一项有助于实现现实和建设性成就的事业。

INTERNATIONAL SECRET SERVICE ORGANIZED BY
WANG CHING-WEI'S GROUP IN SHANGHAI

Mr. Wang Ching-wei's traitorous campaign in this part of China is becoming internationalized according to exclusive information secured from a reliable foreign source in close touch with the situation. Mr. Chow Fu-hai (周佛海), formerly minister of propaganda of Central Kuomintang headquarters and a trusted agent of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, had been active in Shanghai for the past three months, as previously reported. He organized for Mr. Wang's campaign, a secret service net-work in Shanghai and entrusted the job to a Mr. Liu Shou-kwei (劉少魁), alias Gen. Liu Hai-sheng, a military man from Szechuen. This Gen. Liu is reported to have drawn a subsidy of $400,000.00 per month from the various gambling dens in the west district of Shanghai through special arrangements made by the Japanese Special Service Organ. It is also learned that several of Mr. Wang Ching-wei's leading subordinates have also invested heavily in these gambling houses, hence the subsidy. Another Cantonese called Mr. Chu Ting collects money from these gambling houses for Gen. Liu regularly. With this huge amount of money, Gen. Liu is maintaining a force of 900 Chinese and foreign agents engaged in various kinds of secret activities. Under Gen. Liu there is a native of Hupeh by the name of Li Lien-fang (李聯芳) who is specially assigned to supervise the work of foreign agents. Mr. Li was formerly in charge of the intelligence service under Mr. Kao Tsung-wu (高宗武), then director of the Asiatic Bureau of Waichiaopu under Wang Ching-wei's ministership several years ago. My foreign informant after mixing up with this group found out
pages.zh:
汪精卫集团在上海组织的国际秘密情报机构

据从与局势密切联系的可靠外国来源获得的独家消息，汪精卫先生在中国这一地区的叛国活动正日益国际化。正如先前报道的那样，前中国国民党中央宣传部部长、汪精卫先生的亲信周佛海（Chow Fu-hai）过去三个月一直在上海活跃。他为汪先生的运动在上海组织了一个秘密情报网，并将这项工作委托给刘少魁（Liu Shou-kwei），别名刘海生将军（Gen. Liu Hai-sheng），一名来自四川的军人。据报道，刘将军通过日本特务机关做出的特别安排，每月从上海西区的各个赌场抽取400,000.00美元的津贴。还获悉，汪精卫先生的几名主要下属也在这些赌馆中投入巨资，因此才有这笔津贴。另一名广东人朱定（Chu Ting）先生定期为刘将军向这些赌馆收钱。利用这笔巨款，刘将军维持着一支由900名中外特工组成的队伍，从事各种秘密活动。在刘将军手下有一名湖北籍人士李联芳（Li Lien-fang），专门负责监督外籍特工的工作。李先生几年前曾在高宗武（Kao Tsung-wu）领导的情报部门任职，当时高宗武在汪精卫任部长期间担任外交部亚洲司司长。我的外国线人在混入该团伙后发现

pages.en:
- 2 -

that Mr. Li has under him a big number of foreign agents among whom there
are a Ing. Nino J. Brondello, an Italian air officer, a Count du Berrier,
a French munition salesman, a Mr. Wright, a Canadian young man and a certain
German staying at the Palace Hotel. Their secret headquarters are at Mr.
Li's residence situated at Flat D. 21, Sun Court Apartments, 621 Weihaiwei
Road. But these first three foreigners have their own quarters some where
at Route Pere Robert. My informant believes that these foreigners besides
doing intelligence service for Mr. Wang Ching-wei, also purchase arms and
munitions for their leader. Their houses are well guarded with armed men
and they carry pistols with them whenever they go. They claim that they
have good connections with both the S.M.P. and F.M.P., that is why they are
able to get licenses for their pistols from the police. Mr. Brondello told
my informant that Mr. Wang Ching-wei is receiving a subsidy of $5,000,000
from the Japanese every month. From the observations made by my informant,
it is believed that these men are also engaged in the assassination of Wang
Ching-wei's enemies. At least they are preparing to do so.

Mr. Li Lien-f'ng is reported to have decided to send Mr. Wright to
Hankow, Court du Barrier to Nanking and Ing. Brondello to Wuhu for important
mission. They are to help in "reconstruction" of these cities, Mr. Li said.

My informant is working hard to find out the whole situation as
she has the trust of these foreigners. If she has the necessary backing, it
is believed that she will be able to unearth a most alarming story of inter-
national significance.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

李先生手下有大量外籍特工，其中包括
意大利空军军官尼诺·J·布龙代洛工程师（Ing. Nino J. Brondello）、
法国军火商杜·贝里埃伯爵（Count du Berrier）、
加拿大青年赖特先生（Mr. Wright）以及某位
住在华懋公寓（Palace Hotel）的德国人。他们的秘密总部设在
威海卫路621号孙科特公寓（Sun Court Apartments）D座21室李先生的住所。但这前三名外国人在
罗伯特神父路（Route Pere Robert）某处有自己的住处。我的线人认为，这些外国人除了为汪精卫先生从事情报工作外，还为其领袖购买武器和弹药。他们的住所均有武装人员严密把守，外出时随身携带手枪。他们声称与上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）和法租界公董局警务处（F.M.P.）都有良好关系，这就是他们能够从警方获得手枪许可证的原因。布龙代洛先生告诉我的线人，汪精卫先生每月从日本人那里获得5,000,000美元的津贴。根据我的线人的观察，相信这些人也参与刺杀汪精卫敌人的行动。至少他们正在为此做准备。

据报道，李联芳先生已决定派遣赖特先生前往
汉口，杜·贝里埃前往南京，布龙代洛工程师前往芜湖执行重要任务。李先生说，他们将协助这些城市的“重建”工作。

我的线人正在努力查明全部情况，因为
她得到了这些外国人的信任。如果她得到必要的支持，相信
她将能够揭露一个具有国际意义的惊人故事。

S.2 Special Branch
REPORT
Date ____ 19 39.

Subject Reported doubtful attitude of General Ho Chien and
General Chen Yi.

Made by ________ and ________ Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

Information has been received from a reliable source
that one Dr. Liu Hua Jui (劉華瑞) alias Liu Wei Kiu (劉穗九),
is in Shanghai busily entertaining Japanese military and naval
officers. He is said to be representing General Ho Chien (何健),
until recently Governor of Hunan.

It may be recalled that General Ho was removed from his
post a few months ago because Generalissimo Chiang, it is alleged,
was dissatisfied with him on account of his indifference during
the hostilities prior to the fall of the Wuhan cities as he had
failed to respond to orders to dispatch Hunan troops to the front.
He was replaced by General Chang Chih Chung (張治中), former
Commander-in-Chief of the Shanghai Expeditionary Forces, and
summoned to Chungking where, it is reported, he has been placed
under surveillance and his troops have since been transferred to
the front in Hupeh.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 24 MAY 1939）
FILE

It is interesting to note that Liu Hua Jui, the alleged
delegate of General Ho, was formerly a strong agitator against
the Japanese. In 1931 he was reported to have participated in
the organization of the People's National Salvation Association
in Shanghai and in 1932 when the League of Nation's Commission
of Inquiry visited Shanghai he was a technical advisor to the
Commission and drafted the memorandum on the diplomatic problems
of Manchuria.

Another delegate of Chungking official equally as active
as Liu is a man named Hsu Veng Yuen (徐文元). Little is known
of his antecedents but he claims to represent General Chen Yi
(陳儀), the present Governor of Fukien.

General Chen Yi received his military education in
Japan where he married a Japanese lady. He was at one time the

从可靠来源收到消息，
一名叫刘华瑞（Liu Hua Jui），别名刘穗九（Liu Wei Kiu）的博士，
正在上海忙于宴请日本海陆军军官。据说他代表
不久前曾任湖南省主席的何键将军（General Ho Chien）。

回想起来，何将军几个月前被免职，原因是据称
蒋委员长对他不满，因为在武汉三镇陷落前的敌对行动中他表现冷漠，未能响应命令派遣湖南部队前往前线。
他由前上海远征军总司令张治中将军（General Chang Chih Chung）接替，
并被召至重庆，据报道，他在那里受到监视，其部队此后已被调往湖北前线。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处处长办公室 1939年5月24日）
归档

值得注意的是，据称是何将军代表的刘华瑞，以前曾是强烈的反日煽动者。据报道，1931年他参与了上海民众救国会的组织工作，1932年国际联盟调查团访问上海时，他是调查团的技术顾问，并起草了关于满洲外交问题的备忘录。

另一位与刘同样活跃的重庆官员代表是一个名叫徐文元（Hsu Veng Yuen）的人。对他的背景知之甚少，但他声称代表现任福建省主席陈仪将军（General Chen Yi）。

April 17, 1939. Morning Translation.

Shanghai Daily News, a mosquito paper, dated April 16 :-

Activities of Wang Ching-Wei's Followers in Shanghai

It is learned that Ling Pah-sun (林柏生),
the principal follower of Wang Ching-wei, has arrived
in Shanghai secretly and is very active. Apart from
buying over a certain printing plant to expand propaganda
work, Ling has made arrangements to take over two evening
newspapers at a price of several tens of thousand dollars
each. The arrangements for the purchase of one of these
two papers have been settled. It is said that the policy
of the paper will be changed.

Hwa Mei Chen Pao published the following article on April 16 :-

The activities of the followers of Wang Ching-
wei in Shanghai are gradually becoming more apparent.
A certain printing plant on Avenue Road has been bought
over and renamed the Hsin --- Printing Press (新--印刷所).
Preparations are being made for the publication of a
paper to be known as ----Daily News.

O.S.L. Liao

4月16日的《上海日报》，一家小报：-

汪精卫追随者在上海的活动

据悉，汪精卫的主要追随者林柏生（Ling Pah-sun）已秘密抵达上海，并且非常活跃。除了收买某家印刷厂以扩大宣传工作外，林还安排以每家数万美元的价格接管两家晚报。其中一家报纸的购买安排已敲定。据说该报的方针将发生改变。

汪精卫追随者在上海的活动逐渐变得明显。
爱文义路上的一家印刷厂已被收买，并更名为新--印刷所（Hsin --- Printing Press）。

Subject Activities of Wang Ching Wei's followers in Shanghai.

Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

The reported arrival in Shanghai of Mr. Wang Ching Wei
could not be confirmed by enquiries made amongst pro-Japanese
elements. It is believed however that Chou Fu Hai (周佛海),
one of the principal followers of Mr. Wang is now in Shanghai
actively but secretly carrying on "peace" propaganda.
Mr. Chou was until recently attached to the Central Kuomintang
Party of Chungking and is reported to have a large following
of students and teachers here whose acquaintance he made when
he was Commissioner of Education of the Kiangsu Provincial
Government in 1935. Several Chinese prominent residents
in Shanghai have received printed circulars through the post
reproducing the telegrams despatched by Mr. Wang advocating
peace. Like Mr. Wang Ching Wei, Chou Fu Hai received his
education in Japan. He is a good writer and is the author
of several books.

Date October 28. 1938.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE REGISTRY A.D. 8986 (c)）

Subject Return of Mr. L.P. Sung to Shanghai.

Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

Mr. L.P. Sung (孫履平), who styles himself
Colonel L.P. Sung, B.Sc., a former adjutant and secretary
to General Yang Hu, the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commander
in 1936/37, who left Shanghai in November last, has returned
to Shanghai. He called at this office on the afternoon of
October 27. Questioned as to the object of his visit to
Shanghai, he stated that he had just returned to visit friends
in a private capacity. He had been to Hongkong, Hankow,
Szechuen and Yunnan. In the course of further conversation
he revealed he was now representing the Waichiaopu in Shanghai
and would undertake the visa of passports if these are required
by Counsil's employees. I warned him in a friendly manner to
cease such activities in the Settlement as they would be to
his disadvantage. He stated he would call on the Commissioner
and D.C. (Crime) who, he alleges, are his personal friends.

It will be remembered that Mr. Sung was at one time
an active member of the Chinese Seamen's Union who figured
prominently in the trouble with the stewards of the Indo China
Steam Navigation Company and in a strike of tallymen of the
same firm. It is believed he was once expelled from the
Seamen's Union for corrupt practices when settling a dispute
for compensation in connection with the death of a seaman
who was alleged to have been thrown overboard from a foreign
steamer.

（左侧手写批注：Take him to keep out of Settlement & warn him re ship.）
（左侧印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 28 OCT. 1938）
（左侧手写批注：Noted 31/10 Jaw L.P. Sung warned.）

主题：L.P. Sung 先生返回上海。

制作及呈报人：谭绍良警司

L.P. Sung (孙履平) 先生，自称 L.P. Sung 上校，理学学士，曾是1936/37年吴淞-上海守备司令杨虎将军的副官和秘书，去年11月离开上海，现已返回上海。他于10月27日下午来到本办事处。当被问及来沪目的时，他表示刚回来以私人身份拜访朋友。他曾去过香港、汉口、四川和云南。在进一步的谈话中，他透露他现在代表外交部在上海工作，如果工部局雇员需要，他将负责护照签证事宜。我以友好的方式警告他停止在租界内的此类活动，因为这对他不利。他表示将拜访警务处处长和刑事处处长 (D.C. (Crime))，他声称这两人是他的私人朋友。

记得孙先生曾是中国海员工会的活跃成员，在印度支那轮船公司服务员纠纷以及该公司理货员罢工事件中表现突出。据信，他曾在处理一名据称被从外国轮船上抛入海中致死的海员的赔偿纠纷时，因腐败行为被海员工会开除。

（左侧手写批注：带他离开租界并就船只问题警告他。）
（左侧印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处处长办公室 1938年10月28日）
（左侧手写批注：10月31日 noted。已警告 L.P. Sung。）

A new organization entitled the "Kiangsu
Provincial Kuomintang Headquarters" (江苏省有党部)
was recently established at 3rd floor, 75 Jessfield
Road. One LI TSE MING (李志明), a deputy of the
new "Central Government" for Shanghai, is in charge
of the headquarters in question.

LI TSE MING has been also appointed by the
Administrative Yuan of the new "Central Government"
to take charge of the "Foh Shing National and Party
Flag Company" (復興裝銷黨國旗公司)
in the place of WANG MAI YUNG (汪曼雲), an
ex-committee member of the defunct local Tangpu, who
joined the Wang Ching Wei party in 1939, and who has
since been a member of the Central Executive Committee
of Wang Ching Wei sponsored Kuomintang. The company
is situated in the same premises (75 Jessfield Road)
which house the various tangpus formed by Wang's
clique. It came into existence at the beginning
of April, 1940, with a view to effecting control over
flag manufacturing shops and factories in Shanghai
and places under the occupation of Japanese troops.

一个名为“江苏省国民党总部”（江苏省有党部）的新组织最近在极司菲尔路 (Jessfield Road) 75号三楼成立。一位名叫李志明 (LI TSE MING) 的人，是新“中央政府”驻上海的代表，负责该总部。

李志明也被新“中央政府”行政院任命，接替汪曼云 (WANG MAI YUNG) 负责“复兴装销党国旗公司”（復興裝銷黨國旗公司）。汪曼云是已解散的地方党部的前委员，于1939年加入汪精卫派系，此后一直担任汪精卫支持的国民党中央执行委员会委员。该公司位于同一地点（极司菲尔路75号），那里设有汪派系组建的各个党部。该公司成立于1940年4月初，旨在控制上海及日军占领地区的旗帜制造商店和工厂。

C. Crawford
D. I.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.I., Special Branch. xxxxxxx
REPORT
Date March 19, 1940.
Subject Wang Ching Wei's Kuomintang - nominal establishment
of ten local District Branch Tangpu.
Made by....................................................Forwarded by....................................................

Following the recent inauguration at 75 Jessfield
Road, O.O.L. of the local Tangpu of the kuomintang
sponsored by the Wang Ching Wei clique, arrangements
have been in progress for the establishment of ten
District Branch Tangpu in Shanghai for the purpose
of taking charge of affairs appertaining to the
Kuomintang in the various parts of this city. While
no definite measures have been announced regarding
the spheres of influence of these ten district
branches, it has been reported that they will be
similar to those of the now defunct local Kuomintang,
prior to the outbreak of the local hostilities in
1937. During a meeting held on March 13, 1940
in the office of the local Tangpu at 75 Jessfield
Road, the following personnel were nominated who will
be responsible for the affairs in their respective
districts:-

District Personnel.
1st District (formerly Yao Yuin Po (姚雲甫),
covering the areas formerly secretary of the

standing committee of the
29th District Tangpu.

Pan Yao Ting (潘耀庭),
formerly secretary of the
26th District Tangpu.

2nd District (formerly Tu Mong Sung (杜夢森),
covering the formerly secretary of the
French Concession) now defunct local Tangpu.

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

JUL 5 1938

A Wang-Brand “Kuomintang”

EVEN the whereabouts of Mr. Wang Ching-wei (various reported as visiting Shanghai, Hongkong, Tokyo and Peiping) have been in doubt for weeks past. His state of mind, if any, is conveyed by proxy. One wonders at times if he is not just a myth, after all. Yet busy rumors keep explaining just what he is about to do—though they are usually rather cautious when it comes to details as to how and when he is going to do it.

Latest of the crop of reports is a Peiping Reuter dispatch which says that Mr. Wang has been visiting the northern ex-capital and that he is about to head a new government to replace the one functioning (the word is Reuter’s, not ours) in Nanking, although the Peiping Government will continue on a semi-independent basis. Just what it is to be semi-independent of is not made clear; we feel sure it is not to be even semi-independent of Japan, but probably it will be considerably more than that with reference to Peiping.

According to this report the new administration is to be known as the Chun Min, or All-People’s Government; it is to govern all Japanese-occupied territory south of the Lunghai, that it is to have a flag with white sun on blue ground of the Kuomintang with the old five-barred flag in the corner, and that “elements in the Kuomintang opposed to General Chiang Kai-shek” will be allowed to carry on their activities in Chun Min territory while the Japanese army will train Chinese troops for the new government.

Parenthetically it may be pointed out that North China reports indicate that Marshal Wu Pei-fu has decisively dropped the Japanese, finding them indisposed to agree to his proposals that they withdraw garrisons from China and treat China as an elder brother or grandmother. This development should be weighed against the latest Wang report, probably, as showing an abandonment of emphasis on the northern regime and a fresh effort to put weight into the Nanking balance.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》。

1938年7月5日

一个汪氏品牌的“国民党”

甚至汪精卫先生的下落（有各种报道说他访问了上海、香港、东京和北平）在过去几周里也一直是个谜。如果他还有什么心态的话，也是通过代理人传达的。人们有时不禁怀疑，他毕竟是否只是一个神话人物。然而，忙碌的谣言不断解释他正要做什么——尽管在涉及他将如何以及何时去做这些事的细节时，它们通常相当谨慎。

最新的一批报道来自北平路透社电文，称汪先生一直访问这座北方前首都，并且即将领导一个新政府来取代在南京运作（这个词是路透社用的，不是我们用的）的政府，尽管北平政府将继续保持半独立状态。究竟对谁半独立并不清楚；我们可以肯定，它对日本甚至不会是半独立的，但相对于北平而言，情况可能远不止于此。

根据这份报告，新行政机构将被称为“新民”，即全民政府；它将管辖陇海线以南所有日军占领区，其旗帜将是国民党青天白日旗，角落里有旧五色旗，并且“反对蒋介石将军的国民党分子”将被允许在新民领土内开展活动，同时日军将为新政府训练中国军队。

顺便可以指出，华北的报道表明，吴佩孚元帅已经果断地抛弃了日本人，发现他们不愿意同意他的提议，即从撤出在中国的驻军并将中国视为兄长或祖母对待。这一发展或许应与最新的汪氏报道加以权衡，因为它显示出对北方政权的重视程度有所放弃，并重新努力增加南京方面的分量。

pages.en:
Mr. Wang is proving a rather hot chestnut
for the Japanese, it would appear, but they
want to find use for him and this may be it.
Having learned that his defection signally failed
to split the National Government, an attempt
will be made to create the semblance of a split
in the Kuomintang. The Kuomintang has flung
Mr. Wang out with enthusiasm but that is not
to matter; all the rest of the army will be out
of step and only Mr. Wang will be in step; he,
and he alone, will emerge as leader of the
"true Kuomintang" which the people of China
will be invited to follow. Mr. Wang will be given
a Kuomintang Government, a Kuomintang
capital, even a made-by-Japan Kuomintang
army armed with cap pistols and lath swords,
or grown-up equivalents. We imagine that it
may even become possible for members of the
Automobile Club of China to display their of-
ficial insignia, Kuomintang blue field white
star and all, without objection from Japanese
sentries.

It's quite an idea. We shall have an official
Kuomintang and an unofficial Kuomintang,
and which is which will depend upon our sym-
pathies. By the Japanese, of course, only the
Wang brand Kuomintang will be regarded as
kosher.

The sole question is whether anybody is
going to be kidded. It seems to us that there
are elements of confusion there for everyone
except the Chinese, who are, after all, the only
people who much matter. And the Chinese are
a rather shrewd straight-thinking lot with a
great deal of experience in detecting counter-
feits. They have Mr. Wang very well figured out
at the moment, which is one reason why his
whereabouts are being kept such a profound
mystery.
pages.zh:
看来，汪先生对日本人来说是一个相当棘手的难题，但他们想利用他，这可能就是用途所在。既然得知他的叛逃未能显著分裂国民政府，他们将试图制造国民党分裂的假象。国民党热情地将汪先生驱逐出去，但这无关紧要；其余所有的军队都将步调不一，只有汪先生步调一致；他，且只有他，将作为“真正国民党”的领袖出现，中国人民将被邀请追随他。汪先生将得到一个国民党政府，一个国民党首都，甚至一支由日本制造的国民党军队，装备着玩具手枪和木刀，或者成年人的等效替代品。我们想象，中国汽车俱乐部的成员甚至可能在不受到日本哨兵反对的情况下展示他们的官方徽章，包括国民党蓝底白星等所有标志。

这真是个主意。我们将有一个官方的国民党和一个非官方的国民党，哪个是哪个将取决于我们的同情心。当然，在日本人看来，只有汪氏品牌的国民党才是正统的。

唯一的问题是是否有人会受骗。在我们看来，除了中国人之外，这对所有人来说都有混淆的因素，而中国人毕竟是唯一重要的人群。中国人是一群相当精明、思维直率的人，在识破伪造品方面有着丰富的经验。他们目前对汪先生看得很清楚，这也是他的行踪被保持如此神秘的原因之一。

With reference to the report that over
10,000 copies of the Chinese American Daily News
had been bought up by followers of Wang Ching Wei
(Ind. Stockpola)
on the morning of September 4, the management is
of the opinion that the copies were bought up with
the express purpose of preventing the public from
reading an anti-Wang Ching Wei article which was
published in the paper on that date.

Enquiries made amongst the Chinese staff of
the paper reveal that a group of men intimidated
the news boys and took all available copies of the
paper, later sending the money for same to the
newspaper offices, 160 Avenue Edward VII.

The news boys from whom the papers were
taken are alleged to have told the Chinese circu-
lation manager of the Chinese American Daily News
that they recognised the men as employees or ex-
employees of the Central China Daily News, the
local pro-Wang Ching Wei propaganda organ.

Date September 5, 1939.

Subject Chinese-American Daily News.

Made by. C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang,    Forwarded by. C. Gaspar J.J

At 7 a.m. September 4, a number of Chinese
appeared at Shantung Road between Hankow and Soochow
Road, where news vendors gather every morning for
distribution of news papers, and purchased all copies
of the Chinese-American Daily News found available
there. Some 10,000 copies were thus cornered and
only 5,000 copies succeeded in reaching the public
as they had been distributed prior to the incident.
Consequently the price of the paper instantly rose
to 5 cents per copy as against the usual price at
2 cents.

On learning of this sudden wholesale purchase,
the management of this Daily News immediately printed
an additional 10,000 copies in order to meet the
demands of the public.

The situation has returned to normal this
morning, the original price of 2 cents per copy being
maintained and so far no person has appeared to
repeat the attempt.

A general belief among news vendors regarding
the attempt at cornering this paper is to the effect
that the purchasers were followers of Wang Ching
Wei's clique, and were sent there to deliberately
disrupt the circulation of the paper. This belief is
quite logical in view of the fact that the Chinese-
American Daily News, an American registered Chinese

REPORT
Date September 4, 1939.

Subject Wang Ching-wei's followers buy up 10,000 copies of
"Chinese-American Daily News."

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Golder

Further
Rudy
//
F
Mr. Stanton

On the morning of September 4 over 10,000 copies
of the day's issue of the "Chinese-American Daily News"
(中美日報), an American registered Chinese language daily
newspaper, were bought up at 3 cents per copy by a
number of followers of Wang Ching-wei's Clique.

The news vendors, who gather on Shantung Road
every morning to distribute newspapers, commonly sell
this paper at the special price of 2 cents per copy
although the proper price of the paper is 3½ cents each,
this is done apparently with the idea of increasing the
circulation of the paper.

The action taken by Wang Ching-wei's followers
was obviously to suppress the paper from circulation,
but a careful perusal of to-day's issue made by the
staff of this Section has failed to bring to light any
special feature in the paper's columns which could
warrant such action.

The management is unable to offer any explanation
of the occurrence.
However,
Two articles present themselves as possibilities,
one being a reference to No.1500 Brenan Road, a primary
school, which is reported to have been occupied by a
certain society, which remains unnamed, and the other,
entitled "University Principals Send Out Circular Telegram
Denouncing Wang Ching-wei for his Conspiracy with Japan
and Betrayal of the Nation," being very anti-Wang Ching-
wei (copies attached).

C. 4g

E. M. Golder
D. S. I.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

Chinese-American Daily News and Ta Mei Wen Pao (3/9) :- (4/9/39 A.M.)

PRIMARY SCHOOL IN WESTERN DISTRICT OCCUPIED

The Kang Kung Primary School ( 幹工小學 ),
No. 1500 Brenan Road in the Western District, was established
20 years ago by Tan Kang-chen ( 陳幹臣 ). At present,
Wu Chung-yuen ( 吳仲元 ) is the principal of the school
and has about 1,000 pupils.
On the early morning of September 3, 5 or 6
well dressed male Chinese visited the school and told
Principal Wu that the school must be closed immediately.
The visitors threatened Wu and claimed that they belonged
to a certain body.
Knowing that it is difficult to deal with
these visitors, Wu told the latter that he could not
find suitable houses for the pupils and asked if a section
of the school premises could still be used to house the
pupils. Arrangements were then made that the visitors
would occupy three rooms of the school and that huts
would be erected on the recreation ground.
At noon yesterday, a large number of persons
entered the school and commenced functioning.

《中美日报》与《大美晚报》（9月3日）:- （1939年9月4日上午）

西区一所小学被占领

位于西区白利南路1500号的干工小学（幹工小學），
由陈干臣（Tan Kang-chen）于20年前创办。目前，吴仲元
（Wu Chung-yuen）担任该校校长，学生约1000人。
9月3日凌晨，5或6名衣着考究的中国男子来到
学校，告诉吴校长学校必须立即关闭。
来访者威胁吴校长，并声称他们属于某个团体。
吴校长知道难以应付这些来访者，便告诉后者他
无法为学生找到合适的校舍，并询问是否仍可使用部分
校舍来安置学生。随后达成的安排是，来访者占用学校
的三个房间，并在操场上搭建棚屋。
昨天中午，大量人员进入学校并开始运作。

Chinese-American Daily News of Sept.3 (Chungking telegram) 8-4/9/39 AM

UNIVERSITY PRINCIPALS SEND OUT CIRCULAR TELEGRAM
DENOUNCING WANG CHING-WEI FOR HIS CONSPIRACY WITH
JAPAN AND BETRAYAL OF THE NATION

On September 1, Messrs Wu Nan-hsien (吴南轩),
Principal of the Futan University, Chang Shou-yung(张寿镛),
Principal of the Kwang Hwa University, Chiang Maung-ling
(蒋梦麟), Principal of the Peking University, Mei Yi-gee
(梅贻琦), Principal of the Tsing Hwa University, and
Principals of 20 other universities throughout the country
despatched a circular addressed to General Chiang Kai-shek
and the Chinese nation, strongly denouncing Wang Ching-wei
for his acts of revolt against the nation and his
conspiracy with Japan. They also pledged their allegiance
to the National Government and their decision to put up
a bitter struggle against Japan and the vacillating elements.
The telegram said: "While the war of resistance
was being carried on smoothly, Wang Ching-wei rebelled
against the Party and nation, left the capital and
surrendered to the Japanese in order to work shamelessly
for the enemy. Besides taking up his abode in Hongkew,
a district where the flames of war have just been
extinguished and where bloodstains are still fresh, he
also travels to Nanking and Canton under the armed
protection of the Japanese and devises means and ways to
menace the fatherland and to betray the nation. One
cannot find in history another man as shameless and
heartless as he is. The object of his forming a puppet
regime is to plant his own influence with the help of
the Japanese. Let us ask this question: Will the
Japanese, who have suffered a casualty of 800,000 officers
and men killed and wounded and who have spent Yen 100,000,000
in the war, permit rebel Wang Ching-wei to enjoy the
privilege? The answer is very plain and even a child
can understand it."

Chinese-American Daily News (Chungking telegram) :-

Mohammedans Despatch Circular Telegram Denouncing
Wang Ching-Wei

On behalf of 500,000 Mohammedans throughout
the country, the Chinese Mohammedans' National Salvation
Association on August 29 despatched a circular telegram
denouncing Wang Ching-wei.

Chinese-American Daily News, Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao, Hwa Pao:-

People's Political Council To Meet In Chungking To-day

The Fourth Session of the People's Political
Council will be held to-day in the suburbs of Chungking.
Over two-thirds of the representatives have already
arrived. The diplomatic policy will form the main
agenda of the meeting.

各大学校长发出通电
谴责汪精卫勾结日本、背叛国家

9月1日，复旦大学校长吴南轩（Wu Nan-hsien）、
光华大学校长张寿镛（Chang Shou-yung）、北京大学校
长蒋梦麟（Chiang Maung-ling）、清华大学校长梅贻琦
（Mei Yi-gee）以及全国其他20所大学的校长，向蒋介
石将军和全国同胞发出通电，强烈谴责汪精卫叛国投敌
及勾结日本的行径。他们还宣誓效忠国民政府，并决定
与日本及动摇分子进行艰苦斗争。
电文称：“在抗战顺利进行之际，汪精卫背叛党
国，离开首都，投降日本，无耻地为敌人效力。他不仅
居住在战火刚熄、血迹尚新的虹口区，还在日军的武装
保护下前往南京和广州，策划危害祖国、背叛国家的方
法。历史上找不到像他这样无耻和狠心的人。他组建伪
政权的目的是在日本的帮助下培植自己的势力。让我们
问一个问题：遭受了80万官兵伤亡、战争花费1亿日元
的日本，会允许叛徒汪精卫享受这种特权吗？答案非常
明显，连孩子都能理解。”

《中美日报》（重庆电）:-

穆斯林发出通电谴责汪精卫

中国回教救国协会代表全国50万穆斯林，于8月
29日发出通电谴责汪精卫。

《中美日报》、《新闻报》、《申报》、《华报》:-

国民参政会今日在重庆召开

国民参政会第四届会议今日在重庆郊区举行。
超过三分之二的代表已经抵达。外交政策将成为会议的
主要议程。

Mr. Chang Pah-ling (张伯苓), Vice Chairman
of the Council, at the meeting on September 2 strongly
denounced Wang Ching-wei who, while in the beginning
advocating war of resistance to the end and expressing
his wish not to be a traitor, is now acting to the

nation would not undermine the unification of the country.
--- United Press.

Chinese-American Daily News, Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao :-

Anti-British Movement in North China Growing More
Serious : Peiping Puppets Cool to Wang Ching-wei

The "Hsin Min Pao" (新民报), the official
publication of the Provisional Government has temporarily
dropped its anti-British and anti-Communist tone. It
has changed its policy and agrees to suppress the
"Kuomintang spirit" movement advocated by Wang Ching-wei.
It is said that the officials of Peiping
are maintaining a cool attitude towards the "New-Kuomintang
Party" because their own positions will be replaced by
members of the Wang Ching-wei Clique.

《中美日报》、《新闻报》、《申报》:-

华北反英运动日益严重：北平伪政权对汪精卫态度冷淡

临时政府的官方刊物《新民报》（Hsin Min Pao）
暂时放弃了其反英和反共的论调。它改变了政策，同意
压制汪精卫倡导的“国民党精神”运动。
据说，北平官员对“新国民党”保持冷淡态度，
因为他们的职位将被汪精卫集团的成员取代。

Subject Chinese-American Daily News - mouthpiece of Central Kuomintang
Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih Forwarded by C. Groom

The Chinese-American Daily News, 160 Avenue
Edward VII, came into existence on October 1, 1938,
and is registered with the Municipal Police
(Registration Certificate No.C-281). It is
incorporated in U.S.A., and is published by the
Roosevelt Publishing Corporation with Mr. H.M. STUCKGOLD
as Manager. Ostensibly this paper is American owned.
It is actually under the control of the Managing
Director Mr. WOO NING CHONG (吴任沧), and serves
as the mouthpiece of the Central Kuomintang.
Mr. WOO is the ex-manager of the Kiangsu
Farmers Bank (Shanghai Communication Office at 1182
Avenue Joffre), which was controlled by Mr. CHEN KOO FU
(陈果夫), former Chairman of the Kiangsu Provincial
Government. This bank suspended payment of deposits
after the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities
and is still closed.
In September, 1938, the Central Kuomintang
decided to publish a newspaper in Shanghai to serve
as its mouthpiece. Owing to lack of funds, the
Kuomintang authorities discussed the matter with
Mr. CHEN KOO FU who agreed to a proposal for the
appropriation of some $200,000.00 from the funds of
the bank towards operating the Chinese-American Daily
News. WOO NING CHONG was appointed Managing Director
of the vernacular, and concurrently Inspector of the
Tangpu by the Central Kuomintang.
In February, 1939, GENERAL KOO TSOH TUNG

《中美日报》位于爱多亚路160号，成立于1938
年10月1日，并在警务处注册（注册证书号C-281）。该
报在美国注册成立，由罗斯福出版公司出版，H.M. STUCKGOLD
先生任经理。表面上该报为美资所有。
实际上，该报受总经理吴任沧（WOO NING CHONG）
控制，并作为国民党中央的喉舌。
吴先生曾任江苏省农民银行（上海通讯处位于霞
飞路1182号）经理，该行由前江苏省政府主席陈果夫
（CHEN KOO FU）先生控制。中日敌对行动爆发后，该
行停止支付存款，至今仍处于关闭状态。
1938年9月，国民党中央决定在上海出版一份报
纸作为其喉舌。由于缺乏资金，国民党当局与陈果夫先
生商议此事，陈先生同意从该银行资金中拨出约20万
美元用于运营《中美日报》。吴任沧被国民党中央任命
为该中文报纸的总经理，并同时担任汤浦督察员。

Extract from daily Intelligence Report dated July 5, 1939.

July 7 Anniversary

It is somewhat difficult to confirm reports bearing
on observance of this anniversary. Summarising such
information as has come to hand, it is possible that
literature on the following points will be distributed:

(1) Anti-Wang Ching-wei : It is reported that
a campaign scheduled to be launched on July 1 will
continue for a week. So far there is nothing to
confirm this.

(2) Pro-Wang Ching-wei : The recent visit to
Shanghai of Wang Ching-wei and the existence in Shanghai
of a clique allegedly working on his peace movement may
result in advantage being taken of this anniversary to
carry out a propaganda campaign.

(3) Pro-Chiang Kai-shek : Literature bearing on
this anniversary may be distributed surreptitiously.

(4) Anti-British : Attempt to extend to the
Settlement the sponsored movement in territory under
Japanese control. Demonstrations are hardly possible
owing to police arrangements for that day but
dissemination of literature is not unlikely.

Reports that certain elements plan sabotage are
without confirmation but inquiries are being continued
in this connexion and any further information will be
circulated in due course.

七七纪念日

确认有关纪念此周年活动的报告 somewhat 困难。
汇总目前已掌握的信息，可能会分发涉及以下要点的宣传品：

(1) 反汪精卫：据报道，定于7月1日发起的运动
将持续一周。目前尚无证据证实此事。

(2) 亲汪精卫：汪精卫近期访问上海，以及上海存在一个
据称致力于其和平运动的派系，可能导致利用此纪念日
开展宣传活动。

(3) 亲蒋介石：涉及此纪念日的宣传品可能会被秘密分发。

(4) 反英：试图将在日本控制区内的受赞助运动扩展至租界。
由于警方当日的部署，示威活动几乎不可能发生，但
分发宣传品的可能性不小。

About two months ago, the Social Affaire
Department of the Special Service Corps of the
Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National
Salvation Army (Wang Ching Wei's organization)
at 76 Jessfield Road, O.C.L., attempted to
persuade the Chinese Chamoer of Commerce, 59
Hongkong Road, to support the Wang regime, but
without success because the responsible members
of the Chamber showed reluctance. Subsequently,
Mr. Ling Kong Hou (林康候), Chinese Councillor
to the Shanghai Municipal Council and Secretary
to the Chinese Bankers' Association, who virtually
controls the Chamber, caused the various trade
associations registered with the Chamber, to publish
separate announcements in the local press that
they had no desire of meddling in politics. By
this ruse it is hoped that the Chamber in an
indirect way will avoid offending or answering
direct the petition from the Wang Ching Wei regime.

The members of the Chamber are endeavouring
to steer a policy of neutrality as much as possible
because the favouring of either side may result
in serious consequences, and the majority of the

My dear Bourne,

        I have heard a report, so far without
any corroborative evidence, that the new Wang
Ching Wei Government is planning to reform the
Shanghai Chinese Chamber of Commerce so as to
utilise it as a means of enforcing some form of
export control.  I was wondering if perhaps
your police reports might contain any indications
to this effect, such as pressure being brought to
bear on the Chamber, or any of its leading members,
with a view to the Chamber becoming the tool of
the new "puppet" regime.

        Any information, one way or the other,
which you may be able to pass on to me in this
connection would be much appreciated.

                                        Yours sincerely,

February 21, 1940. Afternoon Translation.

Ta Mei Wan Pao dated February 20 :-

REPORTED ARRIVAL OF GENERAL DOIHARA IN SHANGHAI （批：SP 13- Ar.）

According to reliable information, General Doihara has arrived in Shanghai and is making arrangements with Dr. Hu Shih-tseng (何世楨), Chen Chung-fu (陳中孚) and others to carry out certain plots. Should these plots be successfully carried out, it will weaken the influence of Wang Ching-wei or deal a serious blow to Wang's plan for the inauguration of a new Central regime. （印：FEB 21 1940 COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE）

It is learned that both Dr. Hu Shih-tseng and Chen Chung-fu are in disagreement with Wang's peace movement. The flat refusal on the part of the late Marshal Wu Pei-fu to join their movement and his death frustrated the schemes of General Doihara, Chen Chung-fu and others.

In view of the fact that the supporters of the Wang regime belong to different cliques, General Doihara secretly came to Shanghai towards the end of the lunar year and opened negotiations with Dr. Hu Shih-tseng and Chen Chung-fu over certain peace activities. The residences of Dr. Hu and others in the Western District are being guarded by Japanese soldiers.

According to certain reliable quarters, it is possible that Wang Ching-wei's scheme to head the new puppet regime on April 1 may fail in view of the increased activities of General Doihara, Dr. Hu Shih-tseng and Chen Chung-fu.
pages.zh:
1940年2月21日。下午译文。

《大美晚报》2月20日讯：-

报道土肥原将军抵达上海 （批：SP 13- Ar.）

据可靠消息，土肥原将军已抵达上海，正与何世桢博士、陈中孚等人安排实施某些阴谋。若这些阴谋得逞，将削弱汪精卫的影响力，或严重打击汪精卫组建新中央政权的计划。（印：1940年2月21日 总监办公室）

据悉，何世桢博士和陈中孚均不同意汪精卫的和平运动。已故吴佩孚元帅断然拒绝加入他们的运动并随后去世，致使土肥原将军、陈中孚等人的图谋受挫。

鉴于汪伪政权的支持者属于不同派系，土肥原将军于农历年末秘密来到上海，就某些和平活动与何世桢博士和陈中孚展开谈判。何博士等人在西区的住所正由日本士兵守卫。

据某些可靠方面称，鉴于土肥原将军、何世桢博士和陈中孚活动的增加，汪精卫于4月1日领导新傀儡政权的计划可能会失败。

pages.en:
September 12  39.
Dr. Ho Shih Cheng, founder of Xin Tung Meng Kuomintang Party.


In view of the growth of influence of the
Waung Ching Wei Clique and the possibility of its
seizure of all powers in the new government, Dr. Ho Shih
Cheng, a prominent pro-Japanese element, has organized
a group amongst the disgruntled politicians known as
the "Sin Tung Meng Group" (新同盟会), the principal
object being to overthrow Chiang Kai Shek's regime and
support Japanese in the campaign.
Dr. Ho Shih Cheng (何世桢) is a native
of Anhwei, educated in America. In 1927 he was elected
member of the Central Executive Committee of Kuomintang,
being then a follower of Hu Han Min. In 1928 he was
educational commissioner of Anhwei and in 1929 he was
president of the Shanghai Provisional Court. Since
retiring from the Court he practised as a lawyer but
becoming dissatisfied with the government under Chiang
Kai Shek he has never ceased his political intrigues
against the Government. General Hsiung Shih Hwe, former
Woosung-Shanghai Defense Commissioner, once ordered his
arrest in connection with a plot to start an uprising in
Chitung Hsien, Kiangpeh. With the cooperation of the
Settlement Police, detectives from the Defense Commission-
er's Office raided a room in the New World Hotel, Yu Ya
Ching Road, but found Ho and his men had left in a hurry
leaving behind important documents revealing his plans.
Dr. Ho has since continued his political
activities and having been to Canton for sometime his
followers consist of politicians of the South-west as
pages.zh:
1939年9月12日。

日本放弃与重庆进行和谈的希望。

According to information from ex-government officials, peace negotiations between Chungking and Japanese delegates which have been going on secretly in Hongkong for the past month are reported to have ended in a complete failure. It is alleged that the Japanese refusal to withdraw their troops from China and the demand for the resignation of Chiang Kai Shek and his close followers were the principal obstacles to successful discussions. Added to these difficulties was the alleged failure of T.V.Soong in inducing the Chungking Government to rely on America for intervention in China affairs and to act as mediator and guarantor for the carrying out of the peace terms. Further Sun Fo protested and alleged that Soviet Russia would discontinue her assistance to China should the latter solely depend on assistance from the United States in the settlement of the China Affair.

Since a deadlock has been reached in the Sino-Japanese discussions, the Tokio Authorities now realize that it is useless to proceed further, and will pledge their whole support to Waung Ching Wei and assist in the new organization, it is further alleged.

In view of the growth of influence of the Waung Ching Wei Clique and the possibility of its seizure of all powers in the new government, Dr. Ho Shih Cheng, a prominent pro-Japanese element, has organized a group amongst the disgruntled politicians known as the "Sin Tung Meng Group" (新同盟會), the principal object being to overthrow Chiang Kai Shek's regime and support Japanese in the campaign.

Dr. Ho Shih Cheng (何世楨) is a native of Anhwei, educated in America. In 1927 he was elected member of the Central Executive Committee of Kuomintang, being then a follower of Hu Han Min. In 1928 he was Educational Commissioner of Anhwei and in 1929 he was President of the Shanghai Provisional Court. Since retiring from the Court he practised as a lawyer but becoming dissatisfied with the government under Chiang Kai Shek he has never ceased his political intrigues against the Government. General Hsiung Shih Hwe, former Woosung-Shanghai Defense Commissioner, once ordered his arrest in connection with a plot to start an uprising in Chitung Hsien, Kiangpeh. With the cooperation of the Settlement Police, detectives from the Defense Commissioner's Office raided a room in the New World Hotel, Yu Ya Ching Road, but found Ho and his men had left in a hurry leaving behind important documents revealing his plans.

Dr. Ho has since continued his political activities and having been to Canton for sometime his followers consist of politicians of the South-west as

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.2 Special Branch ............
REPORT
Date August 28 1939.
Subject Alleged Peace Talks amongst Japanese.
Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

Observers do not believe likely that peace
terms offered by Japan at the present moment will be
favourable and will be accepted by the Chungking
Government, especially the point regarding the with-
drawal of Japanese troops from China. The peace talks
advocated by Waung Ching Wei refer to economical
cooperation but he does not mention of the evacuation
of Japanese troops from China and that is the reason
why Marshal Wu Pei Fu refuses to have anything to do
with the new regime. It will appear that despite
the tension in Europe the policy of Japan in establishing
the New Order in Asia is still unchanged. With the
entry of Waung Ching Wei's group into the new regime,
Japan is permitting the introduction of Kuomintang
principles and display of Kuomintang flags with the
object of having more sympathizers amongst the
disgruntled Chinese politicians.

According to pro-Japanese elements, Waung
Ching Wei with the assistance of the Japanese is contem-
plating on the convention of a "People's Conference"
sometime in September 1939 for the purpose of deciding
on the election of a new President to a Central Govern-
ment. Should this be correct, the new Government will
sit in opposition to the Chungking Government which will
make peace talks almost impossible.

〔左侧批注及印章：FILE E C98；（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 28 AUG. 1939）〕

Tan Shaoliang
Superintendent.

主题 日本人之间所谓的和平谈判。
由 制作并由谭绍良警司转呈

观察员认为，日本目前提出的和平条款不太可能有利，也不会被重庆政府接受，特别是关于日军从中国撤军的条款。汪精卫倡导的和谈指的是经济合作，但他未提及日军从中国撤离，这就是吴佩孚元帅拒绝与新政权有任何关联的原因。看来，尽管欧洲局势紧张，日本建立亚洲新秩序的政策仍未改变。随着汪精卫集团进入新政权，日本允许引入国民党原则并展示国民党旗帜，目的是在不满的中国政客中争取更多的同情者。

据亲日分子称，汪精卫在日本人的协助下，正考虑于1939年9月的某个时候召开“人民大会”，以决定选举新中央政府的总统。如果属实，新政府将与重庆政府对立，这将使和平谈判几乎成为不可能。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

AUG 26 1939

Peace Talks Grows
Among Japanese

Peiping, Aug. 24.
Coincident with the "peace statement" by General Yamada, Commander-in-Chief of the Japanese forces in Central China, in Shanghai yesterday, there is considerable peace talk in high Chinese and Japanese circles here, according to well-informed Chinese sources.
This, however, is stated not to have been caused by European events, but to have been accelerated by them. These well-informed sources declare that the younger group among the Japanese officers, regarded as the extremists, is losing some influence to the older officers.
Another source, very close to the "Provisional Government," expresses the belief that the older generals "are willing to lower their price for talking peace."—Reuter.

1939年8月26日

日本人中和平谈判呼声渐高

北平，8月24日电。据消息灵通的中方人士称，随着日军华中方面军司令官山田将军昨日在上海发表“和平声明”，此地中国和日本高层圈子里出现了相当多的和平谈判言论。

然而，据称这并非由欧洲事件引起，而是受其加速推动。这些消息灵通人士宣称，日本军官中被视为极端分子的少壮派正逐渐失势，影响力让位于老一代军官。

另一接近“临时政府”的消息来源表示相信，老一辈将军们“愿意降低和谈的要价”。——路透社。

Date May 31, 19 39.

Subject.. Major-General Doihara - his present whereabouts.

Made by D.I. Kuh Pao Hwa Forwarded by C. Cranston. J.S.

With reference to the query of D.C. (Special Branch) relating to the present whereabouts of Major-General Doihara, I have to report that discreet enquiries made through various channels indicate that the Major-General is, most likely, still in Shanghai. His address is unknown but it is said that he stays in the Japanese Embassy, Rue Pichon, or at the Japanese Military Attache's Office, Dixwell Road.

He is reported to have held discussions with a number of Japanese military officers and Wang Ching Wei, ex-Deputy Executive of the Kuomintang, at the latter's temporary residence on East Recreation Road, Kiangwan, on the following subjects:-

(1) The organization of a new central government by Wang who will be nominated Premier.

(2) The reorganization of the Chinese Kuomintang into which the principles of the Reorganization Clique ( of which Wang is a principal figure) will be introduced.

(3) The possibility of securing the sanction of the Japanese Government to wind up the affairs of the existing Japanese sponsored governments and to reorganize them into provincial governments under the control of the new central government to be organized by Wang.

(4) The formal submitting of peace terms to Japan on the inauguration of the new central government.

(1) 由将被提名为行政院长的汪精卫组织一个新的中央政府。

(2) 改组中国国民党，引入以汪精卫为主要人物的改组派原则。

(3) 争取日本政府批准结束现有日本扶植的各政府的运作，并将其重组为隶属于汪精卫即将组建的新中央政府控制下的省级政府的可能性。

(4) 在新中央政府成立之际，正式向日本提交和平条款。

SHANGHAI TIMES.

MAY 27 1939

PLANS OF WANG
CHING-WEI

BERLIN, May 26.—The creation of a new Chinese Government which will be willing to talk peace with Japan is the aim of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, expelled Kuomintang leader, according to the Shanghai correspondent of the “Frankfurter Zeitung,” a lengthy despatch from whom appears in to-day’s issue of that paper.

The correspondent states it is admitted in circles close to the expelled Kuomintang leader that the latter has been conducting negotiations with Japanese representatives. He also declares that Mr. Wang’s representatives are now in Peking conferring with members of the Provisional Government, while Mr. Wang himself has established contact with the Reformed Government in Nanking.

It is not known, the correspondent goes on to state, which of the politicians who left Chungking with Mr. Wang are participating in the present negotiations. He believes that the most influential of them, Mr. Chen Kung-po, is not, however, in agreement with Mr. Wang’s present plans.—Transocean.

《上海泰晤士报》。

1939年5月27日

汪精卫的计划

柏林，5月26日电。——据《法兰克福报》驻上海记者发自该报今日刊登的一篇长篇电讯称，被开除的国民党领袖汪精卫先生的目标是建立一个愿意与日本进行和谈的新中国政府。

该记者称，在被开除的国民党领袖身边的圈子里，人们承认后者一直在与日本代表进行谈判。他还宣称，汪先生的代表目前正在北平与临时政府成员磋商，而汪先生本人已与南京的维新政府建立了联系。

记者接着称，尚不清楚随汪先生离开重庆的政治家中有哪些人参与了目前的谈判。他认为，其中最具影响力的陈公博先生并不赞同汪先生目前的计划。——跨洋通讯社（Transocean）。

SHANGHAI TIMES.

MAY 28 1939

WANG'S MOVEMENTS
AROUSE INTEREST

Reported In Shanghai
But Doubts Held On
Trip To Tokyo

Current reports that Mr. Wang
Ching-wei, self-exiled Deputy Ex-
ecutive General of the Kuomintang
and concurrently Chairman of the
Central Political Council had
taken a trip to Tokyo are in-
correct, but he is still in Shanghai,
Hongkong Chinese circles close to
Mr. Wang were yesterday reported
to have stated.

The Japanese authorities, the re-
port stated, have up till now not
yet taken any decision regarding
Mr. Wang's proposals that he should
proceed to Tokyo to take up fur-
ther discussions with the compet-
ent Tokyo government authorities.

Quarters close to Mr. Wang were
reported to have declared that he
was willing to become a deputy
chief of the proposed new central
government in China if Marshal Wu
Pei-fu, soldier-poet, would emerge
from his retirement and head the
presidency. This was taken by
Chinese circles in Hongkong to in-
dicated that Mr. Wang has lost
much of his political influence since
his flight from Chungking, the re-
port stated. This fact was also said
to have been appreciated by the
competent Japanese authorities
with whom Mr. Wang was alleged
to have been negotiating, and
hence the Japanese were said to
be quite unprepared to accept his
suggestions about taking a trip to
Tokyo, according to the report.

Close followers of Mr. Wang, ac-
cording to the report, have not
been in agreement with the policy
he is pursuing, and which they be-
lieve will be futile, and this explains
the lull in the political manoeuvring
of Mr. Wang's followers, Hongkong
Chinese circles were reported to
have observed. Mr. Wang, under
such circumstances, the report add-
ed, is not able to do anything.

1939年5月28日

汪精卫的行踪
引发关注

报道称其在上海
但对赴东京之行
存疑

据昨天接近汪精卫先生的香港华人圈子消息称，有关国民党前副总裁兼中央政治委员会主席汪精卫先生已前往东京的当前报道是不实的，他仍身在上海。

报道称，日本当局迄今尚未就汪先生提出的前往东京与东京政府主管当局进行进一步讨论的建议作出任何决定。

据报道，接近汪先生的人士宣称，如果军人诗人吴佩孚元帅肯出山担任总统职，他愿意担任拟议中的中国新中央政府的副职。报道称，香港华人圈子认为这表明汪先生自逃离重庆以来，其政治影响力已大幅丧失。据说，与汪先生据称一直在进行谈判的日本主管当局也意识到了这一事实，因此据报道日本人对接受他关于前往东京的建议毫无准备。

据报道，汪先生的亲信并不认同他所推行的政策，他们认为该政策将是徒劳的，这也解释了汪先生追随者在政治活动上的沉寂，这是香港华人圈子观察到的。报道补充说，在这种情况下，汪先生无所作为。

GENERAL DOIHARA IN SHANGHAI

According to information from foreign sources,

secret meetings with the rebel Wang Ching-wei, plotting to
undermine China's war of resistance and to organize a "bogus"
Kuomintang. The formation of a "bogus" central regime is
also under consideration.

Subject Departure of General Hsu Chung Chi (許崇智) from Shanghai.

Made by/ ____ and ____ Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang.

General Hsu Chung Chi (許崇智), retired elder
statesman of the Nationalist regime, who since 1927 had been
living at 140 Seymour Road, has left Shanghai by the
President Coolidge for Hongkong.

It may be recalled that General Hsu, a native of
Canton, born in 1883, who received his education in the
Japanese Military Cadets Academy, Tokio, was Commander-in-Chief
of the Kwangtung Constitutional Forces in 1923 when Generalissimo
Chiang Kai Shek served as his Chief of Staff. Generalissimo
Chiang disagreed with him and started a coup which resulted in
General Hsu being overthrown and General Chiang taking over
command of the forces and beginning his brilliant career.

Since his retirement General Hsu has invested his
money in real estate and amusement resorts. About eight years
ago his youngest son attending school at the Shanghai City
West Gate was kidnapped and there were strong rumours that
it was a political affair. The Nationalist Government to
please this elder statesman has, from time to time, given him
high honours and positions. In 1932 he was appointed member
of the State Council and in 1935 Vice President of the
Control Yuan. General Hsu, however, seldom attended to these
monthly duties at Nanking although he drew about $1,000.00 for the
maintenance of his family. He remained in Shanghai despite
the outbreak of hostilities when the Government ceased the
usual remittance.

Recently the Chinese Government in Chungking sent
a special deputy to urge him to leave Shanghai. It appears
that the Government have received a report that in consequence
of the death of Tang Shao Yi and the failure of Mr. Wang Ching Wei

国民党政府退休元老许崇智将军（許崇智），自1927年以来一直居住在西摩路140号，已乘“柯立芝总统号”轮船离开上海前往香港。

回顾往事，许将军系广东人，生于1883年，曾在东京日本陆军士官学校受教育，1923年任粤军总司令，当时蒋介石总司令任其参谋长。蒋总司令与其意见不合，发动政变，导致许将军被推翻，蒋总司令接管军队指挥权并开始其辉煌生涯。

退休后，许将军将资金投资于房地产和娱乐场所。约八年前，他在上海西门附近上学的小儿子遭绑架，当时有强烈谣言称这是一起政治事件。为了取悦这位元老，国民政府不时授予他高官厚禄。1932年他被任命为国务会议成员，1935年任监察院副院长。然而，许将军很少去南京履行这些月度职责，尽管他每月领取约1,000.00美元作为家庭维持费。尽管战事爆发且政府停止了常规汇款，他仍留在上海。

Subject Japan Willing to Conclude Peace with General Chiang Kai Shek.

Made by ________ and ________ Forwarded by Inspector Papp.

According to reliable information received,
Admiral Nomura, the Naval Attache of the Japanese Embassy in China and concurrently Director of the Special Service Department of the Japanese Expeditionary Fleet in China, has recently arrived in Shanghai from Tokyo where he received special instructions from his government to work for the early cessation of the war with China. In accordance with this instructions, the Japanese admiral held a conference with a secret Chinese government agent a few days ago.

It is learned that during the conference the admiral outlined the basic terms of the Japanese Government; mostly on the lines of the declaration issued by Prince Konoye on December 22, 1938. But, it is claimed, that he made an important concession in the terms of their forthcoming dealing with China. He said that the Japanese Government is now prepared to negotiate with General Chiang Kai Shek on condition that the latter will openly make an anti-Communist declaration. As soon as such a manifesto was issued, all Japanese military operations in China would be discontinued and direct negotiations opened. In case General Chiang is not able to act freely owing to obstacles made by Communist elements around him, he may send a responsible representative to Japan to confer with the Tokyo authorities secretly. It is claimed that the admiral also pointed out that a great number of Chinese Government leaders including Mr. T.V. Soong favour peace and are ready to support direct negotiations with Japan. In the opinion of the admiral, both Mr. Wang Ching Wei and Marshal Wu Pei Fu would not be of much help in the solution of the present Sino-Japanese impasse. He is stated to have declared that in Japanese governmental circles,

Date ____ February 7, 1939.

Subject Japanese Navy Advocating Peace at all Cost.

Made by ____ and ____ Forwarded by Inspector Papp.

It is learned from a fairly reliable source
that the Japanese Navy as a whole never cherished any
ambition to invade China. The aim of the Imperial Japanese
Navy is to drive Anglo-American interests from the Far East,
and to make Asia for the Asiatics under the leadership of
the Japanese. In order to achieve this aim, Japan needs
the goodwill and co-operation of the Chinese nation more
than anything else. Japan's Naval leaders deeply deplore
that the war situation has reached so serious proportions
and that the whole of the Chinese nation has been so badly
antagonized by the present "meaningless" war, which the
Navy is compelled by circumstances to support on the side
of the army and thereby permit the weakening of Japan as
a naval world power. For this reason the Navy wants peace
with China more than anyone else in Japan. It is claimed
that so far as the Navy is concerned almost any terms would
be acceptable for peace with China. This attitude may be
due to the circumstance that in Japanese naval circles the
conviction is more and more gaining ground that as a result
of a trade war which will soon develope between Great
Britain and Japan, the Japanese Navy will be put before a
severe test.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 8 FEB. 1939）

据一个相当可靠的消息来源获悉，日本海军整体而言从未怀有侵略中国的野心。大日本帝国海军的目标是将英美利益驱逐出远东，并在日本的领导下实现“亚洲人的亚洲”。为了实现这一目标，日本比任何其他事情都更需要中国人民的善意与合作。日本海军领导人深切痛惜战局已发展到如此严重的地步，以及整个中华民族因这场目前“毫无意义”的战争而受到极大的敌视；海军迫于形势不得不站在陆军一边支持这场战争，从而致使日本作为世界海军强国的地位遭到削弱。出于这个原因，海军比日本任何人都更希望与中国实现和平。据称，就海军而言，几乎任何条款都可以接受以达成与中国的和平。这种态度可能是由于在日本海军界，一种信念正日益增强，即由于英国和日本之间即将爆发的贸易战，日本海军将面临严峻考验。

REPORT    Date January 26 19 39.

Subject The Background of Prince Konoye's Resignation.

Made by ________ and ________ Forwarded by Inspector Papp

According to information from a fairly reliable source, Prince Konoye's resignation has a complicated and interesting background. It is claimed that there were at least three main reasons which caused the Premier's resignation. The first was the sudden and unexpected departure of Mr. Wang Ching Wei from Chungking. It is alleged that Prince Konoye had made secret arrangements with Mr. Wang for the latter to issue his declaration at Chungking and to work for peace from within. But Mr. Wang's failure to win over General Lung Yun(龍雲), Governor of Yunnan, and the exposure of his alleged conspiracy created a situation which compelled him to flee for safety. That Mr. Wang's subsequent circular advocating peace did not bring the support as was expected from other leaders of China may have much contributed to the Japanese Premier's decision to resign. Secondly, the proposed enforcement of Article 11 of the General Mobilization Act which requires all individual possessions and properties to be brought under the control of the State is suspected to have been another reason which prompted the Premier to resign. The enforcement of this act was initiated by the Military but as is known, it did not have the sympathy of the civil and financial groups including the Premier himself. Besides these two reasons there is still another which is not so well known. It is learned that recently a big espionage scandal was discovered in Japan involving a number of high military officers in the Ministry of War at Tokyo. According to the story some important secret documents concerning Japan's war plans and defensive projects were lost by the

制作人 ________ 和 ________ 转呈人 Papp 督察

据一个相当可靠的消息来源，近卫公爵的辞职有着复杂且有趣的背景。据称，导致首相辞职的主要原因至少有三个。第一个是汪精卫先生突然且意外地离开重庆。据称，近卫公爵曾与汪先生达成秘密安排，由后者在重庆发表声明，并从内部致力于和平工作。但是，汪先生未能争取到云南省主席龙云(龍雲)将军的支持，加上其所谓阴谋的暴露，造成了一种迫使他为安全起见而逃亡的局面。汪先生随后发出的倡导和平的通函并未像预期的那样获得中国其他领导人的支持，这可能极大地促使了日本首相决定辞职。其次，拟议执行的《国家总动员法》第11条要求将所有个人财产置于国家控制之下，这被认为是促使首相辞职的另一个原因。该法案的执行由军方发起，但众所周知，它并未得到包括首相本人在内的文职和金融团体的同情。除了这两个原因外，还有一个不太为人所知的原因。据悉，最近在日本发现了一起重大间谍丑闻，涉及东京陆军省的多名高级军官。据称，一些关于日本战争计划和防御项目的重要秘密文件遗失于

Date January 5 1939.

Subject Reported resignation of General Ho Ying Ching, a member of
the clique advocating peace with Japan.

Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

According to information received from a former
member of the Central Tangpu, General Ho Ying Ching, Minister
of War, who as has been indicated in previous reports, is in
sympathy with the peace movement, has tendered his resignation
to Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek but it was not accepted.
General Ho, however, does not hold much influence amongst the
military leaders and the step he has taken will not affect the
war situation.

The report that Messrs. Chen Ko fu(陳果夫), Chen Li Fu
(陳立夫) and Chang Tao Fan(張道藩), members of the Central
Kuomintang Headquarters at Chungking, have either left Chungking
or have been placed under arrest is not true. The Chen brothers
who are the "brains" of the Generalissimo have never advocated
peace and their loyalty towards Chiang is above suspicion
although they are hostile to communists.

It is, however, correct that Mr. Pang Hsueh Pei(彭學沛),
Vice Minister of Communications, who assisted Mr. Waung Ching Wei
in making the flight to Yunnan has been placed under surveillance.

The first autonomous government
in South China to be known as the

begun concentrating all available

Japanese on the other hand are re-
ported to be preparing their drive on

civilian population from Wuchow is
said to be in progress.
Confirmation of the recapture of
Samshui reported by the Chinese was

S E C R E T
