SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
__________________________

R E P O R T
. . . . . .

GENERAL DOIHARA OFFERS PEACE PROPOSALS.

According to reliable information, General Doihara
had a secret conference with General Hsu Jui Ling (      )
shortly after his arrival in Shanghai on the morning of
December 18, 1938. Through special arrangements made by
Mr. Miyakoka, Director of the Japanese Special Service Affairs
in Shanghai, General Hsu called on General Doihara at his
residence, House 20, East Recreation Road, off Kiangwan Road,
at 1 p.m. December 18, and had a conference with him lasting
for about two hours. This conference is of great significance,
as General Doihara expressed his views frankly and earnestly.
The meeting between General Doihara and General Hsu is the
culmination of hard work of the Shanghai Office of the
Japanese Special Service Section for the past month in
cultivating an understanding with General Hsu with a view
to using him as a channel for peace negotiations with China.

General Hsu is stated to be a veteran Kuomintang
leader for over thirty years and a close and trusted friend
of Dr. Sun Yat-sen. He served the Chinese Government in
various capacities in the past, but due to his political
views, he has not been on good terms with General Chiang
Kai Shek. For the past few years, he has lived in retirement
and is said to have devoted most of his time to developing
a big farming project in Fukien. After the outbreak of
the Sino-Japanese hostilities last year, General Hsu became
reconciled with General Chiang to signify his support of the
anti-Japanese united front. He also joined the Secret
Service of the National Government, and was sent to Shanghai
pages.zh:
秘 密
* * * * * *

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
___

报 告
 ____ 

土肥原将军提出和平建议。

据可靠消息，土肥原将军于1938年12月18日上午抵达上海后不久，便与徐瑞麟将军(      )举行了一次秘密会议。通过上海日本特务机关主任宫冈(Miyakoka)先生的特别安排，徐将军于12月18日下午1点在江湾路旁的东体育会路20号住宅拜访了土肥原将军，并与他进行了约两个小时的会谈。这次会议意义重大，因为土肥原将军坦率而诚恳地表达了他的观点。土肥原将军与徐将军的会晤是日本特务课上海办事处过去一个月努力工作的顶峰，旨在培养与徐将军的理解，以便利用他作为与中国进行和平谈判的渠道。

据说徐将军是一位拥有三十多年资历的国民党老资格领导人，也是孙中山博士亲密且受信任的朋友。他过去曾以各种身份为中国政府服务，但由于其政治观点，他与蒋介石将军关系不佳。在过去几年里，他一直隐居，据说将大部分时间用于开发福建的一个大型农业项目。在去年中日敌对行动爆发后，徐将军与蒋将军和解，以示他对抗日统一战线的支持。他还加入了国民政府的特务机构，并被派往上海

pages.en:
- 2 -

to mix with pro-Japanese elements and Japanese officials by
posing as an ardent advocate of peace and cooperation with
Japan. It is learned that owing to his Anti-Chiang Kai Shek
stand in the past, General Hsu has become very popular with
pro-Japanese elements in Shanghai.

During the secret interview, General Doihara is said
to have first expressed his appreciation of General Hsu's
interest in the cause of peace and promised to cooperate with
him in his efforts along this line. Question regarding the
terms for the termination of war, General Doihara is said
to have given on behalf of the Japanese Government a detailed
explanation of the conditions for peace, which include the
following points -:

(1) In order to signify her sincerity and absence
of territorial ambition in China, Japan is ready to withdraw
all her troops from the occupied areas.

(2) No indemnity to Japan would be required to be
paid by China, but losses suffered by private interests of
Japanese individuals would have to be made good by China.
This, he explained, was required to satisfy the Japanese
industrialists and businessmen.

(3) China is expected to conclude an anti-Comintern
pact with Japan and permit the stationing of troops at
specified points in China.

(4) China and Japan should conclude a pact for the
mutual development of culture.

(5) China, Manchukuo and Japan should join hands
in economic cooperation.

In case China should accept these terms, the war
would be discontinued immediately and Japan would help
pages.zh:
- 2 -

通过伪装成热衷于和平及与日本合作的倡导者，与亲日分子和日本官员混在一起。据悉，由于徐将军过去持反蒋介石立场，他在上海的亲日分子中颇受欢迎。

在秘密会晤中，据称土肥原将军首先对徐将军关注和平事业表示赞赏，并承诺在这一路线的努力上与他合作。关于终止战争的条件问题，据称土肥原将军代表日本政府详细解释了和平条件，其中包括以下几点：

(1) 为了表明其诚意及在中国无领土野心，日本准备从占领区撤出所有军队。

(2) 不要求中国向日本支付赔款，但必须由中国赔偿日本个人私人利益所遭受的损失。他解释说，这是为了满足日本工业家和商人的要求。

(3) 期望中国与日本签订反共产国际协定，并允许在指定地点驻扎军队。

(4) 中日两国应签订文化共同发展协定。

(5) 中国、满洲国和日本应在经济合作方面携手合作。

如果中国接受这些条款，战争将立即停止，日本将帮助

pages.en:
- 3 -

China to attain the following three goals -:

(1) Abolition of extrality rights enjoyed by certain
foreign nationals in China.

(2) Retrocession of foreign settlements and concessions
in China.

(3) Establishment of a new Central Government.

When asked to give his opinion about the most suitable
personnel for peace negotiations with Japan, General Deihara
is said to have stated that any leader in China, with the
exception of General Chiang Kai Shek, is acceptable to Japan.
However, in the opinion of the Japanese Government, Mr. Wang
Ching Wei is the most suitable person for this task. It
would be ideal if Mr. Wang would volunteer for this purpose
with Marshal Wu Pei Fu as his associate. The combination of
these two great leaders would eventually save the situation
in the Far East. Japan is quite prepared to negotiate with
the Kuomintang Government should the latter give up its anti-
Japanese stand. Japan would even recognise the present
National Government if they would cooperate with Marshal Wu
Pei Fu. In fact all of the political parties in China that
are not anti-Japanese in nature are not objectionable to the
Japanese Government, with the sole exception of the Chinese
Communist Party.

In her peace negotiations with China, Japan is
resolved not to seek the medium of any of the powers such
as Great Britain, the U.S.A. or France. She would best of all
deal with China direct, but in case of necessity, Japan may
ask her allies, Germany and Italy to act as mediators. They
could appear as mediators so as to save Mr. Wang Ching Wei from
embarrassment and from being regarded as a traitor.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

中国实现以下三个目标：

(1) 废除某些外国国民在中国享有的治外法权。

(2) 归还中国的外国租界和租借地。

(3) 建立新的中央政府。

当被问及认为谁是最适合与日本进行和平谈判的人选时，据称土肥原将军表示，除蒋介石将军外，中国的任何领导人都为日本所接受。然而，在日本政府看来，汪精卫先生是执行此任务的最合适人选。如果汪先生自愿承担此任，并由吴佩孚元帅作为其助手，那将是理想的情况。这两位伟大领袖的结合最终将挽救远东局势。如果国民党政府放弃其反日立场，日本完全准备与其谈判。如果他们愿意与吴佩孚元帅合作，日本甚至承认目前的国民政府。事实上，除了中国共产党以外，所有非反日性质的中国政党都不为日本政府所反对。

在与中国的和平谈判中，日本决心不寻求英国、美国或法国等任何列强作为中介。她最好直接与中国打交道，但在必要时，日本可能会请求其盟友德国和意大利担任调停人。他们可以以调停人的身份出现，以使汪精卫先生免于尴尬，并避免被视为汉奸。

pages.en:
- 4 -

In conclusion, General Doihara is claimed to have
suggested to General Hsu that he take a trip to Chungking
to work for peace during the forthcoming Plenary Conference
of the Kuomintang proposed to be held on January 15, 1939.
None of the Japanese officials and pro-Japanese elements are
aware that General Hsu is an important secret intelligence
agent of the National Government.

- - - o O o - - -

IW/.

S E C R E T
* * * * * *

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
__________________________

R E P O R T
. . . . . .

GENERAL DOIHARA OFFERS PEACE PROPOSALS.

According to reliable information, General Doihara
had a secret conference with General Hsu Jui Ling (        )
shortly after his arrival in Shanghai on the morning of
December 18, 1938. Through special arrangements made by
Mr. Miyakoka, Director of the Japanese Special Service Affairs
in Shanghai, General Hsu called on General Doihara at his
residence, House 20, East Recreation Road, off Kiangwan Road,
at 1 p.m. December 18, and had a conference with him lasting
for about two hours. This conference is of great significance,
as General Doihara expressed his views frankly and earnestly.
The meeting between General Doihara and General Hsu is the
culmination of hard work of the Shanghai Office of the
Japanese Special Service Section for the past month in
cultivating an understanding with General Hsu with a view
to using him as a channel for peace negotiations with China.

General Hsu is stated to be a veteran Kuomintang
leader for over thirty years and a close and trusted friend
of Dr. Sun Yat-sen. He served the Chinese Government in
various capacities in the past, but due to his political
views, he has not been on good terms with General Chiang
Kai Shek. For the past few years, he has lived in retirement
and is said to have devoted most of his time to developing
a big farming project in Fukien. After the outbreak of
the Sino-Japanese hostilities last year, General Hsu became
reconciled with General Chiang to signify his support of the
anti-Japanese united front. He also joined the Secret
Service of the National Government, and was sent to Shanghai

秘 密
* * * * * *

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
___

报 告
 ____ 

土肥原将军提出和平建议。

根据可靠消息，土肥原将军于1938年12月18日上午抵达上海后不久，即与徐瑞麟将军（        ）举行了秘密会议。通过日本驻上海特务机关长宫角（Miyakoka，音译）先生的特别安排，徐将军于12月18日下午1时在江湾路旁的东娱乐路20号住宅拜访了土肥原将军，并与他进行了约两小时的会谈。这次会议意义重大，因为土肥原将军坦率而诚恳地表达了他的观点。土肥原将军与徐将军的会晤是日本特务科上海办事处过去一个月来努力与徐将军建立谅解的成果，旨在利用他作为与中国进行和平谈判的渠道。

据称，徐将军是一位拥有三十多年资历的国民党老资格领导人，也是孙中山博士亲密且值得信赖的朋友。他过去曾以各种身份为中国政府服务，但由于其政治观点，他与蒋介石将军关系不佳。在过去几年里，他一直隐居，据说将大部分时间致力于开发福建的一个大型农业项目。去年中日敌对行动爆发后，徐将军与蒋介石将军和解，以表示他对抗日统一战线的支持。他还加入了国民政府的秘密情报部门，并被派往上海

pages.en:
- 2 -

to mix with pro-Japanese elements and Japanese officials by
posing as an ardent advocate of peace and cooperation with
Japan. It is learned that owing to his Anti-Chiang Kai Shek
stand in the past, General Hsu has become very popular with
pro-Japanese elements in Shanghai.

During the secret interview, General Doihara is said
to have first expressed his appreciation of General Hsu's
interest in the cause of peace and promised to cooperate with
him in his efforts along this line. Question regarding the
terms for the termination of war, General Doihara is said
to have given on behalf of the Japanese Government a detailed
explanation of the conditions for peace, which include the
following points -:

(1) In order to signify her sincerity and absence
of territorial ambition in China, Japan is ready to withdraw
all her troops from the occupied areas.

(2) No indemnity to Japan would be required to be
paid by China, but losses suffered by private interests of
Japanese individuals would have to be made good by China.
This, he explained, was required to satisfy the Japanese
industrialists and businessmen.

(3) China is expected to conclude an anti-Comintern
pact with Japan and permit the stationing of troops at
specified points in China.

(4) China and Japan should conclude a pact for the
mutual development of culture.

(5) China, Manchukuo and Japan should join hands
in economic cooperation.

In case China should accept these terms, the war
would be discontinued immediately and Japan would help
pages.zh:
- 2 -

通过伪装成热衷于和平及与日本合作的倡导者，与亲日分子和日本官员混在一起。据悉，由于徐将军过去持反蒋介石立场，他在上海的亲日分子中颇受欢迎。

在秘密会晤中，据称土肥原将军首先对徐将军关注和平事业表示赞赏，并承诺在这一路线的努力上与他合作。关于终止战争的条件问题，据称土肥原将军代表日本政府详细解释了和平条件，其中包括以下几点：

(1) 为了表明其诚意及在中国无领土野心，日本准备从占领区撤出所有军队。

(2) 不要求中国向日本支付赔款，但必须由中国赔偿日本个人私人利益所遭受的损失。他解释说，这是为了满足日本工业家和商人的要求。

(3) 期望中国与日本签订反共产国际协定，并允许在指定地点驻扎军队。

(4) 中日两国应签订文化共同发展协定。

(5) 中国、满洲国和日本应在经济合作方面携手合作。

如果中国接受这些条款，战争将立即停止，日本将帮助

pages.en:
- 3 -

China to attain the following three goals -:

(1) Abolition of extrality rights enjoyed by certain
foreign nationals in China.

(2) Retrocession of foreign settlements and concessions
in China.

(3) Establishment of a new Central Government.

When asked to give his opinion about the most suitable
personnel for peace negotiations with Japan, General Doihara
is said to have stated that any leader in China, with the
exception of General Chiang Kai Shek, is acceptable to Japan.
However, in the opinion of the Japanese Government, Mr. Wang
Ching Wei is the most suitable person for this task. It
would be ideal if Mr. Wang would volunteer for this purpose
with Marshal Wu Pei Fu as his associate. The combination of
these two great leaders would eventually save the situation
in the Far East. Japan is quite prepared to negotiate with
the Kuomintang Government should the latter give up its anti-
Japanese stand. Japan would even recognise the present
National Government if they would cooperate with Marshal Wu
Pei Fu. In fact all of the political parties in China that
are not anti-Japanese in nature are not objectionable to the
Japanese Government, with the sole exception of the Chinese
Communist Party.

In her peace negotiations with China, Japan is
resolved not to seek the medium of any of the powers such
as Great Britain, the U.S.A. or France. She would best of all
deal with China direct, but in case of necessity, Japan may
ask her allies, Germany and Italy to act as mediators. They
could appear as mediators so as to save Mr. Wang Ching Wei from
embarrassment and from being regarded as a traitor.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

中国实现以下三个目标：

(1) 废除某些外国国民在中国享有的治外法权。

(2) 归还中国的外国租界和租借地。

(3) 建立新的中央政府。

当被问及认为谁是最适合与日本进行和平谈判的人选时，据称土肥原将军表示，除蒋介石将军外，中国的任何领导人都为日本所接受。然而，在日本政府看来，汪精卫先生是执行此任务的最合适人选。如果汪先生自愿承担此任，并由吴佩孚元帅作为其助手，那将是理想的情况。这两位伟大领袖的结合最终将挽救远东局势。如果国民党政府放弃其反日立场，日本完全准备与其谈判。如果他们愿意与吴佩孚元帅合作，日本甚至承认目前的国民政府。事实上，除了中国共产党以外，所有非反日性质的中国政党都不为日本政府所反对。

在与中国的和平谈判中，日本决心不寻求英国、美国或法国等任何列强作为中介。她最好直接与中国打交道，但在必要时，日本可能会请求其盟友德国和意大利担任调停人。他们可以以调停人的身份出现，以使汪精卫先生免于尴尬，并避免被视为汉奸。

- 4 -

In conclusion, General Doihara is claimed to have
suggested to General Hsu that he take a trip to Chungking
to work for peace during the forthcoming Plenary Conference
of the Kuomintang proposed to be held on January 15, 1939.
None of the Japanese officials and pro-Japanese elements are
aware that General Hsu is an important secret intelligence
agent of the National Government.

industrialists and businessmen.

(3) China is expected to conclude an anti-Comintern
pact with Japan and permit the stationing of troops at specified
points in China.

(4) China and Japan should conclude a pact for the
mutual development of culture.

(5). China, Manchukuo and Japan should join hands
in economic co-operation.

In case China should accept these terms, the war
would be discontinued immediately and Japan would help China
to attain the following three goals:-

When asked to give his opinion about the most
suitable personnel for peace negotiations with Japan, General
Doihara is said to have stated that any leader in China, with
the exception of General Chiang Kai Shek, is acceptable to
Japan. However, in the opinion of the Japanese Government,
Mr. Wang Ching Wei is the most suitable person for this task.
It would be ideal if Mr. Wang would volunteer for this purpose
with Marshal Wu Pei Fu as his associate. The combination of
these two great leaders would eventually save the situation in
the Far East. Japan is quite prepared to negotiate with the
Kuomintang Government should the latter give up its anti-
Japanese stand. Japan would even recognize the present National
Government if they would co-operate with Marshal Wu Pei Fu.
In fact all of the political parties in China that are not anti-
Japanese in nature are not objectionable to the Japanese
Government, with the sole exception of the Chinese Communist
Party.
In her peace negotiations with China, Japan is
resolved not to seek the medium of any of the powers such as
Great Britain, the U.S.A. or France. She would best of all
deal with China direct, but in case of necessity, Japan may
ask her allies, Germany and Italy to act as mediators. They
could appear as mediators so as to save Mr. Wang Ching Wei from
embarrassment and from being regarded as a traitor.

Date December 28, 1938.

Subject Japanese Peace Overtures at Stalemate.

Made by/ and Forwarded by Inspector Papp.

It is learned from a fairly reliable source that
the Japanese Military Authorities are most anxious to bring
the war with China to an early termination and that they are
ready now to negotiate with any responsible head of the Kuo-
mintang Government, with the exception of General Chiang Kai
Shek. Fully aware of the dangers arising out of the present
political situation as a result of the financial assistance
granted to China by Great Britain and the U.S.A., the Japanese
Military leaders with General Doihara as their leading figure
seem to be ready to enter into peace negotiations, barring
General Chiang Kai Shek with any other leader of the Kuomintang
Government at Chungking. If Mr. Wang Ching Wei or Dr. H.H.
Kung should come forward, they would be willing to deal with
them. Even, if Mr. T.V. Soong should present himself, Japan
would regard him as acceptable. They would not mind if General
Chiang remained behind the scene and directed the negotiations.
They feel, however, that they could not deal directly with
him, nor could they negotiate for peace with China through
the medium of any of the Third Powers.

（印：SHANGHAI COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 26 DEC. 1938）

General Doihara arrived in Shanghai from Peking via
Nanking on December 18, 1938. He is now staying at House 20,
East Recreation Road, off Kiangwan Road, and is busily engaged
in the peace movement. It is reliably reported that he came
this time with a new "formula" for peace with China and a new
anti-foreign program which aims to wipe out the vested interests
of Great Britain, France and the United States in the Yangtsze
Valley, especially in Shanghai. It is also reported that the
local Japanese Special Service Bureau are now preparing some
drastic measures to be employed against the International
Settlement and the French Concession.

（批注：F.E. 4/2）

制作人/ 及转发人 帕普（Papp）巡官。

据相当可靠的消息来源获悉，日本军方当局迫切希望尽早结束对华战争，并且现在准备与国民党政府的任何负责任的首脑进行谈判，蒋介石将军除外。日本军方领导人充分意识到由于英国和美国向中国提供财政援助而导致当前政治局势产生的危险，以土肥原将军为首的日本军方领导人似乎准备排除蒋介石将军，与重庆国民党政府的任何其他领导人进行和平谈判。如果汪精卫先生或孔祥熙博士挺身而出，他们愿意与之打交道。即使宋子文先生出面，日本也会认为他可以接受。他们不介意蒋介石将军留在幕后指导谈判。然而，他们觉得不能直接与他打交道，也不能通过任何第三国作为中介与中国进行和平谈判。

（印：上海总办办公室 1938年12月26日）

土肥原将军于1938年12月18日经南京从北平抵达上海。他现在住在江湾路旁的东娱乐路20号，正忙于和平运动。据可靠报道，他此次带来了一个新的对华和平“公式”和一个新的排外计划，旨在消除英国、法国和美国在长江流域，特别是在上海的既得利益。另有报道说，当地日本特务机关正在准备一些严厉措施，用以对付公共租界和法租界。

（批注：F.E. 4/2）

Date December 21, 1938.

Subject    New Japanese Peace Overtures.

Made by                Forwarded by

According to information received from a
fairly reliable source, the Special Service Department of the
Japanese Military Command in Central China presented its
November Report to the Chief-of-Staff of Tokyo summing up
the China situation as follows :-

(1) That in the opinion of the Special Service
Department, it is absolutely impossible for Japan to conquer
China by force.

(2) That economic co-operation between China
and Japan in friendly spirit is impossible so long as the
British and the Americans are able to exercise their influence
in this part of the world.

(3) That the war between Japan and China cannot
be brought to an early conclusion so long as the British, the
United States and the French Governments continue to give
financial support and continue to send military equipment to
China through the several existing international routes which
have not yet been cut.

In view of the above situation, Japanese
military leaders in Tokyo have adopted a new formula for
a peaceful settlement of their controversies with China.
It is also stated that a new set of terms of peace have
recently been sent to Shanghai, which were brought here by one
Sumitake or Umitake. The terms are very simple and compromising
in their appearance. They are (1) that China and Japan shall
form a military alliance; (2) that China and Japan shall co-
operate in economic developments; and (3) that China and
Japan shall respect each other's political independence.

In the opinion of responsible Chinese Government

根据从相当可靠来源获得的情报，日本华中派遣军司令部特务机关向东京参谋本部提交了十一月报告，总结中国局势如下：-

(1) 特务机关认为，日本绝对不可能通过武力征服中国。

(2) 只要英国人和美国人能够在此地区施加影响，中日之间就不可能实现友好精神下的经济合作。

鉴于上述局势，东京的日本军方领导人已采用一种新的公式来和平解决与中国的争端。另据悉，一套新的和平条款最近已被送往上海，由一名名为 Sumitake 或 Umitake（音译）的人带来。这些条款表面上非常简单且带有妥协性质。它们是 (1) 中日结成军事同盟；(2) 中日在经济开发方面进行合作；以及 (3) 中日相互尊重彼此的政治独立。

在负责任的中国政府

鉴于上述局势，东京的日本军方领导人已采用一种新的公式来和平解决与中国的争端。另据悉，一套新的和平条款最近已被送往上海，由一名名为 Humitake 或 Umitake（音译）的人带来。这些条款表面上非常简单且带有妥协性质。它们是 (1) 中日结成军事同盟；(2) 中日在经济开发方面进行合作；以及 (3) 中日相互尊重彼此的政治独立。

Marshal Wu Pei Fu earned his popularity by a life
of honest integrity and his unchanged loyalty to the Chihli
Army Group which he joined in 1912 when he was commander of the
3rd Division, then known as a crack Northern Division.
Marshal Feng Yu Hsiang was then a Brigade Commander of the
same division and a subordinate to Marshal Wu (both being
followers of the Chihli Clique of which Marshal Tsao Kun was
the leader). Both Feng and Wu played an important role in
the Chihli-Anfu war in 1920 which resulted in the overthrow
of the Anfu Party led by Marshal Tuan Chi Jui. In 1923 Marshal
Tsao Kun was elected President of China and Marshal Wu became
the strongest warlord in China, his influence spreading all
over the country. Marshal Feng Yu Hsiang was promoted Commander
of the 11th Division through the assistance of Marshal Wu but
later Feng betrayed Wu and President Tsao Kun in the Chihli-
Fengtien war in 1924 when the troops under Feng revolted during
the fighting thereby bringing complete defeat to Wu's army
and causing the collapse of Wu's influence. Marshal Wu went
into retirement in Hupeh Province.

1926 and assisted Marshal Chang Tso-lin (Manchu warlord)
in the fighting against Feng Yu Hsiang who was defeated.

after he was defeated in Hupeh by Generalissimo Chiang Kai Shek
in command of the Kuomintang forces. After the death of

        In Shanghai, according to information from pro-
Japanese sources, one Chang Ming (張銘), formerly attached
to the Military Affairs Commission of Nanking, is busily
entertaining Japanese military and naval officers. This man
is a native of Anhwei, age about 50, and is reported to be
living in Hongkew. He calls himself a representative of
Marshal Wu. It is difficult to ascertain his mission or how
far he is able to influence the Marshal. According to him
there has been some disagreement between Marshal Wu and the
Japanese regards terms and it is unlikely that he will take
up any position in the near future. The most serious obstacles
to the terms are reported to be :-

    without Japanese supervision.
(2) That Marshal Wu become President of the Central Government
    and be free to make appointments and exercise administrative
    power.
(3) That Marshal Wu remain in Peiping instead of going to Honan
    as proposed by Japanese.

China into several independent governments and to make Wu

most of the Northern Generals. Unlike Marshal Feng Yu Hsiang
who, through his intrigues, still maintains a powerful military
force with subordinate generals like Gen. Sung Chi Yuen serving
under the Nationalist Government, Marshal Wu since his retire-
ment has ceased all political activities. He is penniless
and has depended solely on the governors of Chihli Province
for funds to maintain his staff. This assistance has never
failed him despite the change of many regimes in the North.
When the Provisional Government was organized in Peiping
the Chairman, Mr. Wong Keh Ming, has continued the issue
of an allowance to the Marshal in order to gain his favour.
This does not mean, however, that Marshal Wu has become pro-
Japanese because he has never displayed gratitude to paymasters
of any regime.

        Since 1937 the Japanese military leaders in the
North have used every means to induce Marshal Wu to accept an
important position in the puppet regime. In the eyes of the
Japanese Marshal Wu is a most suitable senior Northern General
and his popularity amongst foreigners and Chinese would win
their sympathy, and improve the reputation of the puppet
government. It is understood that Marshal Wu has not yet been
moved by any influence although he is being watched closely
and is not permitted to grant interviews or to talk freely.

        Although Marshal Wu disagrees with Marshal Feng Yu
Hsiang in his pro-Soviet policy, he has always maintained
a friendly attitude towards Generalissimo Chiang Kai Shek.
This is evidenced by the fact that a representative of Marshal
Wu named Liu Ping Chuen(刘秉钧) was all the time stationed in
Nanking prior to the evacuation of the Nationalist troops.

大多数北方将军的尊敬。与冯玉祥大帅不同，冯通过阴谋诡计，仍然维持着一支强大的军事力量，其下属将军如宋哲元将军等在国民政府麾下服役，而吴大帅自退休以来已停止所有政治活动。他身无分文，完全依赖直隶省省长提供资金来维持其幕僚班子。尽管北方政权更迭频繁，但这种援助从未中断。当北平组织临时政府时，主席王克敏先生为了博取吴的好感，继续向吴发放津贴。然而，这并不意味着吴大帅变得亲日，因为他从未对任何政权的资助者表示过感激。

        自1937年以来，北方的日本军事领导人使用各种手段诱使吴大帅在傀儡政权中接受重要职位。在日本人眼中，吴大帅是最合适的北方资深将军，他在外国人和中国人中的声望将赢得他们的同情，并改善傀儡政府的声誉。据悉，吴大帅尚未被任何势力所打动，尽管他受到严密监视，不被允许接受采访或自由交谈。

        虽然吴大帅不同意冯玉祥大帅的亲苏政策，但他一直对蒋介石总司令保持友好态度。事实证明，在国民党军队撤离之前，吴大帅的一位名叫刘秉钧(刘秉钧)的代表一直驻在南京。

are now in Peiping or Tientsin and that the Anfuites now
serving in the puppet regime are not his followers but belong
to a different clique although they do not oppose the appoint-

Chen Ling Sung (程靈嵩) is the son of a multi-
millionaire estate owner in Shanghai. After the death of his
father Chen Ling Sung lost heavily in gold speculations and
went into bankruptcy. He has appeared in Court on several

over local organizations and it does not seem likely that he
and other alleged pro-Wu Pei-fu elements will be able to secure

Subject Activities of Local Adherents of Marshal Wu Pei Fu.

Made by/ ____ and ____ Forwarded by Inspector Pamp.

According to information obtained from a fairly reliable source, local adherents of Marshal Wu Pei Fu are manifesting considerable political activity of late. They are convening secret meetings in the Settlement at which measures are discussed for the realization of a scheme aiming at the establishment of the proposed Federal Government of China under Marshal Wu's leadership. Prominent among the local adherents is one Chen Ling Sen(程霖生), who is stated to be a former leading real estate owner who went into bankruptcy.

The adherents are claiming to have secured the secret support of over two hundred prominent Chinese individuals and organizations in Shanghai, who are said to have expressed their willingness to join them, in the movement in due course and to extend an invitation to the old Marshal to volunteer his services to the new regime. They also claim that these individuals and organizations have promised to issue circular telegrams to the whole nation to create a favourable public opinion and political atmosphere to Marshal Wu's assumption of leadership in the new regime.

The adherents are also planning to establish a "Peace Society", which will be inaugurated in Shanghai shortly. The Society would advocate the cessation of hostilities and would favour the organization of a new national regime with Marshal Wu as the leader.

The adherents view favourably the breaking away of Mr. Wang Ching Wei from Chungking and are encouraged in their work by reports reaching Shanghai from Peking, according to which the Japanese High Command have already accepted all terms required by Marshal Wu as basic conditions for his

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. M. P. REGISTRY No. S. B. D. 8656 (C)）
Date December 14, 1938.

Subject Reasons for Marshal Wu Pei Fu's Refusal of Office.

Made by ............ and ............ Forwarded by Inspector Papp.

According to information received from a fairly reliable source, Marshal Wu Pei-fu has agreed to become President of the proposed Federal Government of China on the following conditions:

1. That Japan will unconditionally withdraw her troops from the occupied areas in China.
2. That the Federal Government of China will be entirely free to organize, train and use its army.
3. That the Federal Government of China will have full and independent power to administer its own finances.

In view of these demands, the Japanese High Command considered Marshal Wu Pei Fu unavailable for the position because they could under no circumstances agree to such terms.

With regard to the international situation, the Japanese leaders realize that it is most unfavourable to their country. The success on the part of the Prime Minister, Mr. Neville Chamberlain in handling the European situation has resulted in the alignment of the common interests of Great Britain, the United States and France, which will enable these countries to take joint action for the preservation of their vested interests in China. To counteract any such joint action, Japan can hardly expect any material help from Germany and Italy. For this reason, the Japanese are exploring all available channels, although they still seem to be confident that they will be able to overcome all difficulties by devising plans, which will secure for them China's full economic co-operation, even if they should be compelled to grant the proposed Federal Government of China wide administrative powers, both in an economic and a political sense.

（印：SHANGHAI COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 15 DEC. 1938 B3）

E.
D.B.R. 14/12

To Br.
D. C. (Special Branch).

E. Papp
Inspector.

日期 1938年12月14日。

主题：吴佩孚元帅拒绝任职的原因。

由 ____ 和 ____ 编制，由 Papp 巡官转呈。

据从相当可靠的消息来源获得的情报，吴佩孚元帅已同意在以下条件下出任拟议中的中华联邦政府主席：

1. 日本将无条件从中国占领区撤出其军队。
2. 中华联邦政府将完全自由地组织、训练和使用其军队。
3. 中华联邦政府将拥有充分且独立的权力来管理其财政。

鉴于这些要求，日本最高指挥部认为吴佩孚元帅不适合担任该职位，因为他们无论如何都不能同意此类条款。

关于国际局势，日本领导人意识到这对他们的国家极为不利。首相内维尔·张伯伦先生（Mr. Neville Chamberlain）在处理欧洲局势方面的成功，导致英国、美国和法国的共同利益趋于一致，这将使这些国家能够采取联合行动，以维护它们在中国既得利益。为了抵消任何此类联合行动，日本很难指望从德国和意大利获得任何实质性的帮助。出于这个原因，日本人正在探索所有可用的渠道，尽管他们似乎仍然相信，通过制定计划，他们能够克服所有困难，从而确保获得中国的全面经济合作，即使他们被迫在经济和政治意义上给予拟议中的中华联邦政府广泛的行政权力。

（印：上海总监公署 1938年12月15日 B3）

E.
D.B.R. 12/14

致 Br.
特科副督察。

E. Papp
巡官。
